items.statement: Direct website bookings doubled to 16% of total in Q1 FY27; management expects two-thirds of full-year business from direct channels.
items.quote: our direct bookings for this quarter have been close to 64% from direct bookings from our direct channel, which typically we would expect that for the full year, two-thirds of our business should keep coming and continue to come from our direct business

items.statement: Non-room revenues contribute over 50% of operating revenue; F&B grew 25% YoY to ~INR132-133 crores (38% of operating revenue), with >50% of city hotel F&B from non-resident guests.
items.quote: Non-room revenues contribute over 50% of our overall operating revenue, further strengthening the resilience and diversity of our earnings profile.

items.statement: Portfolio now stands at 25 properties with 5,257 keys across 15 operational hotels and 10 in pipeline; roughly half owned, half managed.
items.quote: Following this addition, our portfolio now stands at 25 properties with 5,257 keys across 15 operational hotels and 10 in the pipeline. We are also maint aining a balanced structure with roughly half our keys owned and half managed

items.statement: Dubai JV recorded INR156 million loss due to reduced travel flows from West Asia conflict; asset is operationally break-even; Leela to take over operations in CY27 with ~1 year renovation.
items.quote: Consolidated PAT increased five-fold year-on-year to INR488 million. This is after a INR156 million loss booked due to the share of profit of JV, which is mainly on account of our Dubai JV.

items.statement: Management confirmed on track for INR20 billion EBITDA target by FY30, citing same-store overachievement, pipeline execution, double-digit RevPAR growth, and operating flow-through.
items.quote: we are on track, we are moving in the right direction to achieve the targets that we have committed.

items.statement: ROCE currently double-digit; expected to reach mid-to-high teens in coming years as new hotels become operational and value drivers stabilize.
items.quote: ROCE obviously we are double digit ROCE and with these new hotels when they open and the value drivers are just stabilized. This will go to mid-to-high teens ROCE in the coming years in few years when all the new hotels will become operational.

items.statement: Coorg resort ADR nearly doubled post-acquisition; asset broke even operationally in Q1 before rebranding; EBITDA contribution negligible but positive.
items.quote: the ADR at Coorg has nearly doubled post our acquisition, and the asset broke even operationally in the qua rter even before its rebranding

items.statement: HMA fees grew 86% YoY to INR262 million; growth driven by managed portfolio ramp-up, performance-linked fees, and key money commitments; management confident in fee growth trajectory.
items.quote: HMA fees grew 86% to INR262 million, driven by ramp-up of managed properties, including higher fees in some contracts linked to performance and past key money investment.

items.statement: Targets FY27 revenue of INR1,900-1,950 crore, about 30% growth over last year.
items.quote: Because in this financial year 27, we have targeted a revenue of close to INR1900 crores to INR1950 crores which would be almost a growth of 30% over the last financial year.

items.statement: EBITDA margins to normalize to 10.5-11.5% from this quarter onwards.
items.quote: And also going forward, as we have always guided the market, our EBITDA margins from this quarter onwards will be normalized at 10.5 % to 11.5%.

items.statement: FY27 order inflow target of INR2,000 crore; INR580 crore already booked in Q1.
items.quote: I think we have guided the market in the month of May that total order in target for us in this financial year is INR2000 crores.

items.statement: Pending order book as of June 30, 2026 was about INR1,380 crore, giving 6-8 months visibility.
items.quote: As we speak today, so the total order book for us as on 30th of June 26 was almost INR1380 crores giving us a clear visibility for the next 6 and 8 months, 6 to 8 months and also the run-up for the entire financial year '27.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 order booking was INR580 crore versus INR240 crore in Q1 FY26, up 150%.
items.quote: So in the order book, there was a growth of 150%. So as compared to INR240 crores orders that we booked in the Quarter 1 of last year, this year, we have been able, in this quarter, last quarter we have been able to book INR580 crores of orders.

items.statement: Peak revenue potential of INR2,700-2,900 crore after new Ghiloth, Mambattu and Vithalapur capacity.
items.quote: The total revenue potential would be close to INR2700 crores to INR2900 crores.

items.statement: Ghiloth sandwich panel line commissioning by end of this quarter, production from next quarter.
items.quote: So first of all, the Ghiloth sandwich panel line would be commissioned by the end of this quarter, so commercial production likely to start from the next quarter onwards.

items.statement: Gujarat plant commissioning in last quarter of FY27, production from April 2027.
items.quote: And about the Gujarat plant, the commissioning should happen in the last quarter of this financial year and the production starting from April onwards, April 27 onwards.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 9.4% vs 10.5% last year; impact limited to ~100 bps.
items.quote: So EBITDA margin in the first quarter last year was 10.5 which stands at 9.4% and we during our first during our last investor call in the month of May for the entire year '26 have already stressed upon the fact that due to the commodity price increase coming from the war in the Middle East, there was a immediate abrup

items.statement: Steel prices rose 12-15% but balance sheet impact limited to ~1% via weekly order repricing.
items.quote: So even though if you see in the last four to five months post the war started, the raw material prices, the steel prices went up by almost 12% to 14%, 15%, but the impact on our balance sheet was just 1%.

items.statement: Energy sector (renewables, transformers, wires/cables) is the most promising demand segment.
items.quote: Yes, see one of the promising sector in India is definitely the entire energy sector, which comprises of renewable energy, wind, and then transformers is again like lot of investments is coming up in transformer, then wires and cable industry, fiber optic.

items.statement: Data centers currently 4-5% of order book; expects substantial growth similar to renewables.
items.quote: So of the total order book, if we talk about it may not be major, it may be just 4% to 5% of the total order book right now.

items.statement: INR75 crore equity earmarked for data center subsidiary; funding plan not finalized, may raise reasonable debt.
items.quote: The reason of having this INR75 crores equity plan is basically to set up a manufacturing facility.

items.statement: Monsoon may delay civil works in Q2, though EPACK sees no major execution challenge.
items.quote: Yes, the only challenge in this quarter could be the monsoon. So because of monsoons, the civil works get delayed. But as far as our role is concerned, I really don't see any major challenge there.

items.statement: FY28 revenue could reach INR2,300-2,400 crore at 80-85% capacity utilization.
items.quote: So even if we are able to achieve say 80% to 85%, it will get us somewhere close to INR2,300 crores to INR2,400 crores for the next FY28 and we'd be very happy to know reach at that level with the capex that we are doing at this moment.

items.statement: Capex guidance: INR1,500 crores for FY27, INR2,000 crores for FY28, INR1,500 crores for FY29, excluding land acquisition for Kutch and Nagore
items.quote: Total for FY27 in 12 months period we expect a total capex of about INR1,500 crores and thereafter next year slightly higher at INR 2,000 crores and then again 1,500.

items.statement: Durg expansion aggregate spend INR400 crores so far; Q1 FY27 spend INR300 crores
items.quote: Total in this quarter we have spent about INR300 crores in this three months period. And if you want to know separately on how much has been spent on Durg only for that expansion is about 400.

items.statement: Capacity target of 30 million tons by 2030 maintained
items.quote: No, we are maintaining that. So, we are on track and on track of achieving 30 million tons by 2030.

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA threshold 2.5x to at best 2.75x until 30 mt target achieved
items.quote: We would not like to cross net debt to EBITDA 2.5x to at best 2.75x.

items.statement: Q2 fuel cost per Kcal expected to rise from 1.65 to 1.8-1.85; packaging cost up INR3.5-4 per bag
items.quote: I think see, major is contributor is going to be fuel cost, so from 1.65 to maybe it can touch even about 1.8 plus or even 1.85 times.

items.statement: Fuel cost per Kcal rose from 1.54 to 1.65 in Q1; pet coke mix 16% vs 14% previous quarter
items.quote: Yes, so last quarter fuel cost was 1.65, which went up from 1.54 preceding quarter. So there is an increase of about, you know, INR0.11.

items.statement: Packaging granule prices rose from ~134 to 145, adding INR3.5-4 per bag cost
items.quote: No, no, packaging cost also the recent trend is now the, you know, granule prices have gone up. I was just kind of, you know, looking at it. It went down little bit, you know, 134 or something, now it has gone to gone up to 145.

items.statement: Industry demand grew ~8% in Q1; July demand slightly better than previous years; prices stable in July-August
items.quote: Despite that, I think demand was better, industry has grown by about 8% or so.

items.statement: Non-trade share 41% in Q1; trade share rose to 59%; blended cement mix up from 62% to 64%
items.quote: Yes and also along with this diesel price, diesel price impact has also been there, right? So combination of diesel price, temporary increase in fly ash cost and some of the auctions which we participated, this has impacted and non-cement business raw material requirement, that has added up to this increase in raw material cost.

items.statement: Non-cement revenue projected ~INR800 crores for FY27 vs INR613 crores FY26
items.quote: Okay. This year, so last year it was INR613, crores so perhaps I think we'll be around INR800 crores plus types, this is what I think our estimation is.

items.statement: Northeast expansion included in capex guidance; mines at approval stages, 1.5 mt plant planned
items.quote: Yes, Northeast, this does include Northeast also of INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: Renewable energy share 49% of consumption (solar 129 MW, WHRS 45 MW, wind 4 MW); thermal 74 MW
items.quote: So you asked, so right, last quarter we have renewable energy 49%, right? So whatever energy we consume 49% is our renewable energy and that includes solar, wind and WHRS, right?

items.statement: Solar SPV: 42 MW captive at INR4.10 fixed tariff, landed cost INR5.85 vs grid INR7.50, saving INR1.65/unit, payback <2 years, benefit from Q1 FY28
items.quote: We have contracted that solar power at a fixed tariff of INR4.10 which landed to us will cost us about INR5.85. So, it will substitute the grid power which is presently costing INR7.50 so per unit INR1.65 saving would be there.

items.statement: Assam land litigation: PIL filed in Guwahati High Court by nearby villages; JK Lakshmi added as respondent via subsidiary Mahabal Cement
items.quote: Yes, Yes, so we had acquired land from local council, Assam government for setting up plant in Northeast, right? So some of the nearby villages they have gone for PIL claiming that this land belongs to us.

items.statement: Invested over Rs 64 billion in the last five years, including Rs 170 crore for a new MAGGI line and Rs 225 crore for a new Munch line in the last calendar year.
items.quote: So, if you look at the last five years, we have invested more than 64 billion. In the last one calendar year, w e started a new MAGGI line with close to Rs.170 Crores plus investment, a new Munch line where again we invested close to Rs.225

items.statement: Cost saving programs accelerated to 2.6% in 2025 from a normal 1.8-1.9%, with further acceleration planned this year.
items.quote: In a normal year, we would be around 1.8 to 1.9%, we have really stepped up, we have gone to 2.6% in 2025 a nd this year we are further accelerating on

items.statement: Volume growth accelerated to double-digits consistently over the last four to five quarters, with a 5-year volume CAGR of 4.2%.
items.quote: But what has been really heartening is if you look at the last few quarters, w e moved into double -digit volume growth consistently. And this volume growth improvement reinforces that our growth is broad based

items.statement: Premium portfolio contribution grew from 11% to 14%, growing ~500 bps ahead of overall growth.
items.quote: If you look at our premium portfolio, the contribution has grown rapidly from 11% to 14%. More importantly, the growth in this part of the portfolio is well, well ahead of our overall growth. So, the premium part is growing by close to 500 bps ahead of overall growth.

items.statement: NESCAFÉ recorded its 20th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, reflecting the shift from tea to coffee.
items.quote: Last quarter, NESCAFÉ recorded its 20th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, so clearly shows a market shifting from tea to coffee and NESCAFÉ playing the role of the lead brand in this space.

items.statement: Secular growth opportunity exists across categories due to low penetration versus peers like biscuits.
items.quote: I believe the secular growth opportunity exists. Having said that, it is for our teams, my team, and all of us to realize that and to realize that opportunity we need the fuel behind our brands and our people.

items.statement: Company aims to maintain margins in line with past track record while reinvesting efficiency savings.
items.quote: We are not chasing growth at the cost of margin. We will deliver and maintain our margin in line with our past track record.

items.statement: Adding capacity for KITKAT after running out of capacity due to strong growth.
items.quote: we did run out of capacity , we are putting in more capacity , but the growth we are seeing is equally strong

items.statement: Focus on right price points to drive penetration; 80% of snacking market below Rs.20.
items.quote: You are aware like close to 80% of the snacking market is still below Rs.20. Consumers are very, they aspire for brands, but it is our job to make it affordable for them.

items.statement: Premiumization and penetration driving growth; portfolio mix shifting toward premium and affordable packs.
items.quote: I spoke a lot about penetration and premiumization. One of the critical things for driving penetration is the right price points.

items.statement: Macro cost pressures exist but low penetration categories provide resilience versus high penetration peers.
items.quote: While we are concerned about some of the rising costs and the challenges, I think the last one year clearly gives me the confidence that my team has the resilience to work around it.

items.statement: Coffee delivering 20 quarters of double-digit growth; KITKAT becoming a viral brand with strong growth.
items.quote: I spoke about coffee, 20 quarters of double-digit growth, so it is not just a confectionery thing. I think KITKAT has now become one of those viral brands.

items.statement: Ad spend increased 40-50% YoY for three quarters; guided by strict ROI/ROAS metrics, not a fixed percentage.
items.quote: Yes, we are dialing up the support and we are dialing it up because putting it simply, you would put money behind the Virat Kohli's. We believe our brands have that kind of legs.

items.statement: CERELAC ZAS (zero added sucrose) and regular variants both gaining traction after consumer feedback.
items.quote: We launched a ZAS version, which is zero added Sucrose. Now across the entire CERELAC range, moms have a choice of using ZAS or the sugar within the permissible limit.

items.statement: Rural contribution half of peers; rural growing faster than urban with right price point packs (Rs.5, Rs.10).
items.quote: We still have half of what some of our peer group companies are. And let us face it with, rural has been one of the more resilient parts of the market when I compare to urban.

items.statement: GST transition executed flawlessly with no downside in Q3/Q4 CY2023; vendors and distributors stepped up.
items.quote: We did not have a GST downside in Q3 of the calendar year last year nor did we have a downside in Q4 of the calendar year we actually saw an upside.

items.statement: Leveraging parent portfolio for relevant formats like Pops, Delight, ready-to-drink cold coffee, Purina, NESPRESSO.
items.quote: We spoke about Pops and Delight and r eady-to-drink cold coffee, the Vietnamese coffee. These are all product formats which we leverage into the worldwide parent group

items.statement: Efficiency programs funding higher brand investment; virtuous cycle of volume growth and profitability.
items.quote: Higher investment, still better profitability because the growth is driven through volume, premiumization. I think those are the things, which are helping us drive the slide a bit faster.

items.statement: Maintains FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,450-1,500 crores and 12% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: Yes. We had projected a margin of 12% EBITDA over this INR1,500 crores. So quarter 1 has been 9%. We hope to recover the rest in the 3 quarters that are to come to average out 12%. We are still maintaining that.

items.statement: Garment division expects about INR100 crores per quarter for next three quarters, ~INR375-380 crores for the year.
items.quote: And overall, the order book is very healthy. So we are expecting in garments probably a INR100 crores quarter for the next 3 quarters, which will take us close to what we were expecting around INR375 crores, INR380 crores to finish plus whatever export incentives, etc.

items.statement: Plans INR140 crores capex this year, already sanctioned, in fabric, garment and common infrastructure.
items.quote: So we are actually thinking of making investments, which we continue to make. This year, we will be investing another about INR140 crores is planned and already sanctioned.

items.statement: Plans 20-25% capacity expansion in garment and 20% in fabric in FY28.
items.quote: I mean in general, we are looking at an expansion next year of about 20%, 25% in garment and an expansion of about 20%. I'm talking now '27-'28 FY.

items.statement: Surat facility restart planned with ~INR50 crores fresh investment for INR200 crores additional revenue.
items.value: INR50 crores investment, INR200 crores revenue
items.quote: So when we will look at restarting Surat, we would look at it in a way of investing fresh into Surat and completely making a modern plant with new machinery. And that would give us additional runway to grow the business an additional INR200 crores with an approximate investment of about INR50 crores.

items.statement: Segment EBITDA targets: fabric 12-14%, garment 8-10%, yarn 8-10%, consolidated 12%.
items.quote: Right now if you get to the segment-wise margins, more or less, we expect the margins in the Fabric business to be about between 12% to 14% EBITDA and in the Garment business between, say, 8% to 10%. And our yarn business is also somewhere between 8% to 10%. And our consolidated EBITDA target is at about 12%.

items.statement: Fabric order book strong with orders up to November end.
items.quote: Our fabric order book position is also quite good and is showing almost orders up to November end.

items.statement: Demand for fabric and garment healthy for next two quarters, meeting or surpassing projections.
items.quote: And I think, yes, the demand is definitely looking good for both, I can say, for both fabric and garment, at least for the next 2 quarters is looking very healthy and meeting our projections or somewhat slightly surpassing our projections.

items.statement: Increasing share of value-added fabrics like bi-stretch, wool blends to improve realizations.
items.quote: We have been consciously increasing the share of premium product categories such as our bi-stretch fabrics, both in poly viscose and poly-rich blends, wool blends, in our portfolio.

items.statement: Garment export share to rise from 60% toward 70% by year end, improving earnings.
items.quote: But I wouldn't be surprised at the end of the year if we're even inching towards 70% of export.

items.statement: Jacket volumes expected at 800,000-900,000 this year vs 600,000 average, 70,000-75,000 per month.
items.quote: This year, we expect to close between 800,000 to 900,000 jackets. We will probably be averaging between 70,000 to 75,000 jackets a month.

items.statement: Q1 impacted by labor shortage in spinning and delayed garment dispatches; issues now largely eased.
items.quote: The major reason for the top line not increasing has been the labor availability in the first quarter in our spinning business and some dispatches being held back in the garment.

items.statement: Surat SEZ debonding expected complete in 3-5 months, facility operational by April 2027.
items.quote: And we expect that these remaining 2 parts should get done within the next 3 months, hopefully, and definitely within the next 4 to 5 months. So we're hoping that we should have the facility for use in DTA by November or December and operational for start in, let's say, April of '27.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at small single-digit; Dahej plant revenue guided at Rs 65 cr for full year
items.quote: We are looking at a small single-digit growth, I would say. Yes.

items.statement: Dahej plant EBITDA expected negative Rs 4-5 cr in FY27; breakeven difficult
items.quote: EBITDA, breakeven appears to be difficult. They are trying hard, but I think it is difficult. That will be in the range of around negative Rs. 4 crore-Rs. 5 crore.

items.statement: Nagpur capex spend of Rs 100 cr+ in FY27-28; Dahej capex to be communicated later
items.quote: You see, in terms of this Nagpur, the CAPEX would be around Rs. 100 crore plus. Dahej will communicate it later.

items.statement: Bayer products (Iprovalicarb, Triadimenol) acquired for global markets; customers established in some markets, distribution setup ongoing in others
items.quote: We have acquired Iprovalicarb and its variants and Triadimenol and its variants from Bayer for global markets. As we speak, we have already established some customers in various markets and already business started with them.

items.statement: New product introductions benchmarked at minimum 20% margin; 9(3) patented and nutrition products command significantly higher, often more than double
items.quote: We benchmark a healthy 20% margin minimum for any new introduction, but mostly 9(3) and nutrition would have significantly higher, more than double sometimes.

items.statement: Price hikes attempted in April-June to offset raw material/logistics costs but could not sustain; prices declined from May, further in July
items.quote: Price hike happened in the month of June. It could not sustain. From May, it started declining. In June, significant decline in many molecules. In July it further declined.

items.statement: Q1 impacted by 40% rain shortfall in June (15% by July-end); delayed sowing, resowing in Rajasthan, Gujarat, MP, Maharashtra; Q2 remains difficult with large parts of country still rainfall deficit
items.quote: In the month of June, we had 40% shortfall in the rain, and by the end of July, it came down to 15% shortfall. Even 1% shortfall in the rainfall impacts the sowing areas and the overall growth of the crops.

items.statement: Five new product launches planned: one Liquid Fertilizer, three Fungicides, one Herbicide; Innovation Turnover Index 13.89% last year, 11.56% from last 3 years' launches
items.quote: We are pleased to inform you that in the upcoming months, we are planning to launch five new products consisting of one Liquid Fertilizer, three Fungicides, and one Herbicide.

items.statement: GST notice on molecule categorization; company confident of winning as per 5% fertilizer circular; hearing date pending
items.quote: Now these molecules are categorized under that category of fertilizer. Currently, as per the circular, it is 5%. We are sure we will win the case, absolutely. There's no doubt about it.

items.statement: Final dividend of 100% (Rs 2 per share) approved at AGM; buyback of 5 lakh shares at Rs 1,400/share (Rs 70 cr) completed
items.quote: As shareholders of the company, in the 41st annual general meeting held today at 11:00 A.M., considered the final dividend of 100%, that is Rs. 2 per equity share, having face value of Rs. 2 per share, and the result for the dividend will be declared within due course. The company already rewarded the shareholder with

items.statement: Dahej plant revenue Rs 26 cr in Q1 FY27 vs Rs 16 cr YoY; EBITDA improved from -Rs 3 cr to <Rs 1 cr
items.quote: You see, in terms of Dahej, the turnover last year it was around Rs. 16 crore. This year is around Rs. 26 crore. In terms of EBITDA, last year EBITDA was negative Rs. (-3) crore. This year is less than Rs. 1 crore.

items.statement: Bayer product revenue in India nominal in Q1; major turnover from Iprovalicarb expected in September (Q2) for grape season
items.quote: It's a product for grapes. Grape season starts in the 2nd Quarter. Major turnover will come from Bayer products Iprovalicarb in the month of September.

items.statement: Biologicals: two products launched, third by August-end; two more nutrition biologicals planned in FY27; regulation favoring organized players
items.quote: Out of three products, we have already introduced two, and one more is in the pipeline to be introduced pretty soon. Probably by August end, we will be launching the third one also.

items.statement: Targets revenue of Rs 900-950 crore in FY28 and Rs 1,000-1,050 crore in FY29 with current capacity.
items.quote: So, I would say '27-'28 is when we would target 900-950 and then '27-'28 with 1,000-1,050, 2029.

items.statement: Expects ESSEKAN premium PP yarn revenue of about Rs 10 crore this year with 20-25% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: So, ESSEKAN, we are expecting the revenue of about Rs. 10 crore rupees this year, which should be at an EBITDA level 20 %-25%, which is significantly higher than what we are doing.

items.statement: Aims to reach Rs 100 crore revenue in ESSEKAN within four years.
items.quote: The ultimate aim is to reach Rs. 100 crores in the next four years in Essekan.

items.statement: FIBC capacity expansion of up to 6,000 MT over five years on track; adding 1,200 tons annually.
items.quote: As informed earlier, the capacity expansion of FIBC to further add up to 6,000 metric tons per annum over the next five years is on track.

items.statement: Non-woven fabric facility on track for commissioning by Q3 FY27; revenues to start then.
items.quote: The Company remains on track to commission the non -woven fabric facility by Q3 of 2026 -'27.

items.statement: Plans new Rs 40 crore term loan for new project; long-term debt to rise to ~Rs 74 crore by year-end.
items.quote: And by the yearend, it will be near about Rs. 74 crores because the Rs. 40 crore new term loan we will take from here for the new project that we are making.

items.statement: Expects to sustain current EBITDA margin level; no exact guidance given.
items.quote: I would not be able to give a very exact guidance on it at the moment, but we should be able to continue the level that we are at.

items.statement: Raw material price increases and decreases are passed on to customers, with possible lag.
items.quote: So, in our business, mostly whatever the raw material increase and decrease is either ways, we are able to pass it on to the customers.

items.statement: Demand visibility remains about four weeks due to cautious customer procurement at high prices.
items.quote: Demand visibility continues to be about four weeks, reflecting the current procurement pattern of customers where they do not want to procure at extremely high prices.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 product mix: 52% FIBC, 20% Fabric, 12% Small Bags, 8% Multifilament Yarns, 8% others.
items.value: 52% FIBC, 20% Fabric, 12% Small Bags, 8% Multifilament Yarns, 8% others
items.quote: In Q1 FY '27, we did 52% of FIBC, 20% of Fabric, 12% of Small Bags, 8% of Multifilament Yarns and others contributed abou t 8%.

items.statement: Renewable power saves about Rs 3-5 crore annually; no plans to increase beyond 60% now.
items.quote: What we are able to save annually is about close to Rs. 3 crores to Rs. 5 crores a year is what we are able to save annually.

items.statement: Non-woven project targets 15-20% IRR and ROCE above 20%.
items.quote: So, in non-woven, we were expecting between 15% to 20% IRR and a ROCE of above 20%.

items.statement: FY27 launch pipeline of INR3,000 crores GDV plus Wadala land bank INR18,000 crores GDV, total pipeline INR21,000 crores

items.statement: Revenue visibility INR10,000+ crores from ongoing and upcoming launches
items.quote: In addition, our upcoming launch pipeline is expected to contribute about INR6,500-plus crores, taking our overall revenue visibility to INR10,000-plus crores, providing a very solid foundation for sustained growth as we move forward on our ongoing and launch portfolio.

items.statement: Estimated pretax post-debt cash flow potential INR3,380 crores over project life cycles
items.quote: The estimated cash flow potential pretax and post debt on ongoing projects, upcoming projects and other revenues is estimated to about INR3,380 crores over the life cycle of the project.

items.statement: Added asset-light Bangalore project with INR400 crores GDV in Q1FY27
items.quote: During the quarter, we've added an asset-light project in Bangalore with an estimated GDV of INR400 crores, approximately, further strengthening our development pipeline while maintaining our disciplined growth strategy.

items.statement: Q1FY27 EBITDA margin 29%, PAT margin 14%
items.quote: EBITDA grew at 18% Y-o-Y to INR94 crores from INR79 crores in Q1FY26 with EBITDA margin at around 29%. PAT at INR45 crores, which is also a 14% Y-o-Y growth over INR39 crores in Q1FY26 with margin stood at 14%.

items.statement: Residential demand healthy with structural shift to lifestyle/premium; commercial demand driven by GCCs and data centers
items.quote: Speaking about the residential market, we've witnessed to see a structural shift, although over this entire quarter, we've seen lifestyle and premium development seeing good demand coming across all sectors.

items.statement: Q1FY27 sales value INR146 crores, 43,000+ sq ft sold, collections INR173 crores
items.quote: Ajmera Realty delivered steady start to FY27, reporting sales value of INR146 crores with a sales active area of about 43,000 plus square feet sold out and collections being at around INR173 crores for the quarter.

items.statement: Kanjurmarg land conversion targeted in 2-3 months before December deadline; strategic tie-up talks ongoing
items.quote: So we are working very aggressively on the land conversion process. But yes, it's a regulatory process, which we've involved the government as well as the other processes which we need to do. So we are working on that. Hopefully, our target is we should be able to achieve that very soon, hopefully, in the next 2 to 3 m

items.statement: Boutique office Phase 1 launch increased to 8-8.5 lakh sq ft (INR3,600 crores GDV) from earlier 4-5 lakh sq ft plan
items.quote: Earlier, we were doing about 4-5 lakh square feet of office space launch. Now we are going to do about 8 to 8.5 lakh square feet of office space launch. And that is why we are seeing this larger number coming.

items.statement: Received INR89 crores from asset monetization out of INR330 crores guided; further stake sale sealed in July 2026 to be reported in Q2
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that in this quarter, we have received an INR89 crores towards our share of investment and profit from a property sale out of the INR330 crores, which we had mentioned in our potential cash flows, which are coming.

items.statement: Debt reduced by INR57 crores to INR680 crores; debt-equity 0.47x; weighted average cost of debt 11.01%
items.quote: On the back of the strong collection and asset monetization, we have reduced our debt by INR57 crores in this particular quarter from INR737 crores, which stood at around 31st March 2026 to INR680 crores as on 30th June 2026. As a result, we achieved a debt equity ratio of 0.47x as on 30th June 2026.

items.statement: Debt-equity guidance FY27 1x but expect lower levered position with asset monetization
items.quote: But yes, there would be about a quarter or two whereby this kind of a situation are going to be there. And that's the reason we gave the guidance of FY27 to 1x, but with this asset monetization and another also absolutely sealed out kind of a thing, we are now seeing a much lower levered position as we go forward kind

items.statement: Ajmera Vann luxury project sales subdued this FY due to excavation stage; expect traction when superstructure progresses next year
items.quote: We will see subdued sales this financial year for this project. But over the time and next year when the progress of the superstructure is happening, we will start seeing traction coming in a faster way.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin above 30% in near term and 40% long-term.
items.quote: we remain confident of progressing towards an EBITDA margin above 30% in the near term and towards our long-term benchmark of 40%.

items.statement: Targets Courtyard occupancy 80-85% and ADR 6,800-8,500 over next two financial years.
items.quote: we would like to maintain the 80% to 85% levels across the next 2 financial years. But ADR is something that we'd like to pick up from about that late 6,800 to 8,500 in the next 2 financial years.

items.statement: Courtyard ADR could reach 9,000-9,500 by FY28 due to limited supply.
items.quote: I wouldn't be surprised if we are closer to the 9,000-9,500 mark by FY28.

items.statement: Hyderabad ADR expected to grow 10-12% annually.
items.quote: Hyderabad is some -- is one of the markets where you can expect a 10% to 12% growth in ADRs.

items.statement: Phase 2 renovation to complete by December (Q3 FY27).
items.quote: we're expecting to finish this by December of this of this financial year. So, third quarter.

items.statement: Greenfield Courtyard at Madhapur: total project cost INR120-130 crores, 180-200 keys.
items.value: INR120 to INR130 crores; 180 to 200 keys
items.quote: the total project cost will be around INR120 to INR130 crores, the total project cost, and we look to build about 180 to 200 seats.

items.statement: Greenfield construction to start Q4 FY27, operational by FY29-2030.
items.quote: Expecting fourth quarter to start.

items.statement: Convention center offline causes ~INR10 crores EBITDA displacement in FY27.
items.quote: in terms of displacement, it's close to about INR10 crores in combination of the kind of business that you're losing through the convention and the rooms that comes with it.

items.statement: Confident of crossing 30% EBITDA margin this year, targeting 40% after full renovation.
items.quote: all the other quarters put together, we will easily cross that 30% EBITDA margin, and we are looking -- once we have the complete renovated product, we'll be looking to hit that 40% margin, as I already promised.

items.statement: Renovated rooms achieve ~30% higher ADR (~INR9,000 vs INR6,700-6,800).
items.quote: there's almost a 30% delta. The ADRs for the renovated inventory, I mean, the newer rooms, is closer to 9,000 versus the 6,700-6,800 mark that you see at a consolidated level.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 demand strong; expects to beat previous year's quarters despite renovation.
items.quote: Q2 is pretty strong. It is coming back well and I think everybody has come to terms that this war is not something that is going to -- it's in anybody's hands to stop anytime soon or when it's going to stop.

items.statement: Shifting mix from corporate to higher-paying retail/groups; F&B 40-45% of revenue, rooms 50-55%.
items.quote: about 40% to 45% of overall F&B, which includes your banqueting and your restaurants, there is about 50%-55% kind of contributes from the rooms.

items.statement: Rights issue of INR107 crores to reduce promoter stake below 75% and repay debt.
items.quote: we're just repaying the debt and to keep the limit open for the Greenfield project or any other future expansion.

items.statement: War impacted foreign demand in Q1; no permanent business loss from convention center closure.
items.quote: we also witnessed a war where a lot of the foreign demand dropped in the country. So, that is where you see the drop in ADR.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance maintained at Rs 700-800 crore with Rs 180 crore deployed in Q1
items.quote: In line with our earlier guidance, FY27 CAPEX remains on track within the Rs. 700 to 800 crore range, with about Rs 180 crores already deployed in Q1FY27.

items.statement: Zone 4 project delayed 3-6 months due to labour constraints and war issues, phased commissioning in FY27 with ramp-up over FY28-29
items.quote: Barring the 3-6 months delay due to labour constraints and war related issues, our Zone 4 project expansion continues to progress. The project is being commissioned in a phased manner this year, FY27, with ramp-up expected over FY28 and FY29.

items.statement: Augene JV commissioning in Q2 FY27, steady-state revenue projected at Rs 300-400 crore, PAT consolidation from Q2
items.quote: Our partnership with Superform Chemistries through Augene Chemicals combines our deep chemistry expertise and raw material backward integration with their market application insights to build a differentiated specialty chemicals platform; this joint venture remains firmly on track for commissioning in Q2FY27.

items.statement: Energy volumes down 17% QoQ, Non-energy down 7% QoQ, overall down ~12% QoQ; recovery expected in Q2
items.quote: So volumes on energy business were down 17% on a quarter-on-quarter basis and on non-energy business, they were down by 7% on a quarter-on-quarter basis. On an overall organization level, they were roughly 12% down on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: EBITDA Rs 385 crore (+79% YoY) driven by mix optimisation, inventory gains, stable demand; inventory+FX gain estimated Rs 50-60 crore
items.quote: EBITDA of Rs. 385 crore, growing 79% Y-o-Y, driven by a combination of product mix optimisation, monetisation of low-cost inventories. This was also supported by stable demand, improved realisations for select products and resilient execution despite temporary disruptions.

items.statement: NCB chain pricing benefited from China VAT removal; pharma/dyes price hikes from RM inflation plus structural China policy change
items.quote: The second is the NCB chain forms a significant part of these two end segments. NCB chain, the China's VAT removal led to changing of the pricing regime for the products in the entire value chain.

items.statement: West Asia conflict cut regional revenue share from 15% to 2%; volumes redirected to other markets; recovery expected in coming quarters
items.quote: The West Asia crisis had a direct impact on our Energy business, temporarily halting exports to the region. The region's share in our revenues declined from about 15% to 2% in this quarter.

items.statement: Execution across long-term contracts stable, underpinning baseline volume growth and revenue visibility
items.quote: Execution across all our long-term contracts remains stable, continuing to underpin baseline volume growth and safeguard revenue visibility.

items.statement: DCB capacity debottlenecking to 140 KTPA backed by PDCB and downstream demand increase
items.quote: We are also looking to debottleneck our DCB capacity to 140 KTPA backed by volume increase supported by PDCB and downstream demand.

items.statement: Aarti Circularity plastic recycling JV with Re Sustainability slated for H2 FY27 commissioning
items.quote: Our commitment to sustainability and circularity is anchored by our plastic recycling initiative with Re Sustainability through Aarti Circularity, that is slated for commissioning in the second half of FY27.

items.statement: EcoVadis Platinum Rating 2026 achieved with score 87/100, placing company in top 1% globally for sustainability
items.quote: We were pleased to achieve the EcoVadis Platinum Rating 2026 during the quarter with a score of 87 out of 100, placing Aarti Industries among the top 1% of companies globally for sustainability performance.

items.statement: Planned subsidiary in China to expand footprint in market accounting for >45% of global chemicals market and enhance RM sourcing
items.quote: We have planned to set up a subsidiary in China. This entity shall facilitate our plans to expand our base in one of the large global Chemicals' markets, accounting for more than 45% of the global market.

items.statement: FY28 EBITDA guidance of Rs 1,800 crore includes Augene JV contribution; other JV not expected to contribute meaningfully before FY27-28
items.quote: So INR1,800 crore guidance included the EBITDA, especially for Augene JV because we expected it to start contributing by that time frame. The other JV, we did not anticipate will start contributing meaningfully before FY27, '28 time frame.

items.statement: Gasoline-naphtha cracks averaging $15-20/bbl, healthy levels supporting robust fuel additives demand
items.quote: Overall, at the gasoline naphtha level, the cracks have averaged in the range of $15 to $18 per barrel, which are pretty healthy and this is a global market.

items.statement: Crude-linked raw material volatility risk remains; domestic RM procurement 7-15 days inventory, imported 1-1.5 months; hedging strategies in place
items.quote: We typically will not have more than 7 to 15 days inventory, wherever we are purchasing raw material in the domestic market. I think in the imported raw materials, which is where we tend to have 1 to 1.5 months of inventory ideally in stock or over waters, which is where this price fluctuation sometimes could impact us.

items.statement: Zone 4 to launch 5-10 products in FY27, targeting 25-30 products by FY28 across diversified end markets (agro, pharma, coatings, polymers)
items.quote: I think by FY28, we are talking about anywhere in the range of 25 to 30 products. Within this year, we are looking at anywhere between 5 to 10 products.

items.statement: Expect 10-15% volume growth over next two years driven by existing capacity headroom
items.quote: So achieving 10% to 15% volume growth in next two years should not be a problem.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 13.8% in Q1 FY27, up 120 bps YoY; 14% already achieved, 15% target as utilization improves
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 13.8%, an expansion of 120 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Sayakha backward integration to add ~1% gross contribution at peak utilization
items.quote: We are hoping that it should add another 1% or so in the gross contribution at the peak level.

items.statement: Sayakha facility at 65% utilization in Q1 FY27; Phase 2 brownfield capex at Sayakha and Tarapur to yield 3-4x asset turn
items.quote: During Q1 FY27, our Sayakha facility continued its planned ramp-up and operated at nearly 65% utilization.

items.statement: Baddi formulation expansion to nearly double oral solid dosage capacity
items.quote: Once completed, this project is expected to nearly double our oral solid dosage manufacturing capacity.

items.statement: Metformin capacity to scale from 1,400 to 2,200 tons/month including 500-550 tons USFDA block
items.quote: Our current plan is to scale up Metformin from 1,400 tons per month to roughly around 2,200 tons per month.

items.statement: USFDA API plant expansion planned to more than double capacity with 3 new multipurpose lines
items.quote: So that will give us capacity enhancement of slightly more than double our existing capacities.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 aggregate volume growth 3.5%; pricing drove 16-17% YoY revenue growth; volumes to improve as prices stabilize
items.quote: Overall company level, we still achieved around 3.5% aggregate volume growth both domestic and local markets.

items.statement: Metformin prices up ~20% vs pre-war levels; aggregate pricing up 16-17% YoY in Q1 but easing from March-April peaks
items.quote: In Y-o-Y basis, at the aggregate level, we saw somewhere around 16%, 17% aggregate growth.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals quarterly run rate of ~3,500 tons (methylamine) to repeat for next 3 quarters
items.quote: This first quarter's performance will definitely repeat for the next 3 quarters.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty on salicylic acid delayed by ~1 year; shifting to derivatives to achieve breakeven
items.quote: We'll have to wait most probably 1 more year for anti-dumping duty to come up.

items.statement: Geopolitical volatility in West Asia creating freight cost elevation, longer procurement cycles, RM price volatility
items.quote: Geopolitical developments, particularly the ongoing conflict in West Asia, remained an important factor affecting international trade, logistics, and supply chains.

items.statement: US DMF filed for Metformin; USFDA inspection after new 500+ ton block completion in 10-12 months
items.quote: It will take roughly around 10 to 12 months for that capacity to come up, and immediately as it comes up, we will file for the USFDA inspection.

items.statement: Regulated market sales still in business development phase; 9 products with CEP approvals, USFDA oncology and EU oral solid dosage approvals for formulations
items.quote: We got European-CEP approvals for European markets for 9 products.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue guided at Rs 1,400-1,500 crore, EBITDA at Rs 525-575 crore, blended ROCE at 16.25-16.5%
items.quote: Our guideline stands as published. So, FY '27 consolidated revenue of roughly Rs. 1,400 crores to Rs. 1,500 crores, EBITDA of 525 to 575 and a blended return on capital of 16.25 to 16.5.

items.statement: FY27 core crane rental EBITDA guidance unchanged at Rs 525-575 crore despite Q1 margin compression
items.quote: Taking all together, we regard this core margin are structurally intact and our guidance for FY'27 is still between Rs. 525 crores to Rs. 575 crores which is unchanged.

items.statement: FY27 capex pool of Rs 652 crore approved; Rs 92 crore capitalized in Q1, balance Rs 560 crore to be deployed in H2
items.quote: On CAPEX, FY'27 pool of Rs. 652 crores as approved by the board of directors. Rs. 92 crores already capitalized in Q1 and balance deployment is in second half.

items.statement: Blended FY27 EBITDA margin lower due to renewables mix, but absolute EBITDA up 20-30% YoY to Rs 525-575 crore
items.quote: Yes, the blended EBITDA margin will be lower, but in absolute terms, it has gone up significantly as the EBITDA in FY'26 was 429. So, we are forecasting a 20 to 30% growth on this EBITDA for FY'27.

items.statement: Revenue mix: ~60% crane rental, ~37% renewable E&C, ~3% project EPC; full year target ~2/3 crane rental, ~1/3 renewable E&C
items.quote: For the full year, we continue to expect roughly two-third revenue from crane rental and one-third from renewable E&C business.

items.statement: ECL provision Rs 6.2 crore in Q1 (mostly India, aged receivables); expected to normalize over FY27 as collections improve
items.quote: Two points related to a higher expected credit loss provisions driven by aging of receivables that is around Rs. 6.2 crores. We expect it to rationalize over the course of this year as collection improves.

items.statement: FY27 focused on accelerating growth; expects double-digit or high single-digit growth, not anemic.
items.quote: Now, will I deliver double-digit growth, or will I do high single digits? That remains to be seen.

items.statement: Margins should stay in current ballpark; will reinvest for growth rather than maximize short-term margins.
items.quote: It should be in this ballpark. Let me put it that way. It should be in the ballpark.

items.statement: Expects reasonable margin expansion versus last year while reinvesting in AI and growth.
items.quote: Margin expansion is something that we are looking at. A reasonable margin expansion that gives us room to reinvest.

items.statement: ESOP: postal ballot in ~2 weeks, market acquisition of up to 2% in Q3, allocation within 6 months.
items.quote: I'm expecting Q3 is when you should see us starting to acquire from the market.

items.statement: Board considering capital restructuring to write off accumulated losses; will appoint consultant; needs board, shareholder, NCLT approvals.
items.quote: We will appoint a consultant. We will figure out, what's the best way to do it where we can protect all the shareholder interest.

items.statement: Board discussing meaningfully improving core employees' stake; action expected within weeks.
items.quote: You will see action on that within a few weeks.

items.statement: Maintains qualified pipeline at 3-4x annual order intake target at any point.
items.quote: Qualified pipeline is around 3-4x.

items.statement: 70% of revenue recurring; 30% won in-year; last year's announced deals to contribute 30-40% this year.
items.quote: For the deals that we announced last year, let's say, you can assume that we are going to take in at least 30-40% of that value this year.

items.statement: Some slowdown in Middle East; cautious buying and extended timelines in APAC; US better, Europe okay.
items.quote: Where we are seeing caution is obviously from the Middle East, and we are seeing some cautious buying on, I would say, little extended timelines even from Asia Pacific.

items.statement: Contract closures delayed by a month or two due to legal/liability negotiations; no big deals lost.
items.quote: We are seeing some drag, I would say, I would not call it even a quarter delay, but, yeah, it's moving a month or two here and there.

items.statement: Contract signing to subscription revenue typically takes four to five quarters, with milestone billings during implementation.
items.quote: Typically, we have seen it can take four or five quarters between when you will sign a contract and you will start seeing the subscription revenue.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue INR 79.45 crores, EBITDA margin 21.2%, PAT 17.9%; cash INR 184.8 crores.
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter stood at INR 79.45 crores as against INR 72.96 crores in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Will invest in product innovation, AI capabilities, customer-facing teams, and delivery excellence.
items.quote: As opportunities present themselves, we will continue to invest in product innovation, AI capabilities, customer-facing teams, and delivery excellence.

items.statement: Implementation cycle already shortened by about a month to 45 days on average.
items.quote: I'm seeing on an average, we are able to gain almost a month to 45 days in our implementation cycle.

items.statement: INR 100 crore top line expected in a few quarters; management has line of sight.
items.quote: I feel that we will get to that number. We'll get to that. I have a line of sight.

items.statement: FraudZap margins expected much higher; investment already recovered.
items.quote: I think it's much higher. I think if it gives you any comfort, we have already recovered our investment on this. My ROI is already done.

items.statement: Margins to be held in a healthy range; excess cash reinvested in business rather than further expansion.
items.quote: you will start seeing that we will start holding margins in a certain range. After that, we will take any excess money or any excess cash that we are generating, we will start going back to the business for investment.

items.statement: Current margin level seen as sustainable in this ballpark.
items.quote: Today, as we see the margins, I think, we should be able to sustain it in this ballpark.

items.statement: Company holds about INR 185 crores cash; inorganic acquisitions under consideration but no active talks.
items.quote: Because we do have some cash, as you know . We have about INR 185 crores.

items.statement: R&D intensity to increase, funded by holding margins; investment in engineering and AI engineering.
items.quote: Do I see that our R&D density will increase in the coming quarters? Absolutely.

items.statement: Aims to shift portfolio split to 60% H1, 30% H2, 10% H3 within two years.
items.quote: In the next two years, I want to transition my split to, like, a 60, 30, 10. 60 becomes my H1, 30 becomes my H2, and 10 becomes my H3.

items.statement: Middle East conflict causing order slowdown, not cancellations; risk partly baked into this year's plan.
items.quote: I think the effect that we are seeing is in terms of slowdown. Slowdown of orders, not cancellation, a slowdown or shifting of orders.

items.statement: All Middle East delivery offshored to India; on-site resources pulled back to Bangalore.
items.quote: we have offshored all the delivery to India from the Middle East.

items.statement: Sectoral contract litigation ongoing; hopes to close one large contract this quarter and all litigation this financial year.
items.quote: We are looking to close the other two hopefully, we have been chasing it honestly from our end, but I'm hoping that this quarter we are able to close.

items.statement: No further capital infusion expected into Middle East subsidiary; it is self-sufficient.
items.quote: Currently, not. It is self-sufficient.

items.statement: Q1 currency gain of about INR 3 crores on revenue.
items.quote: I think it's about INR 3 crores, this currency gain, yeah, to answer your question.

items.statement: Consolidated top-line growth guidance of 10-12% for FY27 with profitability improvement
items.quote: The guidance for this year, as we have indicated, about 10 -12% on the top line should also apply to this business, and our profitability should improve from the last year.

items.statement: Supply chain business top-line growth guidance of 12-15% for FY27
items.quote: So, again, I think this business should grow in the higher teens, 12-15% for the top line.

items.statement: FY27 capex budget of 550-600 crore; 167 crore spent in Q1
items.quote: We are at about 550-600 crore budget, out of which we've done about 167 crores.

items.statement: Two new ships expected in September-October and October-November; Q3 induction
items.quote: The new ship is expected in September end of this year, the next two months. And the next ship should be, well, actually probably September-October and again October-November for the second ship. So, somewhat in that line that we're looking at. Q3 is when we see that they both get inducted in.

items.statement: Freight business EBITDA margin slight improvement expected in FY27
items.quote: On the freight business side, the margin has been slight, there has been slight improvement, but top line has also grown by about 10-11%.

items.statement: Seaways EBITDA margin expected 25-30% in Q2 despite bunker volatility
items.quote: But the margin profile of the business is such that you will should achieve a 25-30% kind of EBITDA, irrespective of, you know, some, you absorb some of the costs also and some revenue increases might happen also.

items.statement: Diesel price hike impact ~1-2% on supply chain; pass-through via supplementary bills in Q2 onward
items.quote: Also, the trends towards, of course, you will also get a little bit of a value increase because of diesel price increase. That also will start kicking in because we have submitted supplementary bills, etc. to our clients and those will come in this quarter and subsequent quarters also.

items.statement: Bunker price at ~Rs 86,000/ton last week; dynamic daily pricing compresses margins
items.quote: As you can see by the graph, really shot up in the end of February-March because of the Middle east crisis. It came down a little bit in the first few months, but now again it is ramped up to about, I think, till last week, about Rs. 86,000 per ton.

items.statement: Festival season restocking starting; cautiously optimistic on demand outlook
items.quote: There is some uncertainty because of the Middle East, but with the possibility of increased sales during the festival season, we are seeing that restocking starting, and we do expect that to continue in the next few months.

items.statement: LTL mix shift gradual; LTL gross margin ~20% vs FTL ~10%; few bps margin improvement per 1% LTL share gain
items.quote: I think, you know, the LTL business has a higher double the gross margin at about 20% to 10% for the FTL business. So, certainly, there is some change that happens in the margin structure, but it's more gradual rather than straightfo rward. So, there will be some few basis point improvement with every 1% increase in share of the LTL business

items.statement: Strong pipeline of contracts in supply chain; new contracts acquired in Q3-Q4 last year ramping up
items.quote: we've acquired some decent contracts in Q3-Q4 of last year, which has started to play out in this year

items.statement: Transystem JV margin expected ~10% (down from 14-15% earlier); pricing pressure and investment in expansion
items.quote: I do not think we'll get back to that 11 -12% type of range because that seems to be always a little bit on the higher side. Probably, I think about 10% is more reasonable.

items.statement: Concor JV grew 88% YoY; Cold Chain JV grew 48% YoY
items.quote: On the JV side, Concor joint venture has grown about 88%. Co ld Chain has grown quite well at about 48

items.statement: Care rating upgraded to AA+
items.quote: Our care rating has also been enhanced to AA+.

items.statement: 24th consecutive quarter of growth; consolidated top-line grew ~9% YoY in Q1
items.quote: On the quarter gone by, it's a consecutive quarter, 24th consecutive quarter of growth, grew at about 9% on the top line console level.

items.statement: FY27 sales guidance of INR 20,000 crores remains on track despite Goa residential project litigation
items.quote: And I think that the 20 billion number should ballpark still be on track.

items.statement: Exit rental income for FY27 at group level expected between INR 7,300-7,500 crores
items.quote: They will be between 7,300 and 7,500.

items.statement: FY28 expected as inflection point when large projects like Arbour start contributing to P&L and unlock gross margin potential
items.quote: We strongly believe that FY 28 would be an inflection point from a reporting perspective, wherein all our large products, starting from the Arbour, will start to contribute to the P&L and consequently, we will start to unlock the significant gross margin potential that we have been highlighting over the last several quarters now.

items.statement: Capex program for Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 and Downtown Chennai Phase 2 progressing at full speed
items.quote: Our capex program on Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 and Downtown Chennai Phase 2 are going at full speed and the leasing here in Gurgaon is about 40%.

items.statement: New sales bookings for Q1 FY27 were INR 657 crores, impacted by deferment of Aureva senior living launch
items.quote: New sales bookings for the quarter were INR 657 crores, reflecting the timing impact of deferment of our launch of Aureva, our senior living product.

items.statement: Gross margin potential across projects stands at approximately INR 39,000 crores
items.quote: Just to remind, the gross margin potential as it stands today, is approximately INR 39,000 crores.

items.statement: Construction costs remain stable with average cost increase versus last year; land acquisition advances of INR 545 crores in last two quarters including strategic parcels in Gurgaon
items.quote: Our average cost versus last year has definitely increased, and our momentum and trajectory remains very, very strong. On the land, as we have always maintained that as and when we come out with reasonable parcels, which are of interest, we will definitely evaluate.

items.statement: Green shoots visible in GCC and multinational leasing decisions after 4-5 week improvement; Q2 and Q3 expected to be good quarters
items.quote: But last about 4, 5 weeks, I personally see the green shoots of the international companies coming back and making enquiries and starting to take decisions and I believe that Q2 and Q3 will be good quarters from that point of view.

items.statement: Dahlias super-luxury project 65% sold with price realization over INR 1 lakh/sq ft; entry level now INR 100 crores+ per unit
items.quote: We have created history in terms of the first 9 weeks of sale as well as if you see the kind of collections that are going on, plus the price realization of Dahlias is now over INR1 lakh a square foot and on higher floors about touching INR 120000-INR 125000 a square foot and selling.

items.statement: Aureva senior living launch awaiting final RERA approvals expected in next few weeks
items.quote: We are awaiting the final approvals and expecting them to be received over the next few weeks.

items.statement: Privana next phase launch expected early next fiscal year; remains high-rise scheme with no plotted development planned
items.quote: Privana, Parvez, right now will definitely be early next year, if not last quarter. I think it will be early next year.

items.statement: Goa residential project involved in PIL litigation but company remains on track to meet FY27 sales plan; Goa component only ~10% of INR 20,000 crore guidance
items.quote: So yes, I mean, the Goa Residential project, as you know, is involved in some sort of PIL form of litigation, which is not uncommon in that part of the country. But in the morning only Aakash and I did a reiki check with each other. And I think we are on track to hopefully meet the plan that we had laid out at the beginning of the year.

items.statement: Three malls in DLF Limited to be operational in FY27; Goa mall OC received, targeting opening by end of year or early next year
items.quote: In the month of July, we also got the operation certificate for our mall in Goa. With this, all 3 malls in DLF Limited will be operational in the current financial year, leading to a significant increase in run rate of rental business within the DLF entities itself.

items.statement: Net cash position at INR 15,200 crores with INR 11,000 crores in RERA 70% escrow accounts; operating cash flow over INR 1,300 crores in Q1
items.quote: Consequently, our net cash position at the end of the first quarter stood at INR 15,200 crores, of which close to INR 11,000 crores is sitting in the RERA, 70% escrow accounts.

items.statement: DCCDL borrowing rate at 7.14%; CRISIL and ICRA ratings maintained at AAA
items.quote: Our rating from CRISIL and ICRA continue to be AAA, and we have a reasonably fine rate of borrowing at the portfolio level. Our borrowing is for this quarter at a rate of 7.14%.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 20% on LTM basis with plus-minus 2-3% range
items.quote: The 20% promise, LTM basis, we continue to live up to that in that plus-minus 2-3%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement expected in FY27 over FY26
items.quote: Sure, sure. You can assume that.

items.statement: Pipeline grew 15% year-on-year to Rs 13,000 crores
items.quote: Our pipeline, as I said, grew ₹ 13,000 crores, 15% year on year, and we've crossed 100-plus destiny deals

items.statement: 19 strategic wins in Q1 and 61 wins over past 12 months
items.quote: During quarter one, we secured 19 strategic wins and completed 16 transformations. And over the past 12 months, we have achieved 61 wins.

items.statement: Operating leverage expected to start playing out as headcount cost remained constant this quarter
items.quote: The operating leverage, which Rahul is asking, will come in this quarter; we didn't have a salary increase.

items.statement: iGTB expected to reach Flexcube-level profit margins in next two to three years
