items.quote: In June 2026, in line with our strategic approach to establish a strong presence across high potential growth segments and invest in upcoming sports, the company partnered with FIFA to bring the world's biggest football property and secure digital and broa dcasting rights for various FIFA events until 2034 for the Indian market

items.statement: Cash and treasury investments stood at INR 22.1 billion as of June 2026
items.quote: Cash and treasury investments as of June' 26 stood at a healthy INR 22.1 billion, comprising of cash balance of INR 4.4 billion, fixed deposits and other treasury investments of INR 5.9 billion and mutual fund investments of INR 11.8 billion.

items.statement: Expect high-teen revenue growth on base case over next 3-5 years
items.quote: on a base case basis, we want to grow on high-teen basis, I can say.

items.statement: Most capex completed, only INR10-15 crores left for last mile items
items.quote: I think probably to do some last do the last mile thing, we may have a little bit left, about INR10 crores to INR15 crores, but otherwise, most of the capex is already done by the company.

items.statement: Expanded fermentation capacity fully operational by end of month, running at full scale
items.quote: So from a fermentation perspective, it's 0 or 100. So basically, we will be running capacity at full scale. So the expanded capacity will be fully operational and running and producing by the end of this month.

items.statement: Hybrid power plant Phase 1 live in September, Phase 2 two months later, will improve EBITDA margins via lower power cost
items.quote: We are expecting Phase 1 to go live in September. And then 2 months later, the second phase will start. And it should improve our EBITDA margins for sure, this will allow us to get power at a significantly lower price.

items.statement: Expect post-integration margins close to current GTBL levels
items.quote: We would hope that once this integration is completed and once the stabilization is done, we would be -- we'll be close to where we are right now.

items.statement: Healthy demand outlook reflected in 22.1% YoY revenue growth from volume increase
items.quote: This growth came in from a robust increase in sales volumes, which reflects a healthy demand outlook for our products.

items.statement: MicroBiopharm 100% API CDMO, 60% CDMO revenue, 60% Japan / 40% ex-Japan revenue split
items.quote: MicroBiopharm is 100% API CDMO. There is very little formulation, probably about 4% or 5% formulation, which is there and APIs, which are predominantly made by fermentation. And 60% of their business is currently CDMO.

items.statement: Sanofi acquisition closing delayed 6-9 months due to regulatory approvals from 50+ countries, long stop date June next year
items.quote: The second one is still probably about 6 months or 9 months, if not longer away because the long stop date over there is June next year. The reason for that essentially being that there are significant regulatory approvals that have to be obtained from over 50 countries.

items.statement: Equity raise up to INR1,000 crores decided; debt amount and mix still being finalized
items.quote: Right now, I think what we have decided is that we are raising equity up to INR1,000 crores. That is what we are looking at right now to raise equity up to INR1,000 crores. And then we will figure out exactly whether we raise INR1,000 crores or how do we go about the debt -- sorry, what do we do with regards to the debt part.

items.statement: Promoter pledge expected to reduce significantly within 12-15 months
items.quote: I think within a year, it should be going down year to 15 months should be going down significantly.

items.statement: MicroBiopharm synergies expected to yield projects within first year
items.quote: We expect some projects to start within the first year.

items.statement: Asset turn of 1.4x-1.5x expected on INR200 crores of new fermentation and API facilities
items.quote: if I can say on asset turn basis, it is around INR200 crores, you can say 1.4x to 1.5x is the asset turn.

items.statement: Company expects topline to grow about 20% in FY26-27 with commensurate bottom-line increase
items.quote: The Company expects topline to grow by about 20% in FY26-27 on overall basis with commensurate increase in bottom-line.

items.statement: New businesses expected to grow about 60% in FY26-27
items.quote: Further four new businesses are expected to grow about 60%.

items.statement: ROCE target of 15% to 20% over next 12 to 24 months
items.quote: We are now working to improve these ROCE over the next 12 to 24 months. We intend to take it to anywhere between 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Capex cycle largely complete after ₹1,200 Cr invested over last 3 years; focus now on leveraging assets
items.quote: Capex cycle of the Company is largely complete. Now the focus will be to fully leverage the strategic capex done in last 3 years (₹1,200 Cr.).

items.statement: Plastech adding 50% capacity over next 2 quarters with minimal capex
items.quote: The business is also augmenting 50% growth in capacity over the next 2 quarters with minimal capex, which will pave future growth in the next financial year and bring efficiencies of scale.

items.statement: US subsidiary received USD 7 million refund in July 2026 post reversal of additional custom duty
items.quote: Post reversal of additional custom duty imposed in FY 25-26 on imports from India into the USA, the US subsidiary received a refund of about USD 7 million in July-2026 which has not been appropriated pending finalization of customers' refunds there against.

items.statement: BOPP gross margin Rs 30/kg in June 2026Q vs Rs 20/kg in March 2026Q and Rs 23/kg in June 2025Q (includes stock gain)
items.quote: BOPP gross margins was running at Rs 30/- per kg in June 2026Q vs Rs 20 per kg in March 2026Q and Rs 23/- per kg in June 2025Q. This includes stock gain as well which is non-repetitive.

items.statement: BOPET gross margin Rs 9/kg in June 2026Q vs Rs 18/kg in March 2026Q and Rs 13/kg in June 2025Q
items.quote: BOPET gross margin was running at Rs 9/- per kg in June 2026Q vs Rs 18/- per kg in March-26 quarter & Rs 13/- per kg in June-25 quarter.

items.statement: Specialty film margins stable at Rs 63/kg; semi-specialty improved to Rs 45/kg from Rs 36/kg in Q4
items.quote: Our speciality film margins remain stable at Rs 63 per kg. This is why the Company is focusing more to improve speciality films.

items.statement: Specialty chemical EBITDA margin 25% in June 2026Q, improved 2% despite 34% topline growth
items.quote: In fact, in this quarter itself, we have improved our EBITDA margins by 2% in specialty chemical in spite of such phenomenal growth in the specialty chemical segment.

items.statement: Plastech normalized EBITDA margin 7% (ex-incentives) in June 2026Q, 10%+ including incentives
items.quote: Plastic again, which till last year was a loss-making business, has a normalized EBITDA of 7% excluding incentives. Including incentives, they are 10% plus this quarter.

items.statement: Demand is quite strong across businesses
items.quote: The demand is quite strong.

items.statement: Specialty film mix at 61% in June 2026Q, targeting 70% and capability to reach 85-90% without significant capex
items.quote: The current mix of 61% is anyways the highest that we have in the last five quarters. And as a company, our objective is to move it to 70%.

items.statement: Net debt at Rs 1,166 crores (2.3x EBITDA) flat vs Q4 FY26 despite Rs 85 cr working capital increase; target below 2x in 12 months and reduce debt by Rs 400-500 cr over 2 years
items.quote: Net Debt at June 2026 end was flat at Q4, FY26 level (Rs 1,166 crores which is 2.3 times to EBITDA) despite net working capital increase by Rs 85 crores due to increased raw material prices post West Asia war. There is clear roadmap to reduce net debt over next 2 years. We are expecting net debt to EBITDA to reduce to below 2 times to EBITDA in next 12 months.

items.statement: Plastech revenue target Rs 150-160 cr in FY27 and Rs 200+ cr next year; Zigly breakeven around Rs 250 cr revenue; Cosmo Consumer breakeven before Rs 100 cr
items.quote: So, this year we expect to grow from Rs. 100 crores of last year's revenue to Rs. 150 crores-Rs. 160 crores this year, and next year we would like to take this business to Rs. 200 plus crores.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals likely to surpass Rs 400-500 cr target by FY29 (earlier than FY30)
items.quote: There is a good likelihood that by FY '29 itself, we will surpass this target.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR1,310 crores bifurcated rig-wise and day rate-wise with year-wise split
items.quote: The order book stands at INR1,310 crores, and we've also bifurcated the order book year-wise.

items.statement: Three rigs expected to be dehired within current financial year with 4-6 month refurbishment period and no revenue during that time
items.quote: three of our rigs are expected to be dehired within the current financial year. Jindal Drilling & Out of the four rigs, which were getting rehired in the current calendar year, more or less, one has recently received a contract, and we are hopeful that we'll get contracts for the remaining three rigs as

items.statement: Revenue will decline in H2 FY27 due to three rigs going into refurbishment but EBITDA decline will not be proportional
items.quote: Yes, absolutely right. Because these three rigs will get dehired, they will go into refurbishment. No revenue will accrue till they get redeployed. So revenue will decline in the second half of this financial year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin may increase in H2 FY27 despite absolute earnings decline as dehiring includes one owned rig and one rented rig on good rate
items.quote: you might even see an increase in the EBITDA margin, although absolute earnings would see a decline in the second half of the current financial year.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA target guided at 35% for revenue assessment
items.quote: we've guided earlier that you should target a blended EBITDA of 3 5%

items.statement: Refurbishment cost estimated at INR90-110 crores per rig considering inflationary trends and increased labor and material transit costs
items.quote: Considering the recent inflationary trend and the increase in labor cost and transit cost of materials, I think a figure between INR90 crores to INR110 crores would be a fair estimate per rig.

items.statement: New contract for Pioneer rig at fixed day rate of INR45 lakhs denominated in INR not USD
items.quote: It's at a fixed day rate of INR45 lakhs approximately. This contract was denominated in INR.

items.statement: Expect day rates to improve for three rigs due for redeployment but previous contract saw rate pushed down from $62,000 to $47,800
items.quote: We expect day rates to improve. But then again, we were also expecting day rates to improve in the current contract that we received. Unfortunately, that has not been the case in this contract.

items.statement: ONGC legal dispute ongoing for 14-15 years with potential liability of INR163 crores including interest and forex on original INR63 crore USD-denominated receivable
items.quote: There is a receivable of INR63 crores, the original receivable of INR63 crores. And then there is interest and forex appreciation on the said amount. The original receivable was denominated in USD. So, the total amount is close to INR163 crores.

items.statement: Not planning any acquisitions currently; focusing on redeploying three dehiring rigs and conserving cash for refurbishment
items.quote: As of now, we are not looking at any acquisitions right now. We are only looking at the ability to redeploy the 3 rigs, which are going to get dehired in the later part of this financial year.

items.statement: Jindal Pioneer refurbishment expected to complete by first week of September with deployment in October 2026
items.quote: We expect the refurbishment exercise to be completed by first week of September and deployment of this rig to take place in the month of October.

items.statement: Optimistic on market outlook due to Samudra Manthan initiative and improved oil and gas sector expenditure
items.quote: We remain optimistic considering what we hear in the media and from industry insiders. There has also been an improvement in oil and gas sector expenditure in other sectors.

items.statement: JV loss of INR5 crores in Q1 FY27 due to Pioneer refurbishment expenses incurred by JV entity as per sale purchase agreement
items.quote: The loss in that entity is on account of the refurbishment expenses that are being incurred by that entity so as to bring the rig into a certain condition before Jindal Drilling takes delivery of the rig.

items.statement: Three rigs due for redeployment will participate in tenders; tender denomination (USD/INR) clarity expected by next quarter earnings call
items.quote: Regarding the tender denomination, whether it will be USD or whether it will be INR, I will be able to update you in the earnings call for the next quarter because then we will have more clarity.

items.statement: PBT margin target of 7% over next 3 years from current 5.38%
items.quote: What we have guided to is over the next 3 years, reaching a PBT of 7%. We are right now at around 5% change, I think, 5.3, probably 5.38 I'm told is where we're at.

items.statement: ROCE target of 25% for FY27, currently at 20%
items.quote: ROCE for the year, I mean, our stated target is higher at around 30%, but we will definitely be over 20% for Q2, higher than that. For the year as an average, I think we said 25% that's at -- 25%, we can comment.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity target of 0.7 by end of FY27
items.quote: We would consider any debt equity around 0.7 to be healthy. From an annualized point of view, by the end of the year, we are quite confident we will be able to get close to that number.

items.statement: PAT growth target of at least 20% for FY27
items.quote: Yes, that is our stated goal that we achieve these numbers.

items.statement: PEB India order book at INR1,008 crores, highest ever
items.quote: The order book now sits at INR1,00 8 crores, the highest we have ever carried.

items.statement: PEB U.S. order backlog crossed USD 100 million
items.quote: PEB U.S. also our order book is at a new peak. We have now crossed USD 100 billion in order backlog.

items.statement: Boilers order backlog at INR150.75 crores, highest ever
items.quote: Boilers again highest ever order backlog in over INR150.75 crores.

items.statement: PBT margin improved to 5.38% from 4.77% YoY due to favorable mix shift
items.quote: On profitability and margins, PBT margin was at 5.38%, up from 4.77% last year. Mix moving in the right direction, higher-margin businesses, PEB U.S. and engineering services are growing faster and the group margin follows.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded to 43.85% from 42.56%, contribution margin to 28.51% from 27.14%
items.quote: Gross margins have been expanded from 42.56% to 43.85% at a consolidated level , while the contribution margins has increased from 27.14% to 28.51%.

items.statement: Majority of steel price increases passed through in PEB, margin dip was temporary
items.quote: We were able to get the vast majority of the pass-through steel price increase pass-through, that did happen. Some I think there was a little bit of a bleed effect where it took some pain for us to get those increases.

items.statement: Hydraulics order bookings running lower due to U.S. tariff uncertainty, in wait-and-watch mode
items.quote: Activity in the U.S. has slowed, to Europe has done well the introduction of some tariffs, uncertainty, even though it's the Senate and not the house, the expectation that something may come in is causing order backlog to order bookings to run a little lower than we expect.

items.statement: Legacy businesses (steel, railways) now 25% of revenue, down from 35% a year ago
items.quote: Those legacy revenue streams currently contribute about 25% of our revenue. It used to be 35, a year ago it was 35, 33. It's reducing, quarter-on-quarter it reduces.

items.statement: Capacity ramped up in PEB India, PEB U.S. and BIW; Hyundai BIW plant commissioned this month
items.quote: Order books, strong production capacity is up in both U.S. and in India. So we have the capacity to deliver on those order books.

items.statement: Hydraulics U.S. market uncertainty due to potential tariffs creating order booking slowdown
items.quote: We are in wait -and-watch mode on the Hydraulics. Every other business, I think we'll have a clear articulated growth plan and we're confident of revenue profit growth. Hydraulics, we'll wait see for the next few quarters as far as U.S. is -- is one of the biggest markets for us for Hydraulics.

items.statement: Engineering Services revenue ~INR70 crores/year, grew 26.3% YoY, AI automation may improve productivity 30-35%
items.quote: From a revenue standpoint, I can tell you that it's about INR70 crores per year. It's composed primarily of structural engineering and building information modeling.

items.statement: Tech Pennar weak due to thin order book and execution issues; new sales team in place, improvement expected from Q2
items.quote: Tech Pennar has been the weak spot. The order book was thin and a few execution flips cost at some customers. A new sales team is now in place, and we expect that trajectory to improve from Q2.

items.statement: Consolidated sales growth guidance revised to 15% excluding Foskor and Awuko, up from prior 11-12% comparable guidance
items.quote: Given our current order load and forecasts from customers, the growth could be 15% without the sales from Foskor and Awuko in both the periods.

items.statement: Consolidated ceramic sales growth guidance raised to 23-25% from prior 15-15.5%
items.quote: We feel that this could go up to 23%-25%.

items.statement: Consolidated abrasive sales growth guidance retained at 5.5-6% reported, 11-12% excluding Awuko
items.quote: I gave a guidance of 5.5% to 6%. However, if we exclude the revenue from Awuko which is about INR 108 crores, the sales growth will be 11% to 12%.

items.statement: Consolidated electrominerals sales decline guidance retained at 6.5-7% reported, 8-10% growth excluding Foskor
items.quote: The consolidated Electrominerals, I communicated sales decline of 6.5% to 7% on account of the closure of Foskor Zirconia which accounted for INR 235 crores in FY'26.

items.statement: Consolidated abrasive margin guidance retained at 9.5-10%
items.quote: Consolidated Abrasive margins were expected to be around 9.5% to 10%.

items.statement: Consolidated ceramic margin guidance retained at 20.5-21%
items.quote: Consolidated ceramic margins were expected to be 20.5% to 21%. We maintain our same guidance here.

items.statement: Consolidated electrominerals margin guidance retained at 9-9.5%
items.quote: Consolidated Electrominerals margins were expected to be 9% to 9.5%.

items.statement: Rhodius Abrasives FY27 guidance maintained at 5% sales growth with small PAT loss
items.quote: During the last call, we said Rhodius could grow by 5% in FY '27 and that there could be a small loss at the PAT level. We maintain the same guidance.

items.statement: Consolidated CAPEX guidance retained at INR 400 crores for FY27
items.quote: We gave a guidance of INR 400 crores for the full year FY'27 and we keep the same guidance.

items.statement: Standalone abrasive PBIT margin declined to 10.4% in Q1 FY27 from 13.1% in Q1 FY26 due to cost push and volume drop
items.quote: PBIT margin declined from 13.1% to 10.4%.

items.statement: Abrasives segment faced INR 16 crores cost push from oil-based raw materials in May-June 2026, offset by normal price increases
items.quote: The overall cost push is around INR 16 crores. Besides this, raw material cost push, normal inflationary cost push and other costs were there. These were offset by the normal price increase reali sation that we had

items.statement: Standalone electrominerals growth 33% YoY driven by strong domestic and export demand, predominantly volume-driven
items.quote: Growth was largely volume driven, predominantly exports centric.

items.statement: Ceramics guidance upgrade driven by Engineered Ceramics, Metallized Cylinders, and SOFC Ceramics
items.quote: It will be a combination of Engineered Ceramics, Metallized Cylinder, and as well as this, SOFC Ceramics.

items.statement: Foskor Zirconia closure evaluation ongoing, expect solution in a quarter; Awuko voluntary winding up process to complete in a quarter
items.quote: We are evaluating all options, and we expect to reach a solution in a quarter. When we meet in the next quarter, I will update you on the progress that we are making.

items.statement: VAW Russia business remains domestic-focused under sanctions, aim to stay compliant and serve domestic market
items.quote: No broader change in the way the Russian business is happening. It is predominantly domestic centric business and they continue to focus only on that.

items.statement: Semiconductor wafer fab equipment component revenues to start small in FY27, pick up in FY28, peak in FY30
items.quote: FY'27 will be small. FY '28, it will start picking up. I earlier communicated it will peak in FY '30.

items.statement: Expect around 10% top-line growth over the last year
items.quote: With a healthy order ba cklog and good inquiries in hand, we at Batliboi are optimistic that we will be delivering around 10% top -line growth over the last year

items.statement: Order backlog stood at approximately INR618 crores as of June 2026
items.quote: As of June '26, our order backlog stood at approximately INR618 crores and we recorded an order inflow of INR283 crores.

items.statement: Environmental Engineering secured landmark order from SAEL Industries valued at around INR52 crores
items.quote: This order is valued at around INR52 crores and the project is on track for commissioning within next six to eight months.

items.statement: Investment in machine tool division capex increased production capacity by around 30% over the last year
items.quote: Based on the customer feedback and competitive benchmarking, our investment in capex is in machine tool divisions has started yielding results in terms of increasing production capacity around by around 30% over the last year.

items.statement: Planning one or two quick investments including in machine tool space and a solar plant to make energy cost revenue neutral
items.quote: Yes, Shaishav, we are looking at some -- one or two quick investments, one maybe in our machine tool space its elf and we are also probably looking at the idea of putting one more solar plant in our factory to bring our overall operational cost lower and make the energy value almost revenue neutral

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin of 7% to 8% in next 1-2 years from current 4-6%
items.quote: Going forward in next t wo, 3 years, definitely any company would look at improving the EBITDA by having operational efficiency coming in and we are working towards that. We are looking at something around 7% to 8% in next 1 year or 2 years to reach that operating level

items.statement: Absorbing part of raw material cost increases and passing on copper and steel price increases to customers
items.quote: So, for manufacturing space, of course, whatever the raw material cost increase comes up, like any other manufacturer, we are now trying to absorb part of it, trying to pass on to the customer, especially the copper, steel prices and there is an overall increase with all the manufacturers on terms of the raw material increase that are coming in.

items.statement: Demand for machine tools picking up due to government push for private industry participation in defense, aerospace and power
items.quote: Demand for machine tool is picking up, primarily due to government push for private industry participation in defense, aerospace and power industries.

items.statement: Textile industry expected to do better with new incentive policies and FTAs with UK and EU
items.quote: Regarding textile industry, we expect this industry to do better with introduction of a new textile incentive policies announced by the government. FT As with UK and EU in the offing would also help

items.statement: Penta Automation acquisition to be integrated across divisions for automation and robotics solutions
items.quote: So, going forward, we are going to leverage Penta's technical expertise and integrate with our divisions operations wherever we find possible, we can connect an d move forward. So, that was the whole aim of having Penta on board, Shaishav

items.statement: Penta Automation expected to grow 25-30% this year and average 25-30% for next 2-3 years from INR25 crores base
items.quote: Last year they did a turnover of, I believe, INR25 crores and going forward, this year we may be ending over almost 25% to 30% growth and for next two, three years, we are looking at an average growth of 25%-30% for Penta.

items.statement: Performance subject to no further adverse impact from prolonged Middle East conflict or tariff-related headwinds
items.quote: This is subject, of course, to not having any further adverse impact, if any, on the global and Indian economy in the event of a prolonged conflict in the Middle East and any tariff-related headwinds for the balance year.

items.statement: Quickmill focusing on new geographies like Gulf, Mexico, Egypt, South America with large orders booked in Saudi Arabia
items.quote: We are focusing on a new market geography like Gulf, Mexico, Egypt, South America, and happy to share with that with our new renewed focus on the Gulf, we have been able to book one or two very large orders in Saudi Arabia and it goes out a very promising market for us.

items.statement: Bioconserve Renewable Envirotech targeting ZLD in textile first, then pharma, food, chemical sectors after establishment
items.quote: What we are going to do is that first establish our name in few big textile markets, textile collaborates, show our strength in doing it neatly and then after a year or so we will look at other operators like pharma, food, pharma, all those other sectors.

items.statement: Solar power currently covers 65-70% of factory connected load, planning to augment remaining 30-40% capacity this fiscal
items.quote: Right now, we have almost 65%-70% of the power commission solar power commissioned on our factory, and another 30%-40% of spare capacity available that we are definitely looking at augmenting that capacity by in this fiscal end.

items.statement: Q1 order intake was INR11.4 billion, down 30% year-on-year due to lower TBCB realization in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: Coming to financial performance during the first quarter, we saw order book at INR11.4 billion, down 30% year-on-year compared to INR16.2 billion in the quarter ended June '26.

items.statement: Order backlog stood at INR209.3 billion as of June 2026, down 2.5% quarter-on-quarter, representing over 3 years of FY26 revenue.
items.quote: Execution outpaced new orders because of which the order backlog moderated to INR209.3 billion as of June '26 versus INR214.6 billion as of March '26, down by 2.5% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Management maintains full-year EBITDA margin guidance in the mid-20s band.
items.quote: So Amit, we maintain our guidance of mid-20s EBITDA for the year. There is no reason that we should deviate from that right now.

items.statement: Q1 gross margin moderated to 41.3% from 45.3% in FY26, a 400 bps decline driven by lower export mix, commodity costs, and HV business ramp-up.
items.quote: Gross margins moderated to 41.3% from 48.4% a year ago and 47% in the last quarter. However, in our business, comparison with annual margin is a better reference point. So during financial year '25-'26, we achieved a gross margin of 45.3%. This quarter, gross margins are lower at 41.3%, representing a delta of 4%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin for Q1 was 25.1%, in line with mid-20s guidance, as 50% of gross margin impact was mitigated at EBITDA level.
items.quote: Accordingly, we see the 50% of overall gross margin impact gets mitigated at the EBITDA level, and we delivered an EBITDA of 25.1%, in line with mid-20s band we have consistently guided earlier.

items.statement: INR10 billion capacity expansion program announced last year is on track; INR2.5 billion dividend planned for Q2 subject to shareholder approval.
items.quote: Out of this cash balance, company has announced utilization plan of approximately INR13 billion, which includes INR10 billion of capacity expansion program announced in the last financial year and approximately INR2.5 billion of dividend in Q2, subject to the approval of shareholders.

items.statement: Domestic TBCB pipeline has improved since June-July after a soft January-March; full-year market expected to grow 6-7% on TBCB side.
items.quote: But we are seeing now the TBCB pipeline or decisions are getting much better. The last few months if you really look at June, July, the pipeline is much better than what it was in January to March.

items.statement: HVDC pipeline remains strong with developer bids submitted; 1-2 more projects expected in upcoming NCT, though pace is slightly delayed.
items.quote: The HVDC pipeline remains strong. Of course, the pace at which we would like it to come, it's slightly getting delayed, but it's not going away.

items.statement: Transformer business has price escalation clauses (IEEMA formula) covering commodity increases; non-transformer business builds in anticipated costs at tendering with 1-2 year execution lag.
items.quote: In that scope, we get a price escalation. So all the commodities like CRGO steel, etcetera, there is a formula embedded in the contract with which we get the compensation. So that part of the business is not impacted.

items.statement: INR3,000 crore RPT approval for a non-US project put on hold by customer due to budget issues; will require re-approval at future AGM.
items.quote: So, Sameer, thanks for the question. So basically, the approval what we took for INR3,000 crores that project has been put under hold as of today by the customer.

items.statement: US data center RPT order (INR1,300 crore) delayed due to location/state change requiring solution redesign; expected to finalize in Q2 or Q3 FY27.
items.quote: Regarding the data center opportunities in U.S., etcetera, so yes, we took the RPT approval because we were very close to the final negotiation. But then there were certain other aspects like change of location, change of state.

items.statement: Export orders constituted 46% of Q1 order intake, driven by CTs/CVTs from North America, 400kV GIS from Spain/Morocco, and grid automation from state utilities, EPCs, and data centers.
items.quote: This export diversification, which now stands at 46% of our Q1 orders is a trend, we have been building forward and had flagged in our earlier calls.

items.statement: Order backlog composition: private customers 77%, central utilities/PSUs 21%, state utilities 2%, consistent with counter-party derisking trend.
items.quote: Private customers now account for 77% of our backlog with central utilities and PSUs contributing another 21% and state utilities exposure just down to 2%.

items.statement: Confident of achieving INR7,000-8,000 crore base order inflow for full year despite soft Q1.
items.quote: No, we remain confident on.

items.statement: Vallam project part capacity expected in Q1 FY28, balance by end of FY28.
items.quote: I think part of the capacity we should be able to come up with in Q1 of '27, that is there, but the balance capacity will come, probably by end of '27.

items.statement: Chinese GIS suppliers approved with 60-70% local content requirement; competitive impact uncertain pending private TBCB negotiations.
items.quote: So, what will be the Chinese leverage to go down on prices with 60%, 65% or 70% local content is also to be seen in the market.

items.statement: Maintain FY27 revenue guidance of 15% and EBITDA margin upper band of 18-20%
items.quote: As we said, we continue to maintain our revenue guidance of 15% and the upper side of the 18% to 20% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at INR80-90 crores with INR40-50 crores for quartz sinks, INR20 crores for stainless steel, INR20 crores for faucets and appliances

items.statement: Pipeline of ~400 keys across Gwalior, Dehradun, Dwarka, Nashik, Rishikesh and Mandvi Kutch expected to open over next 12-15 months.

items.quote: Our vertical mix has become more diversified compared with prior quarters, with lower dependence on our largest vertical and broader bas e across BFSI, Retail and Public Sectors, which is exactly the portfolio rebalance we have committed at the start of

items.quote: Having said that, we understand that the heavy dependence on crude -linked material is a risk. And accordingly, we have been working on it for the last 1, 1.5 years. There is a lot of work which is happening in diversification and reducing the dependence on crude-linked raw material.

items.statement: Exo Liquid launched 3-4 months ago, ramping up as per expectations; Maxo incense sticks launched in July, priced at par with competition.
items.quote: So, Percy, we have it's only been 3, 4 months that we have launched it. And from a launch perspective, it has done reasonably what as per expectation. So far, so we'll be able to probably give you more this thing maybe end of the year.

items.statement: Endeavor to deliver double-digit revenue growth from current quarter itself; high single-digit volume growth expected through the year.
items.quote: See, our endeavor is to deliver double -digit revenue growth from current quarter itself. This is what we are aiming for. But of course, 3%, 4% price increase will be sitting over there. So high single digit is the volume growth that we are expecting throug h the year

items.statement: M&A evaluation ongoing with stringent filters; TTK opportunity evaluated but 2 divisions not aligned to strategy and significant overlap in remaining 2.
items.quote: On the specific point that you raised about TTK business, yes, we had looked at the business, but the 4 divisions of the business, 2 of them were not aligned to our business strategy, and there was a significant overlap in the remaining 2. So, we did not take it forward.

items.statement: Secured lifetime orders worth INR131 crores in Q1 FY27, up 51.8% YoY, with EV programs contributing INR64 crores
items.quote: During the quarter, we secured lifetime orders worth INR131 crores, representing a growth of 51.8% year-on-year. Importantly, the EV programs contributed nearly INR64 crores out of this INR131 crores

items.statement: Expects sales numbers to increase quarter-on-quarter in FY27, with strong growth momentum continuing from Q1 into Q2
items.quote: This year, even quarter 2 till date, we are seeing strong growth coming in. So that momentum is still continuing. And quarter-on-quarter, I think what we are expecting is the sales numbers to increase.

items.statement: Capex for FY27 focused on EPDM capability development (3 new lines, one operational in Q2), toolroom expansion, and land near Sambhaji Nagar
items.quote: So investment would be in this financial year in 3 areas. One is the capability development in the EPDM product. Second, in the expansion of the toolroom and for the land requirement on the west area near Sambhaji Nagar.

items.statement: Raw material costs up ~4%, passed on ~2% to customers; balance 50% under discussion, expected to settle by end of Q2 or early Q3
items.quote: So approximately 4% of the raw material cost has gone up due to these increases. Out of that, we're able to pass on around 2% of the raw material prices to the customer. For the balance 50% price increases, we are in the discussion with the customer. And we are hopeful that by end of Q2 and the start of Q3, we will be able to settle those price increases also with the customer.

items.statement: Sustainable long-term EBITDA margin target for automotive ancillary business is 12-13%
items.quote: If you talk about the automotive ancillaries, like us and so, because where we have the OEM customer where we need to be most cost competitive, 12% to 13% margins would be on a sustainable basis.

items.statement: Aftermarket business grew 30% YoY in Q1 FY27, launched 345 new SKUs, expanded to 155 distributors; expects similar 30% growth rate to continue
items.quote: Tanya, last year also this business grew by 30%. And this year also, we are expecting that this business will continue growing at that rate.

items.statement: Technology partnership with Hutchinson for advanced body sealing systems, focused on glass run channel; targeting Indian market initially, expecting breakthroughs by end of FY27
items.quote: Through this partnership, PPAP will offer modern and advanced body sealing system solutions to all the customers in India, enabling access to global technologies and next-generation sealing solutions.

items.statement: Raw material inflation remains a near-term watch item; portion of recent cost increases still under discussion with customers
items.quote: However, raw material inflation remains an important near-term watch item across our businesses. While we have made progress in securing cost pass-through arrangements with customers, a portion of the recent cost increases is still under discussion.

items.statement: Tooling business capacity utilization at 84%; received orders for 30 molds with pipeline of 124 molds; targeting 20% output increase in FY27
items.quote: While last year, this division has successfully developed 148 molds, this year, we intend to increase our output by 20%.

items.statement: Received INR100 crores from JV exit; INR8 crores used for taxes; 25% retained for working capital, rest for strategic capex
items.quote: So on the sale proceeds, which we got from the exit of the JV, so around INR100 crores we got. So out of that, around INR8 crores has been utilized towards the payment of taxes. So out of that balance amount, 25% would be retained for the working capital requirements and rest would be used for the strategic capex requirement of the company.

items.statement: Targets net debt-free status within next 3 years
items.quote: So for the short-term side, our target is that in next 3 years at the net level, we would like to be debt free.

items.statement: Battery business remains loss-making; focus on minimizing losses; expects improvement from Q2 FY27 but still a concern
items.quote: Battery business, that is why in our opening comments also we've categorically said that the focus is basically on minimizing the losses which are contributed by this business. And we are continuously working towards that. We are engaging with customers, getting new customers on board, especially in the energy storage area. And I think quarter 1, contribution was not that good, but we are hopeful

items.statement: Tooling business restructuring into Meraki Precision Tools Engineering Limited expected to complete by Q3 FY27
items.quote: As part of this restructuring, the tooling business is proposed to be hived off into a wholly owned subsidiary of PPAP under the name of Meraki Precision Tools Engineering Limited. This process is currently underway and is expected to be completed by quarter 3 of financial year '27.

items.statement: Merger of Avinya Batteries Limited with PPAP expected to complete by Q4 FY27
items.quote: The merger process is in progress and is expected to complete by quarter 4 of financial year '27.

items.statement: Industry outlook encouraging with festival season, GST 2.0, easier financing, and positive consumer sentiment supporting demand momentum
items.quote: The upcoming festival season, lower vehicle ownership costs following the new improved GST 2.0, easier financing conditions and overall a positive consumer sentiment are expected to support the continued demand momentum.

items.statement: One new EPDM line operational in Q2 FY27, two more lines to be added in FY27
items.quote: And out of that, one new line would be operational in the Q2 itself. And we would be further investing in another 2 lines in this financial year.

items.statement: Order book grew 23% year-on-year to ₹6,095 crores, reflecting continued customer traction and healthy pipeline
items.quote: Our order book has grown 23% year-on-year to ₹6,095 crores, and this reflects continued customer traction and a healthy pipeline of business.

items.statement: Management committed to delivering another healthy quarter in Q2 and will revisit guidance mid-year
items.quote: We continue to be positive. We are committed to have quarter 2 reflect the similar trend. So I think this is what the focus is.

items.statement: New vertical investments reduced 8% year-on-year to ₹37 crores; full-year investment expected to be broadly in line with prior expectations
items.quote: Total investments during the quarter reduced by 8% year-on-year to ₹37 crores from ₹41 crores last year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 111 bps to 2.8% driven by 63 bps gross margin improvement to 20% and operating leverage
items.quote: EBITDA increased 90% year-on-year to ₹96 crores with EBITDA margin expanding from 1.7% to 2.8%, an improvement of 111 basis points.

items.statement: Interest cost flat in USD terms; early payment discounts used to enhance gross margin while keeping finance cost directionally flat or lower
items.quote: Directionally, flat interest cost or going south.

items.statement: North America revenue grew 48% year-on-year; Europe revenue grew 21%; new mandates from marquee customers represent $330 million annual potential over 3-4 years
items.quote: During this quarter, we enhanced our customer base and new mandates from marquee customers, representing an annual business potential of approximately US $330 million.

items.statement: Sourcing-as-a-service GMV of ₹1,700 crores in Q1 yielded ₹42 crores revenue (2.5% of GMV) and ~₹10 crores PBT (25% of revenue); model expected to scale similarly for 2-3 years
items.quote: We had close to ₹1,700 crores of GMV that was under execution in the sourcing as a service business in quarter one. And that translated into approximately ₹42 crores of revenue, about 2.5% of the GMV.

items.statement: Ted Baker losses ~$2 million in Q1; full-year losses not expected to exceed $2-3 million; resolution with Authentic Brands Group underway
items.quote: We believe that on the whole for the entire year, the losses from Ted Baker should not exceed more than $2-$3 million.

items.statement: Net working capital improved to 1 day from 4 days; net debt reduced 73% to ₹29 crores; net debt/equity 0.02x, net debt/EBITDA 0.07x
items.quote: Net working capital reduced from 4 days at March 2026 to just 1 day at June 2026. This improvement, together with strong operating cash generation helped us reduce net debt from ₹105 crores to ₹29 crores, a reduction of 73% during the quarter.

items.statement: AI and digital transformation underway to enhance productivity, improve decision-making and create operating leverage; SAP upgrade to S/4HANA in progress
items.quote: By embedding AI and digital capabilities across sourcing, pricing, supply management, data and operation, we are very positive and expect to enhance productivity, improve decision-making and create greater operating leverage as we scale.

items.statement: Manufacturing margin ~6.5% currently from value retailers; Busana partnership to upgrade customer profile to fashion customers and improve margins
items.quote: As you know, we make at present EBIT margin of close to 6.5% on our manufacturing, that is largely coming in from catering to value retailers. With this Busana partnership, we get to engage with more and more fashion customers, and we also get to benefit from the skill set that Busana brings in.

items.statement: PDS Ventures investment restricted to sub-₹10 crores annually ($1-1.5 million); exploring external fund to leverage platform without additional PDS capital
items.quote: We're restricting that investment to sub ₹10 crores a year, so between $1 million to $1.5 million.

items.statement: Sourcing concentration in Bangladesh not expected to decline in absolute terms; percentage share to decrease as India, Egypt and other geographies scale
items.quote: We do not anticipate the absolute amount of sourcing we are doing from Bangladesh to go down. But at the same time, we see more and more traction building up from some of the geographies I just mentioned.

items.statement: Maintained FY27 revenue guidance of INR 6,000 crore and FY28 guidance of INR 7,500 crore; order inflow target INR 12,000-15,000 crore for FY27
items.quote: No. As of now, we are not contemplating any change in the guidance, what we had given during the last con-call. So, we are maintaining the same guidance. So, we received 5 new projects during the current financial year. So, we expected to secure a total new business worth of INR12,000 crores to INR15,000 crores in FY27

items.statement: Full-year FY27 bookings growth guidance of 35% to 40% over previous year, targeting INR2,100-2,200 crores
items.quote: So in terms of our guidance for the bookings, we've said we expect to grow by about 35% to 40% over previous year, which takes us to a range of INR2,100 crores to INR2,200 crores in terms of a number for the current year.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 business development target of INR4,000-5,000 crores GDV
items.quote: When it comes to business development, INR4,000 crores to INR5,000 crores was the GDV target or the aim we were looking at.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 EBITDA margin guidance on new sales of 22% to 25%
items.quote: We continue to hold our guidance for the full year FY27. So we expect to reach a bookings growth of 35% to 40% over previous year, business development of INR4,000 crores to INR5,000 crores during this year and EBITDA margins on new sales in the range of 22% to 25%.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 launch pipeline guidance of INR3,000-3,500 crores booking value across 6 projects
items.quote: So Amit, we have guided for about INR3000 crores to INR3,500 crores of booking value that we are intending to pu t in terms of the fresh supply in the market

items.statement: Full-year FY27 operating cash flow target of INR400-500 crores
items.quote: So last year, we had done about INR400 crores of OCF. And what we mentioned even in our prev ious call that this year, we are targeting to be somewhere in the range of INR400 crores to INR500 crores on the OCF front

items.statement: FY27 land acquisition outflow guidance of INR600-900 crores
items.quote: So today, when we look at the land outflows, we might be closer to in the range of INR600 crores to INR900 crores.

items.statement: Added projects with aggregate GDV of approximately INR2,600 crores in Q1 FY27 including Goregaon redevelopment and South Ahmedabad horizontal development
items.quote: We added projects with an aggregate gross development value of approximately INR2,600 crores, which includes redevelopment project in Goregaon, Mumbai and the horizontal residential development in South of Ahmedabad.

items.statement: Portfolio EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 22-25%, with JD projects at lower end and outright projects at higher end
items.quote: Largely, I think, more than horizontal and I would say, vertical, I think for us, the margin percentage has varied, whether it's been an outright project or a JD project. When we give a range of 22% to 25%, probably I think our JD projects are slightly on the lower end of this pa rticular range and our outright projects are on the higher end of the range

items.statement: Underlying demand remains strong across core markets of Gujarat, Bengaluru and MMR
items.quote: Yes. I would say, Amit, the underlying demand is still quite strong.

items.statement: Price increase cycle stabilizing, underwriting not dependent on large price hikes, expecting moderated price increases
items.quote: My personal view is, I think now the price increase cycle, I think, is stabilizing. While be cause the demand remains strong, there are pockets where there are opportunities to pull up the pricing. But at least when we are underwriting, our business plan, we are ensuring we are not dependent on very large price hike

items.statement: Comfortable with debt-to-equity up to 1:1, currently at 0.29x, providing headroom for growth
items.quote: So we have said also in the past, and we are maintaining our comfort at 1:1 debt equity. So till that le vel, we are quite

items.statement: 4-5 year growth plan targeting 25-30% CAGR, with balanced inventory across Ahmedabad, Bengaluru and Mumbai markets
items.quote: When we look at, firstly, our 4- to 5-year plan, I think our guidance has been that we can continue to grow at about 25% to 30% CAGR. And I think we remain quite confident that we should be able to achieve this.

items.statement: Unrecognized revenue of INR3,825 crores expected to be recognized over next 4 years, with plotted projects over 2-3 years and high-rise over ~4 years
items.quote: Broadly, I would say that all of this would get recognized over the next 4 years.

items.statement: Estimated operating cash flows of over INR5,119 crores from existing portfolio over next 4-5 years
items.quote: Looking ahead, our existing project portfolio provides strong cash flow visibility with estimated operating cash flows of over INR5,119 crores expected to be realized over the next 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: Long-term credit rating upgraded to AA- with stable outlook by India Ratings
items.quote: Another encouraging development during the quarter was the upgradation of our long-term credit rating by India Ratin g to AA- with a stable outlook

items.statement: Goregaon redevelopment project: 6.7 lakh sq ft carpet area for sale, ~200 units for members, ~4 years to complete after launch
items.quote: So the carpet area that we are generating for the market is about 6.7 lakh square feet. It's a redevelopment project. So this is the area that we will be putting for sale. Remaining, of course, there is a redevelopment component that we are building for the members.

items.statement: Targeting net EBITDA margin well above 47% for FY27 and at least 50% for FY28 on a consolidated basis
items.quote: Patanjali Keswani: 2027 will not be 47%, it will be better. But fiscal 2028, if we do not do 50%, then we have underperformed.

items.statement: Expecting around 2,000 managed and franchised room openings in FY27, broadly confident despite potential minor slippage
items.quote: Broadly, I am pretty confident to be around the 2,000 Keys mark and, things happen. But from the pipeline that we have today and, and the kind of relationships we have with our, with our owners, I feel largely confident unless something large falls on our head, but 2,000 should be okay

items.statement: Targeting Rs. 60 crore EBITDA from Keys portfolio once fully renovated and operating at full performance
items.quote: Basically, I said we are targeting a Rs. 60 crore EBITDA from Keys, and I think that is something that we will achieve

items.statement: Balance renovation spend on remaining 300 Keys rooms estimated at Rs. 13-14 crore at Rs. 4-5 lakh per key
items.quote: I would say that we would end up when we finish the full portfolio, the balance spend on 300 rooms would be about Rs. 13 - Rs. 14 crore

items.statement: Fleur pursuing ~2,500 rooms for capital deployment with Warburg's Rs. 960 crore infusion and Rs. 200-300 crore balance sheet funds
items.quote: Last quarter also we had said that we are pursuing rooms of around 2,500 Keys. So that pursuit is still on, and we are very hopeful to achieve that in the few quarters ahead. We are very confident on the capital side

items.statement: Signed 13 managed and franchised hotels with 1,020 rooms in Q1 FY27, over 3x the inventory opened
items.quote: In this quarter, we also signed 13 managed and franchised hotels with 1,020 rooms, which is over 3x of the inve ntory that we opened

items.statement: Combined operational and pipeline inventory stands at 23,381 rooms across 279 hotels in 170+ cities
items.quote: Our combined operational and pipeline inventory now stands at 23,381 rooms across 279 hotels in 170+ cities, of which 135 hotels, which is 11,946 rooms across 80-plus cities are already operational

items.statement: Q1 FY27 net EBITDA margin at 43.8%, down 99 bps YoY due to SAR provision and GST input credit loss adding 3.1% of revenue to expenses
items.quote: Our net EBITDA margin for Q1 FY27 stood at 43.8%, which was 99 basis points less than 44.8%, which we achieved last year in Q1 FY26. This drop was due to Provision for Stock Appreciation Rights and the loss of input credit in the GST levied, which increased our expenses by 3.1% of total revenue in Q1 this year versus zero in the previous year same quarter

items.statement: Pro forma Lemon Tree (post-demerger) Q1 FY27 net EBITDA margin improved to 58.1% from 54.2% YoY, up 383 bps before SAR provision
items.quote: For Lemon Tree on a pro forma basis in Q1 FY27, revenue stood at Rs. 65.7 crore versus Rs. 54 crore in Q1 last year, which is up 22%. Net EBITDA before provision for stock appreciation rights was Rs. 38.1 crore versus Rs. 29.3 crore and Net EBITDA margin improved to 58.1% from 54.2%, up 383 basis points

items.statement: GST mitigation strategy focuses on shifting rooms above Rs. 7,500 ARR to reduce GST impact, currently estimated at ~2% of net revenue
items.quote: Our GST impact broadly, I would say, you could still say this is ballpark in the range of 2% of net of our overall revenue

items.statement: Q2 FY27 significantly better than Q1 with July showing great recovery and August continuing solid
items.quote: Neelendra Singh: Absolutely. I think Q1 sounds like everybody caught a little bit of a cold. Q2 is significantly better, and July was great, good recovery in July and August continues to be solid as well.

items.statement: West Asia conflict reduced inbound travel causing corporate demand softness in CBD locations like Mumbai and Gurgaon, partially offset by retail strategy in Delhi, Hyderabad, Bengaluru
items.quote: That led to the biggest impact of that was lesser inbound traffic and the uncertainty. Now that had second order effects. And in our segment, that translated largely towards lesser domestic travel as a second order effect of less inbound travel

items.statement: Fleur debt-to-EBITDA target to hover around 2x long-term; may briefly exceed during 6 big hotel developments but currently comfortable at ~Rs. 1,275 crore group debt vs Rs. 700 crore EBITDA
items.quote: We are very clear. See, occasionally, we are building 6 big hotels, which is what our plan is, debt may briefly cross 2x existing EBITDA. But our long-term plan is that in Fleur debt-to-EBITDA should hover around 2x, and that is a good sign because it means we are able to productively deploy capital

items.statement: Fee income from third-party managed hotels grew 42% YoY to Rs. 22.8 crore in Q1 FY27; total management fee up 21% to Rs. 45.4 crore
items.quote: income from management and franchise contracts from third - party owned hotels stood at Rs. 22.8 crore in Q1 this year, an increase of 42% year- on-year. Fees from Fleur Hotels stood at Rs. 22.6 crore, up 6% year-on-year. Total management fee from Lemon Tree stood at Rs. 45.4 crore, an increase of 21% year- on-year

items.statement: Expect acceleration in Lemon Tree fee income over next 8-12 quarters driven by signings trajectory (5,000 rooms signed in FY26 opening in FY29) and Fleur developments
items.quote: And I think over the next 8 -12 quarters, you will start seeing acceleration in the fee income of Lemon Tree

items.statement: Q1 was an aberration; Q2 issues resolved, revenue improvement expected via ARR and balanced occupancy mix
items.quote: Q1, as I said, was an aberration. I still feel and maintain we could have done better. But in Q2, I think all these issues will be resolved. and we will go back to the expected level of improvement in revenue through a mix of ARR and a more balanced mix of ARR and occupancy.

items.statement: Renovation of 487-room Delhi portfolio nearly complete; 37 rooms under renovation, both hotels at 90%+ occupancy, opening by end of Q2
items.quote: I think in the entire portfolio of 487 rooms, 37 rooms are balanced, which are currently under renovation. And the sad thing is both the hotels are doing over 90% occupancy. So there is a real loss of revenue, but we will open this by the end of Q2.

items.statement: Renovated hotels showing RevPAR improvement; confident of significant RevPAR improvement by end of year
items.quote: And wherever we have renovated, we see that customer response is good. So now local market conditions may be X, Y Z, but we are confident that this renovation is going to lead to a significant improvement in RevPAR as it plays out by the end of this year.

items.statement: International expansion targeting 3-hour flight markets where Indians travel; UAE, Nepal, Thailand, Maldives identified; 32M Indians travelled overseas, 12M+ to key markets
items.quote: So what are the markets where Indians go? The biggest and best market is UAE. You will be surprised to know that in spite of war, the Indian movement to UAE was not significantly affected other than a few days, it is still very much there.

items.statement: Keys target: Rs 6.5 lakh per key EBITDA, 50% margin, Rs 13-14 lakh per room revenue, Rs 115-120 crore revenue, Rs 60 crore EBITDA
items.quote: I would not say RevPAR uplift. I would say simply that we have a simple target, Keys should generate Rs. 6.5 lakhs per key EBITDA. And if Keys has an EBITDA margin of 50% when it is stable, it means Rs. 13 lakhs - Rs. 14 lakhs per room. So that is what we want. We want a revenue of about Rs. 115 - Rs. 120 crore from Keys and a Rs. 60 crore EBITDA.

items.statement: Managed portfolio same-store revenue growth 9-10%; new hotels adding incremental fee income; fee income growth rate to accelerate as signed rooms catch up
items.quote: Same-store revenue growth for managed portfolio was in the late single digits; I think it was 9 %-10%. One of the reasons is some of the hotels, which we opened last year were not stable in the managed portfolio. So they stabilized this year. So on a low base, there was a higher impact of revenue.

items.statement: Renovation spend tapering: next year OPEX and CAPEX in renovation will meander towards 1% of revenue from past 3 years' levels
items.quote: But what I can say is that next year onwards, OPEX and CAPEX in renovation will meander towards 1% of revenue from what it was in the past 3 years.

items.statement: High-value renovations (Rs 10-12 lakh/key) mostly done except Delhi and Bengaluru; Q3-Q4 will see refurbs (Rs 2.5-3 lakh/room); full portfolio new by FY27, norm from FY28
items.quote: As far as Lemon Tree goes, we will have finished the full renovation of the main hotels and refurbishment of a lot of Keys and other hotels that needed intervention in FY27. In FY28, we will revert to norm, which is really no renovations, but a continuing thing on refurb.

items.statement: Q1 renovation spend Rs 9.8 crore (2.25-2.3% of revenue) vs normal Rs 3 crore (1-1.2%); incremental Rs 6 crore; EBITDA margin to recover 2-2.5% next summer, targeting 50% net EBITDA margin
items.quote: We spent about Rs. 9.8 crore in renovation in Q1 which is about 2.25 %-2.3% of revenue. So that was the total spend. Now normally, what would we have spent? Normally, we would have spent Rs. 3 crore, which is 1% or 1.2%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin deteriorated 1% on revenue but renovation spend was 2.25%; waterfall shows Rs 5 crore reduction vs last year; margins should recover as renovation tapers
items.quote: So, if you ask me, our EBITDA margin versus last year deteriorated by 1 % on revenue, but our spend in renovation was 2.25%. And if you see the waterfall change, it was a reduction in Rs. 5 crore over last year.

items.statement: Debt for new hotels matched to operating EBITDA, not presumed EBITDA; 1:1 debt-equity; first 2-2.5 years funded from equity, debt needed only in final year matched with cash flows
items.quote: So, we use operating EBITDA, known EBITDA to really look at debt for new hotels rather than fund new hotels based on a presumed EBITDA. So that is a standard risk mitigation practice that Lemon Tree has had from the beginning.

items.statement: Below-the-line expenses (corporate, talent, technology) will not grow at revenue rate; target 75-80% EBITDA margin long-term as fee income doubles and corporate costs drop to 20-25% of revenue
items.quote: When we say that we are targeting in Lemon Tree to ultimately have an EBITDA margin of 75%-80%, it means really, we are saying we will double our management fee income and our below-the-line expenses, which is basically talent and technology as a percentage of revenue will then drop to 20%-25%.

items.statement: GST impact reduction strategy: increase % of rooms sold above Rs 7,500; currently 52% below, 48% above; target weighted average reduction from 2% to 1.7% and lower; some hotels will never reach Rs 7,500
items.quote: Our intent is not that we will be able to get rid of all the rooms will not go to Rs. 7,500. Our intent is that this percentage should ramp up so that a larger and larger percentage of rooms are sold at over Rs. 7,500.

items.statement: Negotiated vs non-negotiated room mix balance improving; better balance visible in July-August; Q2 onwards will see better balance between retail/negotiated and non-negotiated
items.quote: I guess like I said, as we achieve more balance, which is already visible in July and August, you can certainly see in the next presentation, you will potentially notice a better balance of negotiated and non - negotiated b usiness, no doubt about it

items.statement: Fleur demerger: Warburg investing USD 100M at USD 1B valuation for 10% primary; post-demerger shareholding Lemon Tree 41%, Warburg 36%, public 33%; 2,500 rooms acquisition target
items.quote: It is a valuation which is fixed at, I think, USD1 billion. So they are investing in Fleur at USD1 billion. So they are giving USD100 million for 10% primary.

items.statement: Fleur to grow rooms by over 50% by FY30 (from ~6,000 to ~9,300); revenue growth higher as incremental rooms are mostly Aurika brand; Lemon Tree reinventing as asset-light player at scale
items.quote: So we are saying Fleur will increase by over 50% in rooms by FY30 approximate, but much more in revenue because the incremental rooms that are being bought are all Aurika's other than some operating assets.

items.statement: Demerger approval process with SEBI, then NCLT, shareholder vote, creditors, GST; completion targeted first half of calendar 2027, conservatively late second half of next year
items.quote: So currently with SEBI, post we got the CCI approval and some scrutiny by the stock exchanges. So that is in process as of now, post which the NCLT process filing and meetings and hearings would start.

items.statement: Order backlog at end of Q1 FY27 was INR 32,222.1 crs, representing strong double-digit growth vs Q1 FY26
items.quote: As a result, we closed the quarter with an order backlog of INR 32,222.1 crs, representing strong double-digit growth compared with Q1 FY26 and providing good revenue visibility for the coming quarters.

items.statement: Operational EBITDA grew 135.0% YoY to INR 399.9 crs in Q1 FY27, including unrealized forex loss of INR 36.37 crs
items.quote: operational EBITDA grew 135.0% YoY to INR 399.9 crs. It is important to note that this EBITDA performance includes an unrealized foreign exchange loss of INR 36.37 crs recorded during the quarter.

items.statement: Profit before tax margin was 15.6% and profit after tax margin was 11.8% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: As a result, our profit before tax margin stood at 15.6%, while profit after tax margin was 11.8%.

items.statement: First BESS order (165 MW/330 MWh) received in Andhra Pradesh; modular scalable solution excluding batteries; margin profile to mature over time with localization
items.quote: The second project marks a major milestone for Hitachi Energy India. It is a 165 MW / 330 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project in Andhra Pradesh, reflecting strong validation of our capabilities in grid integration, power quality, and advanced energy solutions.

items.statement: Multiple data center orders secured including 40x2500 kVA project in Hyderabad; launched Grid-to-Rack solution for data centers
items.quote: In addition, we secured multiple data center orders from hyperscalers during the quarter. A notable project among these is a 40 × 2500 kVA data center project in Hyderabad, awarded by a leading Indian multinational conglomerate

items.statement: Railway and metro projects progressing slower than anticipated; expected to pick up from second half of FY27; transmission dip is temporary timing issue
items.quote: Railway projects are progressing slower than originally anticipated. Based on the discussion with the rail and metro authorities -- we expect it should pick from the second half of the year. Transmission is just a timing issue.

items.statement: Chinese players allowed in GIS/transformer market with 60-65% local content; management sees no material impact if level playing field maintained
items.quote: view is clear. More competition is welcome to meet the demand and supply challenges or perceived demand and supply challenges, if any. As long as there is a level playing field, we do not see any issue in competing and ensuring that our margin ambition is met in that

items.statement: Plant 6 commercialization on track for H1 FY27; mechanical completion done, validations and customer audits ongoing
items.quote: We are on track for the commercialization of Plant 6 in H1 of FY27, which will further strengthen our manufacturing capacity and enable us to support future growth opportunities.

items.quote: Our CAPEX cycle this year is much lower than last year. However, we still require these working capital funds.

items.quote: What we are signing now, therefore, sees to it that our FY '28-29, the annuity base at that point in time is taken care of what we are doing right now.

items.quote: But it is of course at a very high price, which is about almost 80% higher than the price that we were getting in March. So of course, there is an impact on margins due to that as well.

items.statement: IPO funds deployment to start in next two quarters across RegTech, AI solutions, payment infrastructure
