items.quote: During the quarter, we received orders for injector pen supplies following regulatory approvals secured for the sale of Semaglutide in Canada, Brazil by our pharmaceutical partners.

items.statement: Signed 2 new platform projects strengthening long-term product pipeline
items.quote: In addition, we have also signed 2 new platform projects, further strengthening our long-term product pipeline.

items.statement: Secured global project from FMCG customer and won new business in LED lighting segment
items.quote: In Q1 FY27, we secured a global project from an FMCG customer and also won new business in the LED lighting segment.

items.statement: Received business confirmations for new projects from Appliance and Automotive customers, onboarded new customer with 5 Consumer Electronic components
items.quote: During the quarter, we received business confirmations for new projects from both Appliance as well as Automotive customers. We also onboarded a new customers with orders covering 5 Consumer Electronic components.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 120 bps YoY to 29.7%, PAT margin expanded 40 bps to 17.1%
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR83 crores from INR70 crores, reflecting a growth of 18%, while EBITDA margin improved by 120 bps to 29.7%. Profit after tax stood at INR48 crores compared with INR41 crores in Q1 FY26, representing a growth of 17%. PAT margin improved to 17.1%, an expansion of 40 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Gross margin decline due to commodity and freight cost increases, pass-through delayed to May-July, expected to normalize by Q3
items.quote: So while the pass-through with some customers would have been delayed, would basically have happened between May and June. And with some customers, the cycle would have been probably in July. So that was the reason why you see some gross margin decline. We expect that the gross margin would come back to normalized level by quarter 3.

items.statement: Pen pricing not cost-plus; volume and market-driven contracts with annual price review mechanism based on inflation, polymers, contract longevity
items.quote: These are not cost-plus contracts. They're basically just volume and market-driven pricing contracts with the mechanism to do price review annually. So it all depends on the type of agreement. It's not a cost-plus business, first of all, right? It's an intellectual property-led business.

items.statement: Pen volume mix: 50-60% GLP-1, rest insulin plus other molecules
items.quote: You've got a bit more than insulin and GLP-1. So there is other therapies in the mix, but rough ballpark would be consider 50% to 60% GLP-1 and the rest would be insulin plus other molecule.

items.statement: Appointed dedicated heads of business development for Europe and North America, senior industry leaders, confident of securing partnership with major global pharma near term
items.quote: Building on this, I'm pleased to announce that we have appointed dedicated heads of business development for both Europe as well as North America, our 2 priority growth markets. Both are senior industry leaders and with them in place, we are in discussions and confident of securing a partnership with a major global pharmaceutical over the near term.

items.statement: Started commercial supply for Consumer Electronics, awarded 5 new components from new customer, supply to start before end of FY27
items.quote: We have started commercial supply. We also got awarded 5 new components, as I mentioned that in my earlier speech, from a new customer in Consumer Electronics, which we should be able to put into supply just before the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Semiconductor Trays: INR5 crores investment in existing facility for initial requirements
items.quote: Semiconductor Trays, I think we have mentioned that we are looking at investing about INR5 crores in our existing facility, which would meet initial requirements.

items.statement: Consumer Electronics new plant down south: INR80-100 crores investment planned
items.quote: On Consumer Electronics, again, we have said that once we set up a plant down south, we would be looking at an investment of somewhere between INR80 crores to INR100 crores in that facility.

items.statement: Consumer Electronics tooling and automation investments required from existing facility
items.quote: It will be from existing facility. But yes, there will be some investments which will be required in tooling and automation and everything, which we would be doing.

items.statement: Machine utilization improved to 50.2% in Q1 FY27 from 48.7% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Machine utilization improved to 50.2% during Q1 F Y27 compared with 48.7% in Q1 FY26, reflecting a gradual improvement in capacity utilization

items.statement: Exports accounted for 58% of consolidated revenue vs 76% YoY, shift due to Healthcare sales to domestic pharma companies who export finished drugs
items.quote: Exports accounted for approximately 58% of consolidated revenue during the quarter compared with 76% in the corresponding quarter last year. The change is primarily due to the growing contribution of our Healthcare business where products are supplied to g lobal markets through our Indian pharmaceutical customers

items.statement: No challenge retaining or hiring talent; pay well, ESOP eligibility coming, culture is fun environment, new manufacturing head Joe fully active
items.quote: I don't see a challenge retaining or hiring new employees. And our culture, Ritesh, it's a fun environment to work in. You should try it out.

items.statement: Customer partner supply chain issues could affect volume delivery despite Shaily capacity
items.quote: I mean it's an evolving situation because it's not just our ability to deliver. It's also customer partners having some short-term potential supply chain issues as well.

items.statement: Plan to deliver 2,500 units by end of FY27
items.quote: We plan to deliver 2,500 units by the end of financial year 2027.

items.statement: GDV increased from INR 6,000 crores to INR 14,000 crores over last five years
items.quote: Our GDV (Gross Development Value) has increased from INR 6,000 crore s to INR 14,000 crores in the last five years without any significant

items.statement: Q1 FY27 sales booking of 221 units (2.31 lakh sq ft) up 15% YoY in area and value to INR 173 crores
items.quote: During the quarter, the company achieved a sales booking of 221 units, which is equivalent to 2.31 lakh square feet and that is up by 15% on year-on-year in terms of area, amounting to INR 173 crores and again in value wise an increase of 15%.

items.statement: Average selling price per sq ft remained same at INR 7,500; average ticket size INR 78 lakhs per unit
items.quote: Our average selling price per square feet has also remained same at INR 7,500 per square feet which is almost similar to Q1FY26. For this first quarter of Q1 FY27, the average price of the unit which has been sold stood at INR 78 lakhs per unit.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA INR 28 crores at 21% margin; PAT INR 10 crores at 7.4% margin
items.quote: The EBITDA stood at INR 28 crores and the EBITDA margin stood at 21%. The PAT for the quarter stood at INR 10 crores with a PAT margin of 7.4%.

items.statement: Residential EBITDA margins expected to gradually move up to 30%-35% once Town Villas and villa projects contribute largely
items.quote: Given the real estate sector, sell product of residentials and construct, build, and sell, the EBITDA margins would gradually move up around, 30% - 35% once Town Villas and the villa projects contribute largely.

items.statement: Hospitality segment expected to contribute INR 50 crores+ PAT per year from third or fourth year
items.period: third or fourth year from now
items.quote: And it would in terms of value, the hospitality sector would contribute say third or fourth year from now to an average of INR 50 crores of PAT per year. This represents an annuity income model, with both hotels expected to contribute INR 50 crores+.

items.statement: INR 500 crores total investment program for club and hospitality business over three years
items.quote: For three years the company will deploy INR 500 crores of capital, by debt or by internal resources for these projects.

items.statement: Net debt INR 818 crores, net worth INR 460 crores as of 30 June 2026; focused on reducing debt next year onwards
items.quote: On the balance sheet, our net debt as on 30th June , 2026 stands at INR 818 crores and the net worth stands at INR 460 crores. We remain focused and confident on reducing our debt next year onwards as some of our residential projects have started nearing completion and these reductions will be partially offset by new loans which are being taken for building the annuity assets.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio expected to gradually come down as projects mature and equity builds up
items.quote: Though the intentions are there, yes, there is a plan for it. The debt-to-equity ratio will gradually come down because once the projects get matured the equity gets on, the reserves and capital reserves get on adding up to every quarter-to-quarter or year-to-year basis.

items.statement: Aspire to maintain 40%-45% premium, 30%-35% middle income, 20% affordable housing mix
items.quote: We still will have a mixed bag of it and going forward we can say that we would aspire to have 40%-45% as premium segment and around 30% - 35% as middle income group segment and 20% as affordable housing.

items.statement: Received occupancy certificates for 1,495 units across four projects; ready for possession in coming quarters
items.quote: We are happy to update that our projects are getting completed, we received occupancy certificate for Arihant 5 Anaika, Arihant 6 Anaika, Arihant Anant, Arihant A aradhya Phase 1 and that means around, 1,495 units have been completed and ready for offering of the possession in the coming quarters and days

items.statement: Collections for Q1 FY27 stood at INR 161 crores, up 28% YoY
items.quote: The collections also for the quarter stood at INR 161 crores registered a yearly growth of 28%.

items.statement: Construction expenditures rising due to geopolitical factors and labour shortages; inventory in hand neutralizes cost impact on balance sheet
items.quote: The construction expenditu res already is on a rise due to the geopolitical features, but given the inventory in hand, we are able to see that those increase in cost of the total project versus to the inventory in hand can be equalized or can be neutralized

items.statement: Pre-sales to revenue recognition cycle averages 90 days under percentage completion method
items.quote: It's a general behaviour that for an ongoing project, we are into percentage completion method. Hence, all the pre-sales which happen, it takes around 90 days on an average for them to get into the mode of revenue recognition.

items.statement: No plans for geographic diversification beyond MMR; MMR 3.0 is double the size of Mumbai city with robust demand
items.quote: No, because as when we talk about single region though it is MMR and Mumbai 3.0 which is already a very large envelope. It is double the size of the C ity of Mumbai. For the sake of new geographical diversification with new cities, there are no plans for it in those ways

items.statement: Mumbai 3.0 market just starting off, not yet reached saturation peak unlike Pune, Bangalore, NCR
items.quote: Well today also Mum bai happens to be the core cent re where the state of Maharashtra is spending the highest in terms of bringing up job creations and hence the demand is robust. There is supply also, there is competition, but then that tells that this is the core market and when we compare it to Pune or Bangalor e, it is like the Mumbai 3.0 is just started off and has yet not achieved its satura

items.statement: No new land acquisitions planned for FY27; focus on executing INR 14,000 crores GDV pipeline over 6-7 years
items.quote: Going forward for this financial year, we don't have any program for new capital investments for the business development as there is a good handsome size of projects in hand worth INR 14,000 crores and given the scalability possible at our end, it still is in cycle of six to seven years to complete up this INR 14,000 crores.

items.statement: Average realization expected to increase ~10% from current levels with given product mix; could rise more if new additions are premium
items.quote: Given the whole portfolio with us in our size, if any new addition is firstly of premium segment, then the average rate would increase or else it would be something around 10% addition to the current ones with the given mix of products which we are operating today.

items.statement: Older affordable projects below INR 5,000/sq ft have single-digit PAT margins of 9%-10%; middle-income projects up to 15% PAT margins; premium projects ~20% EBITDA margins
items.quote: Well, as you see on project-to-project basis, the older projects and affordable housing projects which are below Rs. 5,000 per sq.ft, there the total margins are on a single digit and that is something to a tune of 9% to 10%. The middle-income group projects like Arihant Aalishan etc. gives up to 15% PAT margins. And 12% to 13% margin for the Aalishan projects similarly. The premium projects would

items.statement: Sector faces shortage of skilled manpower across labour, engineering, and sales teams; implementation is core key
items.quote: Sector scalability is still increasing overall, which also shows up that implementation is the core key and that is where , there is a shortage of man resources at skill development right from the workers at the labour at the site as well as the monitoring engineering team as well as the sales people and that becomes the key factor.

items.statement: Only past fundraise was INR 36 crores via preferential; GDV grew to INR 14,000 crores without significant fundraise
items.quote: Our GDV (Gross Development Value) has increased from INR 6,000 crore s to INR 14,000 crores in the last five years without any significant fundraise. The only fundraise which we did in the past was INR 36 crores via preferential

items.statement: Investments in annuity assets closing for second hotel near Imagicaa; first 5-star hotel at World Villas with ITC concluded
items.quote: We are happy to share that ASL is already transacting and emerging as an diversified developer rather than only pure residential. Our investments in annuity assets is closing down for the second hotel also with Sunday at near Imagicaa. The earlier one which has been, which has been concluded is the 5-star hotel at World Villas.

items.statement: Next quarter (Q2 FY27) expected to be much bigger than Q1 with revenue and profit from both Jonnagiri and Altyn Tor
items.quote: I think the next quarter is going to be much bigger than this. But however, the mo st significant part of this June quarter, again, it is the contribution from Geomysore

items.statement: Board approved Rs.137 Crores raise via CCDs, equity shares and warrants pending shareholder approval; HNAs and management participating
items.quote: And the other important factor is we are able to raise Rs.137 Crores. Board has approved this particular raise through CCDs, equity shares and equity warrants. And of course, we have to wait for the shareholders' approval.

items.statement: Rs.137 Crore raise to fund exploration of projects other than Kyrgyzstan, which is near full-scale production
items.quote: And this money is going to be used for the exploration of the other projects other than the Kyrgyzstan project, which is now almost ready for the production, full scale production rather.

items.statement: Board changes: Mr. Elango appointed Chairman (ex-CEO Cairn Energy, founded HOEC); Ms. Jade Devenish added as Non-Executive Non-Independent Director (ex-MD Geomysore Services 2012-2022)
items.quote: And we made Mr. Elango as the Chairman of the Board. And I think most of you know Elango has a tremendous track record. He was ex-CEO of Cairn Energy and then he established HOEC, which has become a star on the stock exchange and it got into the production.

items.statement: Jonnagiri expansion from 1,010 to 2,500 tpd processing capacity targeting up to 2 tons gold per annum around 2029-30
items.quote: As of today we have 1010 processing facility approvals, but whereas we are going to increase it to 2,500 tons per day, which actually would take us at some point in time to 2 tons of gold, up to 2 tons of gold, that is the maximum anticipated from this project, 2 tons of gold per annum from this project, that could happen somewhere around 29 or 30.

items.statement: Jonnagiri Q1 FY27 produced 112 kg dore yielding 90 kg bullion; ~1 kg/day run rate; 59 kg sold for Rs.87 Cr revenue, Rs.25 Cr PAT, Deccan share Rs.6.35 Cr
items.quote: in the Q1 that is up to June, the project has prod uced 112 kilos of dore bar from which about 90 kilos of bullion has been produced out of it. So, that effectively means it is like a 1 kilo per day is the strike rate in that project that we have already achieved

items.statement: Jonnagiri end-Q1 stock: 40 kg gold + 60 kg dore (~80 kg gold equivalent); current quarter adding another ~90 kg gold
items.quote: And most importantly you must also note by end of quarter one there is a 40 kilos of gold and 60 kilos of dore bar in the stock which effectively means that about 80 kilos of gold if you convert dore also into the gold about 80 kilos of gold is in the stock and in the current quarter again it will add another 90 kilos of gold.

items.statement: Gold price ~Rs.1,50,000 per 10 grams in current quarter enabling price arbitrage and higher revenue
items.quote: And in terms of gold sales, if you look at the previous quarter to the current quarter, last time the price was slightly low whereas now in this quarter the price is pretty good. I mean you might be seeing that it is like almost like Rs.1,50,000 per 10 grams.

items.statement: Altyn Tor (Kyrgyzstan) gravity circuit commissioned, leaching circuit added; larger leach circuit and tailings dam completion imminent; inauguration very soon
items.quote: we have already commissioned the gravity circuit and we are producing gravity concentrates and now the leaching circuit has been added to it. So we are now lit erally very close to the full scale production which I have always been envisaging

items.statement: Altyn Tor first 4-5 years production from 0.6 Mt tailings (1.3 g/t Au, ~780 kg Au) and ~1 Mt low-grade stockpile; underground resource target >5 tons Au by Oct 2026 adding 6-7 years mine life
items.quote: The first phase revised mine design and life of mine plan we are going to deliver by October 2026 and we are expecting that the underground resources are going to be more than 5 tons. So that would easily take this project to almost like an addition of 6 to 7 years.

items.statement: Altyn Tor employs ~200 locals; adding ~100 more (30 Indian engineers, 70+ local) for total ~350 jobs; Kyrgyz government offered additional ~10 ton gold project
items.quote: With the establishment of the new leaching circuit and enhanced ca pacity, we are going recruit another 100 odd people in this. About 30 engineers are going from India and more than 70 people are going to be recruited. In fact, the recruitment process is already on

items.statement: Kalevala (Finland) $1-2M investment for 51% stake in coming quarter; 1,500m drilling to start ~Sep 15 targeting 4 tons Au resource; production timeline beyond 2028-29
items.quote: By doing this investment of about $1 to $2 million, actually $1 million will take us to 51%, which we want to do it in this coming quarter itself. Money will be used for the drilling activities there.

items.statement: Kalevala Kuikka deposit: ~1 ton Au at >5 g/t avg grade (vs Jonnagiri 1.4-1.5 g/t); target 4 tons via drilling; Pahkalampi ~2 tons at 3.5 g/t; combined >5-6 tons potential
items.quote: Just as I may come back to them if I say, the Jonnagiri, the average grade is around 1.4 or 1.5 grams whereas in this place, the average grade is 5 grams per ton. And also through the drilling, we are going to increase the resource to almost 4 tons.

items.statement: Ganajur project awaiting court verdict; recent Gadchiroli iron ore judgment restoring pre-2015 rights strengthens legal position; mining lease could enable ~1 ton Au production in 2-3 years
items.quote: Particularly, I can take a case that is in Gadchiroli iron ore case where the court has clearly ordered to restore the rights that have been accrued before 2015. So that gives us a strong legal position on that basis we are going to argue in the court.

items.statement: Due diligence on 3 new gold assets (one in Kyrgyzstan ~10 tons offered by government) targeting production by 2028 to fill gap after Kyrgyzstan and Finland
items.quote: So the idea is we look at the near-term gold producing assets so that in the year 2028, will come into the production. Because if you look at our growth story, the way it is panning out, particularly in the gold, once we establish the Kyrgyzstan project this year, And next year and the following year, in terms of the gold projects, there may not be anything which can deliver, which will come into

items.statement: Bhalukona (Chhattisgarh) Ni-Cu-PGE: 2,500m drilled in 15 holes, 1.3 km mineralized zone identified; targeting 3,000 tpd plant (larger than Jonnagiri); mining lease application by mid-2026; feasibility by mid-2026
items.quote: We are thinking of about 3000 tons per day processing plant, which effectively means this plant would be even bigger than what is going to be set up in Jonnagiri. So this would require a good amount of capex, but those details will come out only when we complete the process flow sheet, which we will do by mid next year.

items.statement: Logrosan (Spain) Tungsten: 3,000m drilled in 7 holes at Dehesa, all hit W or W-Sn; best 1.21% W at 535m depth, 7.5m width; preliminary resource model by early Oct; targeting 1,000 tpd plant (~3 Mt resource for 10yr)
items.quote: preliminary based on our, I d o not say intuition, but based on our guesstimate rather, we are looking at 1000 tons of processing facility. That means about 300,000 tons of input every year into the plant. So if it is a 10 year project, we will be looking at around 3 million tons of overall resource in this project

items.statement: Mozambique Li-Cs-Ta: 1,500-2,000m drilling from mid/end Sep; beneficiation testwork; target 200 tpd concentrate plant by end-2027 or Q1 2028; potential expansion to 1,000 tpd with 3 Mt resource
items.quote: We aim to set up a 200 ton per day processing plant to concentrate lithium and tantalum by the end of 2027. We hope to set it up because the money that is coming in now is really helping us to fast track this particular project.

items.statement: Mozambique pegmatites show high Ta values (standalone Ta mines work at ~500 ppm); Li 0.5-1% Li2O mineable via concentrate upgrade to 4% Li2O for battery makers
items.quote: A lithium ore body if it has about 0.5% to 1% of LiO2 here what I have shown is LiO2. It is a bit of a technical thing. 0.5% to 1% of lithium if it is available that can easily get into the mineable situation because we are going to set up a concentrate plant and upgrade it to the 4% LiO2 which is sold to the battery makers.

items.statement: Tanzania gold projects deprioritized due to unsatisfactory results; only two areas retain hope
items.quote: Compared to other gold projects, the results are not fully satisfactory at this point in time. There are two areas which still have hope, probably we will take it forward. But I think considering the number of projects that we have, Tanzania project is still in a kind of slightly in the back in the queue.

items.statement: Bhalukona neighbor Vedanta exploring adjacent area; potential concentrate offtake to Indian smelters (Adani, Vedanta, Birla)
items.quote: As you know our next neighbor in the project are already Vedanta who have been also exploring in that area. So if you see on the map there is a yellow dotted line. That is the mineralized area and within that there are some red patches that are shown.

items.statement: Kalevala concentrates may be shipped to India for refining to capture price advantage
items.quote: And if possible we can bring those concentrates to India to refine and produce gold which will have a price advantage.

items.statement: Jonnagiri price arbitrage: selling more when prices high (currently ~Rs.1.5L/10g) to maximize revenue
items.quote: Whenever the prices are good, you will sell more and then try to get more revenue.

items.statement: Jonnagiri created ~1,000 direct and ~1,000 indirect jobs in drought-prone area; water treatment plants built; strong government support for expansion
items.quote: And last but not the least with regard to this project , it has created thousand employment s already on the site and a similar number of employment outside the Company has been created. A lot of value creation has been done in this project and hence government is coming forward to help

items.statement: Jonnagiri FY27 production target 500-600 kg, FY28 750-800 kg
items.quote: in terms of annual production we still stick to those numbers around 500 to 600 from J onnagiri this year and it will increase to 750 to 800 kilos next year

items.statement: Kyrgyzstan FY27 production 150-160 kg, FY28 300-350 kg
items.quote: we are confident we would be able to reach to this 150, 160 kilos of production in 2027 from Dehesa and from then onwards 300 to 350 kilos we are going to do.

items.quote: If you set up a 1000 ton processing plant, which we are planning to do in many of the projects other than the Bhalukona project, which requires around 3000 ton processing facility, the capital would be in the range of 400 to 500 Crores like what we have spent in J onnagiri. items.quote: Now, yes, we may require around 2,000 Crores.

items.statement: Current Rs 137 Cr fundraise for drilling; future funding via off-take arrangements, debt and equity
items.quote: Now, with this current fundraise of about Rs.137 Crores, a large part of it is going into the drilling operations on these projects.

items.quote: my belief is going forward for these kind of projects, the funding will come through a kind of off -take arrangement. items.statement: Jonnagiri underground block capex upwards of Rs 400 Cr in 4-5 years, funded from internal accruals
items.quote: There we will be sinking the shafts and those shafts could go slightly deeper, like almost like 600 to 500 meter deep shafts that we are going to build. So that may require slightly larger capital. It could be upwards of 400 Crores, I believe another 4-5 years. Again that will also be funded to the internal accruals.

items.statement: Battery metals demand driven by India energy storage growth; Adani building large storage
items.quote: In fact, even some of our partners are setting up like even they are setting up large storage facilities and of course the largest being done by Adani group of industries. So battery storage is going to be a very, very prominent feature in the next 10 years and that battery storage would require so much of battery related metals in this country.

items.quote: So that is the strategy we have been developing and that is what we are looking at. items.quote: to stabilize to about 65%, 70% of EBITDA, I believe it will take another quarter or two. That is how it is going to be and really this coming quarter is something with a lot of gold in the stock and also the production upgradation that is going to happen in terms of grade, not in terms of the plantr anything.

items.statement: Jonnagiri cash flows via dividends from Geomysore; unlikely this FY due to expansion capex
items.quote: In terms of dividends, it is based on the Board's decision of Geomysore and it also depends on how the project is moving forward, because now there is a lot of expansion that is going on in that project. items.quote: So then we thought it us better to have an M oU with them and also partially fund their research efforts so that as a part of this we will be supplying lithium and nickel and graphite concentrates to them so that they can work on a specific battery and eventually when we do it the technology will be transferred to us, we have a different kind of agreement with them.

items.statement: MoU with XTerra for critical mineral beach sand blocks in eastern India; technical support and downstream partnership
items.quote: And also, in the downstream industries, their help is going to be there. If we, at any point in time, decide to go further down into the refinement and etc., they will be our partners.

items.quote: getting this mineral assets is not easy , wherever you go, once you made an offer, then a counter offer always given by another company primarily from our neighbors that is Chinese. items.quote: As I said, the microfinance will be contained between 8%-10%. That will be the cap on a consolidated basis we will put.

items.statement: Sees good momentum in July and August in customers and tonnage.
items.quote: This first quarter, despite seasonally being slow, we had a good momentum, and we continue to build on that momentum in July and August as well, both from a customer perspective and from a tonnage perspective as well.

items.statement: Pricing expected to be in a broad band around 18%.
items.quote: From a pricing perspective, we will probably be in this broad band around 18%. And basically, that's where we will be.

items.statement: Incremental funding cost expected around 8.8 to 9.
items.quote: On an incremental basis, I would say, we will be around the 8.8 to 9 handle, is what I would look at.

items.statement: Interest rate on income-generating gold loan scheme ranges from 14%-16%.
items.quote: The interest rate on this scheme, it ranges from 14%-16%.

items.statement: Income-generating gold loans go up to 85% LTV for monthly EMI.
items.quote: No. Income-generating loan based on the cash flow, we go up to 85%, it is monthly EMI 85% and if it is quarterly, the submission scheme is lesser to that . So the LTV is higher.

items.statement: Vehicle finance GNPA elevated at 13.3%; focus is on collections.
items.quote: Focus is now on collections as GNPA continues to be elevated at 13.3% versus 10.4% in prior quarter.

items.statement: Microfinance disbursement expected at INR400 crores to INR500 crores.
items.quote: The growth will remain at a level of, I feel like INR400 crores to INR500 crores, as a disbursement in MFI.

items.statement: No more vehicle loans to be disbursed this year; may reconsider in FY2028.
items.quote: We do not want to disburse any more vehicle loans during this year. After one year, that probably in FY 2028, we may consider whether to restart or not.

items.statement: New MD and CEO Ashish Singh expected to join by January 1, 2027.
items.quote: Mr. Ashish Singh has been appointed as the MD and CEO and expected to join by January 1st of 2027.

items.statement: Management expects mid-single-digit volume growth for FY27 and aims to maintain or improve EBITDA margins above 11%
items.quote: We remain positive for the entire year for both the single-digit margin -- single-digit volume growth and also a double-digit margin or the margins which we've given today. We'll only better that going forward.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved 360 bps to 11.6% driven by higher capacity utilization and JV profitability
items.quote: As a result of capacity utilization, our EBITDA margins have gone up on operational efficiencies, both on capacity utilization in our plants and also on the JV performances. So EBITDA margins go up by 3.6% to 11.6% for the quarter.

items.statement: Management targets EBITDA margin of 12%+ and believes current 11%+ margins are sustainable due to operational efficiencies
items.quote: Yes, absolutely. That's the target that we achieve 12% and more. But currently, we are very confident of showing the 11-plus percent margins, which we showed last quarter and this quarter.

items.statement: Announced 9+ million sqm greenfield plant in South with INR 220 crore capex, operational by Q3/Q4 FY28, adding INR 350 crore potential revenue
items.quote: Because of that, we have announced setting up a 9 million square meter plant -- 9-plus million square meter plant in the South, which would be up and ready by in the next 12 to 15 months. This would give us a potential revenue of about INR350 crores.

items.statement: Total capex of INR 275 crore planned through FY27 end including South plant and balancing equipment across plants, 65-70% funded internally
items.quote: So from now to '27 end, we have already looked at approximately INR275 crores outlay, which includes the INR220 crores plant plus balancing equipment in various other plants and some more balancing equipment in the Bathware, sanitaryware plant.

items.statement: Adding 4-5 million sqm capacity via balancing equipment in existing lines (Bahadurgarh, Gujarat, Morbi, South) by mid-Q3 to Q4 FY27, focused on value-added products
items.quote: We are taking many more steps, which are all work in progress to augment further capacity by about 4 million to 5 million in our existing lines in Bahadurgarh in -- which is in Haryana and in Gujarat and in Morbi and also in the South.

items.statement: Implemented 16-18% price increase in Q1 FY27 to pass through gas cost inflation; blended natural gas cost at INR 68/scm
items.quote: Fortunately, we've been able to pass on all the gas price increase until now. So the current price increase has been between 16% and 18%.

items.statement: Demand in May-June was decent; July held up despite rains; management sees mid-single-digit volume growth for FY27
items.quote: Demand is looking good. Let's not forget that in the last 30 months, prices had reduced also by 15%, 16%. So that's been the price increase. So from that point of view, because of that scenario, it's been well accepted in the market. And demand seems to be absolutely good.

items.statement: Standalone capacity utilization improved from 72% in Q1 FY26 to 83% in Q1 FY27; JVs swung from INR 10 crore loss to INR 3 crore profit YoY
items.quote: So if you see same time last quarter, which is Q1 last year, it was 72%. We are at 83%, and that's an 11% increase in -- sorry stand-alone, yes. On a stand-alone basis from 72% capacity utilization to 83%.

items.statement: Morbi exports down 50-60% from peak due to geopolitical/freight issues; expected to continue through Q2 FY27 until freight settles
items.quote: The only negative in the quarter has been from a Morbi perspective is exports has been down due to geopolitical reasons, the export is down a good 50%, 60% from the peak. That's been a little bit of a downer for the quarter, and this would continue probably for this quarter until it starts settling, until the freight starts settling.

items.statement: Project business (currently 7-8% retail, 10-11% government) expected to grow 3-4% as a share of total
items.quote: Our total project was about 7%, 8% in retail and about 10%, 11% in government. This in totality will go up by about 3% to 4%.

items.statement: Working capital days improved from 17 to 12 days; inventory reduced significantly due to Morbi shutdown; receivables and creditor days healthy
items.quote: Our debtor days, inventory days, creditor days are all healthy. Working capital days also have come down from 17 to 12 days.

items.statement: South plant capex funded ~60% internal accruals; balance via JV-level debt with no corporate guarantee from Somany
items.quote: About 60% with internal accruals.

items.statement: Maximum revenue potential at current capacity and prices is ~INR 3,700 crore; balancing equipment may add ~INR 300 crore more by year-end
items.quote: Approximately INR3,700 crores, yes, more or less, give or take, INR50 crores at today's price.

items.statement: Targets top line growth of more than 15% year-on-year, about INR1,350 crores for this financial year.
items.quote: We are targeting a top line growth of more than 15% year-on-year, resulting into about INR1,350 crores for this financial year, maintaining a healthy bottom line.

items.statement: Next year revenue target INR1,600 crores plus/minus INR50 crores.
items.quote: Next year, you're looking at about INR1,600 crores plus/minus INR50 crores.

items.statement: Order intake over next 3-4 years should be at least INR8,000-9,000 crores, executed over 5-6 years.
items.quote: Our order intake over the next 3 to 4 years, I think should be in the region of at least INR8,000 crores to INR9,000 crores to be executed over the next 5 to 6 years.

items.statement: At least INR1,600 crores order inflow expected this year, may improve.
items.quote: M.V.R. confirms that we will see at least INR1,600 crores being added this year. And we may improve that number by the way, over the next few quarters.

items.statement: Total order book stands at INR4,300 crores as on date.
items.quote: So with this major win, our total order book sells to a record-breaking of INR4,300 crores as on date.

items.statement: Stand-alone order book INR2,156 crores; consolidated INR2,849 crores including service orders INR244 crores.
items.value: INR2,156 crores; INR2,849 crores; INR244 crores
items.quote: In terms of the opportunities, our stand-alone order book as of quarter end stands at INR2,156 crores, providing strong visibility for the upcoming period. Around 66% of this order book is from defense and the rest that is 34% is from space, metrology and hydrology sectors. Our consolidated order book stands at INR2,849 crores, which includes service orders of about INR244 crores, which are typica

items.statement: Secured INR2,205 crores order from HAL for Uttam Radar subsystems in July.
items.quote: Staying in the order book, I would like to highlight that in the month of July, we secured a significant order worth about INR2,205 crores from Hindustan Aeronautics Limited for procurement of critical subsystems for Uttam Radar.

items.statement: Expect INR700-800 crores orders from QRSAM for first 3 regiments.
items.quote: So that will leave at least INR700 crores, INR800 crores worth of orders to be added from for QRSAM for the first 3 regiments only, at least for now.

items.statement: Expect INR500-750 crores orders from Astra Rafael Comsys JV.
items.quote: We are looking at least INR500 crores to INR750 crores orders from our Astra Rafael Comsys, our joint venture, and at least INR3,000 crores worth of business coming in from Su-30, Virupaksha as well as Angad.

items.statement: Expect INR100-120 crores orders from BEL for Shatrughat and Samaghat programs.
items.quote: Approximately around INR100 crores to INR120 crores worth of orders we expect for these 2 programs put together.

items.statement: Margins expected similar to last year with positive increase.
items.quote: Definitely, definitely, the margins are going to be similar to last year. You can expect a delta increase on that -- positive increase in that margins.

items.statement: Expect to maintain current margin trajectory, but no commitment due to factors.
items.quote: So that gives us the confidence that we should be able to maintain more or less our current margin trajectory. But we don't want to commit to you on the margins because there are a lot of factors which will come into play from incremental products, number one.

items.statement: Invested in automated process engineering workflows and advanced infrastructure.
items.quote: To support this rapidly growing volume and complexity of work, we have invested steadily in automated process engineering workflows and advanced infrastructure.

items.statement: Stretch supply chains across borders due to global restocking; ensuring supply chains remain intact.
items.quote: So we are beefing up our purchase departments and other departments as the risk, which I also want to highlight is stretch supply chains across the border, across every country because everybody is restocking on their ornaments inventory. So we've got to make sure that our supply chains remain intact and stuff comes in within the defined time lines.

items.statement: No dilution for working capital; equity is expensive.
items.quote: Till we have accretive nonorganic opportunities, we will not dilute for working capital. We are fairly comfortable on that part, which goes on to increase our return on equity, which is already has moved up substantially.

items.statement: Revised FY27 revenue guidance to INR2,200-2,300 crores with EBITDA margin of 10-11% (INR220-230 crores EBITDA)
items.quote: So basically, what we are guiding is INR2,200 crores to INR2,300 crores top line and EBITDA margin in the range of 10% to 11%. So, it will be in that range between INR220 crores, INR230 crores kind of EBITDA.

items.statement: FY28 normalized EBITDA margin target of 12-14%
items.quote: In fiscal '28, I think it's in the region of 12% to 14% is what we can look at.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 4% from 45% in Q4 FY26 due to raw material cost increases
items.quote: You would have seen the details of our financial statements and you would have seen that our margins, which were plus 45% last quarter, has come down to 4%, and that's what has percolated down to our EBITDA for the quarter.

items.statement: Specialty Ingredients EBITDA margin at 6.35% in Q1 FY27, down from normalized 10%+ due to 4-5% gross margin hit from geopolitical issues and 1-2% from liquidity constraints
items.quote: If I had done this 4%, my normalized EBITDA at this moment of time and with all the pressures of putting the material to American markets and other things, I would have done 4% at least more on gross margin, which would have straight flown down to my EBITDA.

items.statement: Aroma segment EBITDA negative INR4-4.5 crores in Q1 FY27 due to low 25% capacity utilization on ethyl vanillin campaign; expects positive EBITDA in Q2 FY27
items.quote: As I said, we were cautiously increasing the ramp-up of ethyl vanillin. And you would have seen that we would have produced how many -- 400 tons only in this quarter, with a capacity of 1,500. So naturally, there was cost of the plant, fixed cost, which cannot be absorbed entirely on the 400.

items.statement: Performance Chemicals EBITDA at 2.5% in Q1 FY27 due to diphenol plant shutdown; expects positive EBITDA in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Naturally, the closure of diphenol plant is weighing down on Performance Chemicals, and that's why we have seen a 2.5% EBITDA there.

items.statement: Vanillin demand picking up; channel stocks cleared; U.S./Europe supply gap of 5,000-6,000 tons identified
items.quote: So basically, the demand is U.S. and Europe where the antidumping duties are. So our focus on these 2 markets. And there seems to be a gap of about 5,000 to 6,000 tons of material, which will have to be imported because the local production capacities are fully occupied at that level.

items.statement: Ethyl vanillin 95% customer approval achieved; 350 tons sold in Q1 FY27; switching to methyl vanillin in Q2 FY27 for better margins
items.quote: We are happy to announce that we have almost -- 95% of our customers have approved our ethyl vanillin. In this quarter, we have already sold 350. If you remember in last quarter, we have said that we are taking the campaign of 750 -odd metric tons of ethyl vanillin.

items.statement: Vanillin production guidance reduced to ~3,000 tons for FY27 from 3,600-4,000 tons due to slower ethyl vanillin ramp-up and 4 campaign changeovers
items.quote: So basically, we had guided for 3,600 to 4,000 and now we are saying 3,000 -- around 3,000. The change is basically in our ethyl vanillin run. The ramp-up we took was slower than what we had anticipated purely because we wanted to get the quality standards to be absolutely undoubtable.

items.statement: Diphenol plant remains shut; evaluating alternative uses; decision by Q3 FY27
items.quote: By third quarter, we will take a decision to either have an alternate use for that or maybe if the situation is right, we may shift back to the diphenol production.

items.statement: May need INR100-200 crores additional credit lines for working capital as revenue scales to INR2,400 crores
items.quote: We will try to use the internal cash, but it looks like as the year progresses, we may have to go and go and take credit lines from the market in the range of INR100 crores to INR200 crores plus.

items.statement: Working capital cycle elongated to ~100 days due to Red Sea shipping rerouting and slower customer collections
items.quote: As you know, with the Hormuz Strait and the Red Sea issues, we have to now ship it across the South Africa, and that has increased the working capital needs. The -- because of the global slowdown also the recovery from the customers have also elongated by a few days and that's weighing down on the working capital cycle.

items.statement: Raw material cost pressures persist in Q2 FY27; expects to pass on ~50% of cost increases in blends
items.quote: No, not fully. But in the blends, some of it upwards, we will be able to pass on. I'm not saying that we'll be able to pass on entirely the cost, but maybe half of the cost we'll be able to pass on.

items.statement: Expects double-digit EBITDA margins by Q3 FY27; Q2 FY27 all three segments positive EBITDA
items.quote: Q3 could be there. Rehan: Q2? Nirmal Momaya: Q3. Rehan: So Q3 would swing back to double-digit? Nirmal Momaya: Yes

items.statement: Ethyl vanillin campaign of 750 tons half completed; methyl vanillin orders in hand for Q2 FY27
items.quote: If you remember in last quarter, we have said that we are taking the campaign of 750 -odd metric tons of ethyl vanillin. Half of that is done. We have produced almost more than 300 metric tons.

items.statement: Expect positive sales growth impact visible from Q2 FY27
items.quote: Difficult to give the number, but we should be positive and that positive impact should be visible from Q2 itself, I believe.

items.statement: Target to reach 70% premium product contribution in next 3-4 years
items.period: next three years to four years
items.quote: Now we have reached to 60-plus percentage already and the target is to reach to 70% in next three years to four years time.

items.statement: Expect Granuvia INR20 cr and Spinoace INR10 cr+ in FY27, combined INR30-35 cr gross
items.quote: I believe Granuvia can touch about INR20 crores in this fiscal and Spinoace can go INR10 crores plus, so both products put together INR30 crores to INR35 crores range is possible in this fiscal, gross level.

items.statement: Kaeros targeting 100% CAGR initially, then 50-60%
items.quote: Kaeros is a new company which we had launched and the target is to grow at a CAGR of 100% initially and then it will come down to 50%-60%.

items.statement: Sotanala total investment ~INR200 cr (INR50 cr formulation, INR150 cr technical), INR70 cr spent so far
items.quote: It will be a project total investment. These total investment will go roughly about INR200 crores, out of which I think about INR50 crores will be going in the formulations and INR150 crores will be for the technical. And the total investment made so far is to the tune of about INR70 crores.

items.statement: Annual capex to normalize to INR30-40 cr maintenance after current projects complete
items.quote: Once the current projects are completed, we expect annual capex to normalize around INR30 crores to INR40 crores of maintenance capex, allowing us to increasingly focus on utilization, cash generation and returns.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 240 bps to 31.6% in Q1 FY27 despite volume decline
items.quote: If we compare the value year-on-year results, the revenue from operations has degrown by 12%, INR691 crores to INR612 crores, and the gross profit has decreased from 202 crores to 193.16 crores by 4% though the gross profit percentage has increased from 29% to 31.6%.

items.statement: Premium product margins: Focus Maharatna 35%+, Maharatna ~30%, Generics 10-15%
items.quote: generally I always tell that FMs are the products which have higher profitability, Maharatna have reas onable profitability, say in between, and generics are sales that are low profitability. If you have the price advantage over any generic, you can make some good profits than the normal, because normally generic end up selling the generic at 10% to 15% gross margins. So, there can be cases where

items.statement: Premium portfolio (Maharatna + Focus Maharatna) at 64% of B2C in Q1 FY27 vs 58% YoY
items.quote: if we see some mix here, then the premium product sales has increased during this quarter. Last year, it was 58% of total B2C contribut ion, this year first quarter it is 64% of the total B2C contribution

items.statement: Monsoon improved in August, reservoir levels up, crops healthy; South India rice sowing 40% pending
items.quote: If we talk about August monsoons, we see good rains across all country, the reservoir situation is improving and the crops are very healthy. The only gap what we see is majorly in the South India where the rice sowing is little delayed in many parts where the dams are not full. But the dam situation is improving now. 40-odd percent of rice is pending remaining are to be sown in Karnataka, Andhra a

items.statement: Sales returns possible but expect to reduce to at least half of prior year's INR200 cr
items.quote: Yes, sales return, possibilities are definitely there, but this year I see only 1 or 2 herbicides failing, not many, number 1. Number 2, we were very, v ery cautious looking at the last year. So, the placements were not that strong what we did in the last year. It was a strategic call what we had taken to place lower, otherwise I could have also achieved the sales number by placing more, but we di

items.statement: Took price hikes in March, April (2), attempted May but rolled back due to weak demand
items.quote: We tried, like, as I told you that there was a big expectation of price hike in the month of March, we had taken one hike in March, two hikes in April, and I believe in May also we tried to take one hike, but somehow we had to roll it back because the market was very much delayed and the sentiment of the network was very weak.

items.statement: Dahej technical plant can add at least INR200 cr production capacity
items.quote: At least INR200 crores is possible to be added into the technical production plant and formulation also is going to support in a good way.

items.statement: Volume degrowth ~13% in Q1 FY27 with ~2% price increase
items.quote: Yes, the volume degrowth is about 13%. There is a small value growth of about 2% actually, which is visible in Q1 results.

items.statement: Sotanala formulation facility expected April-May next year, technical by Diwali
items.quote: The formulation facility at Sotanala is expected to commence around April-May next year, followed by technical products-- production by Diwali, subject to the project schedule.

items.statement: Target to double company size in 4-5 years
items.quote: The idea is to double ourselves. In the past, we used to double in 3 to 4 years. Now I believe that we should be able to double in 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of at least 50% for FY27
items.quote: So I think revenue guidance remains the same. It will be at least 50%.

items.statement: SSSG guidance of 8% to 10% for FY27
items.quote: And the guidance for SSSG has always been 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Store opening target of 170 to 200 stores for FY27
items.quote: Yes, we are on track to open 170 to 200 stores this year.

items.statement: New store capex increased to INR1.2-1.22 crores from INR1.1 crores
items.quote: So earlier, the capex used to be about INR1.1 crores. So I think it is up because of the prices rising, it has moved up to INR1.2 crores, INR1.22 crores.

items.statement: Planning 4-5% price increase from Q3 FY27 to pass on raw material cost inflation
items.quote: So I think we'll start seeing that impact from the third quarter onwards, and it will be an increase of about, I would say, 4% to 5% increase in the overall garment cost, which we'll have to pass on to the consumer.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target to be maintained despite aggressive store expansion
items.quote: And we will try to maintain the EBITDA margins even after opening so much new area.

items.statement: Demand in July-August in line with expectations; festive season in Q3 will determine full year
items.quote: July and August are at par with how we see demand and how we forecast the demand. But again, it will completely depend on the October, November period that will have the bulk of the sales.

items.statement: Consumer demand considered inelastic due to necessity-driven categories like kids wear (25% of sales)
items.quote: We think we are selling necessity to the consumers. And for example, kids wear is 25% of our sales. So you have to buy new clothes for your kids every year.

items.statement: Internal accruals and vendor prepayment reversal (INR150-200 crores) sufficient for expansion; no QIP needed
items.quote: No, I think the internal accruals will be enough. And currently, we are using a lot of our cash in prepaying our vendors. So once we want to use that money for expansion plans, we just get the creditor days back to normal. So I think that releases almost INR150 crores to INR200 crores of capital plus the EBITDA we'll generate this year.

items.statement: Inventory target of 90-100 days and creditor cycle of 45-50 days
items.quote: We are looking to target inventory of 90 to 100 days and creditor cycle of 45 to 50 days.

items.statement: Full price sales at 90% in Q1 FY27 vs 92% last year due to Adhik Maas and fewer wedding dates
items.quote: So there was a 30-day period of Adhik Maas in quarter 1. And I think because of that, we saw our full price sales go down from 92% to 90%.

items.statement: New stores operating at INR730-740 per sq ft vs mature stores at INR1,070-1,100 per sq ft
items.quote: But it's at a very respectable level, all the new stores that we have opened, they are already operating more than INR730, INR740 per square feet of sale.

items.statement: Repeat customer rate within first year improved from 40% to 55% over last 3 years
items.quote: So in fact, in the last 3 years, people who came back to us within the first year has moved up from 40% to almost 55%.

items.statement: Lease terms: 9-11 years with 12-15% escalation every 3 years; mostly standalone stores
items.quote: The average lease period ranges anywhere between 9 to 11 years, and the escalation ranges anywhere from 12% to 15% every 3 years. So that's the standard lease format.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 16% to 18% by year-end FY27
items.quote: On our EBITDA margins, I should say that even if things go along the way they are, we should be reaching closer to about at least between 16% to 18% by the year-end.

items.statement: PM3 major rebuild underway, commissioning within a month; major capex program completed
items.quote: Further, Paper Machine 3 has been shut for the time being for a major rebuild, which will lead to enhanced production capabilities and improved quality in the final product.

items.statement: Peak debt estimated at INR 760-770 crores; repayment of INR 170-175 crores annually for next 2-3 years to reach under INR 300 crores
items.quote: Peak debt, we are currently looking at about INR760 crores or INR770 crores maximum. And we have repayments of about INR170 crores, INR175 crores for the next 2 to 3 years. And by the next 3 years, we will be at very, very manageable levels of debt under INR300 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 13.2%; cost increase of INR 4,200/ton offset NSR gain of INR 3,400/ton QoQ
items.quote: As a result, EBITDA stood at INR40 crores, broadly stable year -on-year basis with EBITDA margin at 13.2%.

items.statement: NSR increased ~INR 3,400/ton QoQ but cost rose ~INR 4,200/ton due to West Asia conflict impacting fuel, chemicals, freight
items.value: INR 3,400/ton NSR gain vs INR 4,200/ton cost increase
items.quote: However, the improvement in blended NSR by approximately INR3,400 per ton was more than offset by an increase in cost of around INR4,200 per ton on a quarter-to-quarter basis. Driven by higher raw material, chemical and fuel prices amid the ongoing West Asia conflict.

items.statement: Target NSR of INR 72,000-75,000/ton in next 4-6 months from current INR 68,000-69,000/ton
items.quote: Currently, we are at about INR68,000, INR69,000 per ton level. Ideally, going forward, sensing of how the market is growing and the kind of positivity that -- positive sentiment that we are getting, our price increase is likely to touch and reach about INR72,000 to INR75,000 level in the next 4, 6 months.

items.statement: Healthy demand in Q1 FY27 supported by education, publishing, office consumption; expect demand to remain supportive
items.quote: The paper industry saw a healthy demand suppo rted by education, publishing, office consumption and broader economic activity in the first quarter of the financial year 2027.

items.statement: Specialty paper contribution currently ~18-19% of revenue; targeting 30% with OGR paper launch and specialty grade focus
items.quote: Right now, our contribution from specialty paper is just under 20%. It's about 18%, 19%, but we will surely be making our efforts to reach that level of 30%.

items.statement: West Asia conflict driving raw material, chemical, fuel cost volatility; local wheat straw prices elevated but cooling; import competition diminishing due to shipping costs
items.quote: However, the West Asia conflict intensified cost pressures, particularly across fuel, chemicals and other raw materials, while also affe cting freight and logistics cost. This created a challenging margin environment for paper manufacturers even as demand conditions improved.

items.statement: Commissioned DDS Double Displacement Digester System for wood pulping; installed Folio Ream Wrapping Machine; produced OGR paper on PM2
items.quote: We successfully commissioned the DDS Double Displacement Digester System for wood pulping, which will help optimize pulp quality and yield while reducing utility chemical and overall pulp costs.

items.statement: Pulp capacity to increase to 410-415 TPD from 365 TPD; clonal sapling production at 17.28 lakh/quarter; added 1,300 acres social farm forestry (total ~19,650 acres)
items.quote: So pulp capacity should -- will increase to about 410, 415 tons per day, and that's all that we will require to produce the relevant quantities of paper.

items.statement: AI integration in manufacturing targeted for completion by March 2028; targeting 4-5% cost reduction
items.quote: We could target between 4% to 5% additions in -- or reductions in costs.

items.statement: Antidumping and anti-subsidy duty applications filed for writing/printing paper (40-140 GSM); government reviewing
items.quote: We have already done that. We are already in close coordination with the government, where our applications for antidumping duty and anti -subsidy duty has already been filed, and it is being keenly being looked at by the government.

items.statement: Wheat straw prices cooling; reduction seen in Q2 vs Q1; further decline expected post-September with alternate fodder availability
items.quote: We are seeing a reduction in wheat straw procurement prices for ourselves in Q2 versus Q1.

items.statement: With the capacity being completed in Q3, revenue should reach INR7,000 crores to INR7,500 crores in a normal market.
items.quote: Sir, with the given capacity probably which is getting completed in Q3 of this year, you can say end of the calendar year December 2026, with the given capacity it should reach INR7,000 crores to INR7,500 crores in a normal market.

items.statement: Overall project outlay revised from around INR1,000 crores to INR1,112 crores; balance INR35 crores to INR40 crores to be completed by end of 2026.
items.quote: We have already invested INR1,076 crores, mostly through internal accruals, while the overall project outlay has been revised from around INR1,000 crores to INR1,112 crores, primarily due to technical upgrades, additional ancillaries, some inflation, and some time overruns also. The balance of around INR35 crores to INR40 crores is expected to be completed by the end of this current year 2026.

items.statement: DI pipe order book is around four months based on current dispatch position.
items.quote: Madam, as per the current dispatch position, it is the equivalent of say , the current capacity utilization, it is around four months' order book.
