items.statement: Hello Park indoor centers require INR 8-12 crores capex per center (8,000-12,000 sq ft)
items.quote: The capital investment per center is expected to be INR8 to INR12 crores, making it an efficient capitalized fast-growth format.

items.statement: Outdoor park capex ranges INR 200-500 crores per park depending on location and scale
items.quote: Per park it can vary between INR200 crores to INR450 crores to INR500 odd crores based on which location and size and scale of the park we go for.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 170 bps to 50.7% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA grew 24% ye ar-on-year to INR90 crores, while EBITDA margin expanded by 170 basis points to 50.7

items.statement: Hello Park indoor centers target 24-25% EBITDA margins after rental costs
items.quote: The EBITDA margins as you observe rightly because these will be inside malls, the margins would be not as similar to the water parks or the parks that we operate. It would be around 24%-25% margins, if we account for the rentals to the malls as well.

items.statement: Consciously adopted softer ticket pricing in Q1 FY27 to drive footfall; headroom for price hikes in next 3 quarters
items.quote: We consciously had opted for a slightly softer pricing strategy with regards to ticketing vertical. However, we think that over the next three quarters we have headroom there and we will make appropriate corrections.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 20% YoY to INR 178 crores; footfalls up 22% to 11.5 lakhs despite heatwave and school calendar shifts
items.quote: FY27 began on a strong note with revenue growing 20% Y-o-Y to INR178 crores and footfalls increasing by 22%.

items.statement: ARPU stable at ~INR 1,395; non-ticket revenue focus via dwell time, IP events, Magic Pass program
items.quote: ARPU has remained largely stable at around INR1,395. The strong growth in visitor volumes more than compensated, thus demonstrating the continued demand for our offerings while maintaining pricing discipline.

items.statement: Two Hello Park locations signed: Hyderabad (Lake Shore Y Junction Mall) and Surat (Phoenix Mall); target 2-3 centers per year
items.quote: We are on track to launch our first Hello Park in Hyderabad later this year at Lake Shore Y Junction Mall, and we have also finalized a second location at Phoenix Mall, Surat. We will share more details about these developments as we progress forward. Further, we aim to add two to three Hello Park centers every

items.statement: Debt/EBITDA to be maintained at 2.5-3x average, max 3-3.5x for limited periods
items.quote: the debt to EBITDA of the company we have been clear in this regard that that will be kept in a certain range and at best i t could be 3 to 3.5x for a limited period, but the average debt to EBITDA would be in the range of around 2.5 to

items.statement: Spiritual tourism expansion (Ujjain, Varanasi, Vrindavan) requires government support; active talks ongoing, 1-2 locations in 2-3 years
items.quote: We are in active talks with them and we foresee at least one or two locations in the next two to three years that should come through.

items.statement: Promoter warrants (conversion price INR 73.5) to be converted before deadline; promoters positive on business
items.quote: From the promoter group, we are very positive on the business and overall long-term prospects of it. So, the conversion will happen before the given date and requirement which is there.

items.statement: Novotel Imagicaa occupancy 62%, ARR INR 9,657 in Q1 FY27; revenue stable despite occupancy moderation
items.quote: The occupancy stood at 62% during the quarter, while the average room rates improved marginally to INR9,657. The revenue remained largely stable, despite a slight moderation in occupancy.

items.statement: Gujarat catchment footfalls up 32%, revenue up 15%; ARPU drop due to price elasticity testing and promotional initiatives
items.quote: The Gujarat catchment also continued to perform well, with footfalls increasing by 32% and revenue growing by 15%. While ARPU was tad lower on a year-on-year basis, this was primarily driven by a change in the visitor mix and a few promotional initiatives aimed at driving higher volumes.

items.statement: Gas trading business profit guidance maintained at around INR1,100 crores.
items.quote: I think we stick to our guidance last time we gave around INR1,100 crores of profit from the gas trading business. That still remains.

items.statement: Gas trading margin guidance of 4% to 5% maintained.
items.quote: I think what we have told as a guidance earlier also, basically, we make a margin of close to 4% to 5% in the gas trading business. Yes, there will be exceptional quarters, which would be there, but we stick to that guidance again.

items.statement: CGD EBITDA margin guidance of 5.5 to 6.5 Rs/scm maintained.
items.quote: We have given a guidance of 5.5 to 6.5 Rs/scm.We'll still stick to that guidance.

items.statement: CGD segment capex guidance of close to INR1,000 crores maintained.
items.quote: There is no capex on the gas trading segment, but there will be capex on the CGD segment, which practically we are giving a guidance of close to INR1,000 crores. We still stick with that.

items.statement: Plans to set up own propane import and storage facilities near Morbi market.
items.quote: Yes, we have plans to have our own propane import facility. We have basically shortlisted a few sites in Gujarat where we can put up our own terminal.

items.statement: Expects to sustain CNG growth of around 12-13% for next couple of years with more stations.
items.quote: I think we have been growing at close to 12 percentage, and this growth has continued and this quarter growing at 13 percentage now. Basically, we are expecting that. And as the MD told that we are going to add on more stations now. So we'll be able to sustain that growth for the next couple of years.

items.statement: Expects non-Morbi industrial volumes to reach at least 3 mmscmd in 1.5 to 2 years.
items.quote: As we expect LNG prices to become stable maybe in a year from now, we expect these volumes to be at least 3 mmscmd by 1.5 years to 2 years from now.

items.statement: Expects to do close to 3 mmscmd of gas in Morbi this quarter.
items.quote: Gas prices would be at a premium to propane. And our expectation is that we'll continue to do close to 3 mmscmd of gas at least in this quarter.

items.statement: Expects long-term third-party volumes of 4.5 to 5 mmscmd.
items.quote: Yes. I think it should be in that range, 4.5 million to 5 million.

items.statement: Expects to do at least 4 million tons LNG on term contract basis in 2030.
items.quote: So basically, as of today, around 28% would be like 2 million ton LNG equivalent on term contract basis. We expect to do close to at least 4 million tons in 2030.

items.statement: Morbi gas price is close to Rs 78/scm and propane close to Rs 65/scm.
items.quote: Ours is close to 78 Rs/scm and propane is close to 65 Rs/scm.

items.statement: Non-Morbi industrial gas price close to INR70 in Q1.
items.quote: It close to INR70 for the non-Morbi segment.

items.statement: Sourcing mix: 20% long term, 12.5% domestic gas, rest spot.
items.quote: Long term is 20%, domestic gas is 12.5%, and rest is spot, close to 67%. Out of these long terms, almost 20% is Henry Hub.

items.statement: Morbi volumes may bottom at 1.8 to 2 mmscmd due to lack of propane infrastructure.
items.quote: I think so. I think 1.8 million to 2 million would be a fair number to assume because in the past it had reduced to 1.8 mmscmd, around that number.

items.statement: Cash of around INR7,200 crores; concrete deployment plan by Q3.
items.quote: Yes, we have cash of around INR7,200 crores, so we have a capex plan of around INR1,000 crores for the CGD business. And with respect to the rest of the cash to be utilized, basically, we are working on certain programs with respect to the strengthening of the present business with respect to the CNG and the pipelines.

items.statement: GSPL transmission listing expected towards early September.
items.quote: We expect this towards early September.

items.statement: Blended revenue growth of 30-35% for next 3 years from new brands, vintage business, and capacity expansion
items.quote: So a blended growth of somewhere around 35% to 30% for the next 3 years is kind of on the charts and it's going to be a combination of all the new brands and our existing ones, plus the increase in the capacities that we are building currently at our own facility.

items.statement: GX domestic business expected to grow 30-35% annually for next 4 years from small base
items.quote: But for the next 4 years, we can easily consider around 30% to 35% growth on the GX line as well.

items.statement: Capex of INR30-40 crores planned for FY27 and similar for FY28, targeting INR35-45 crores per year for next 2 years
items.quote: We have a plan of about INR30 crores to INR40 crores of CapEx in this financial year from now. From onwards, maybe the same plan for the next year as well, about INR30 crores to INR40 crores.

items.statement: Revenue target for FY27 around INR800 crores, on track to overachieve; INR1,000 crores not committed
items.quote: This year, our target was somewhere around INR800 crores. I think we are in line to achieve that. We will cross that hopefully. INR1,000 crores, I do not want to comment.

items.statement: Pet care 45-55% gross margin, mobility 40-50%, nutrition 35-50%, dermaceutics 70-75%; margin expansion expected over 8-11 quarters as high-margin products scale
items.quote: Pet care works at around 45% to 55%. Mobility works at around 40% to 50%. Nutrition has a higher intrinsic margin, but right now, we are expansion. So we are looking at around 35% to 45%, maybe even 45% to 50%. Dermaceutics has a gross margin of 70% to 75%.

items.statement: Pet care targeting 40-50% growth for next 3-4 years from INR40-45 crore base; cat food launch by Q3/Q4 FY27, diagnostics and OEM to add revenue
items.quote: So overall, we are looking, again, at 40% to 50% growth in those numbers for the next 3, 4 years. We have a very small base of INR40 crores, INR45 crores overall with this.

items.statement: Inventory days targeted at 135-140 currently, aiming for 120 days within 4 quarters, long-term range 110-125 days due to SKU count
items.quote: We are looking at around 140, 135 days of inventory. Hopefully, within the next 4 quarters, it will come to around 120 days. It will always hover between 110 to 125 days because of the nature of the business and the number of SKUs that we have.

items.statement: Working capital at INR170-175 crores with 50% as cash; absolute working capital will rise with revenue but comfortable with internal cash flows
items.quote: We have a working capital of somewhere around INR170 crores, INR175 crores, which is not a high working capital for a company our size. We also have a lot of debtors. We have a good stock, and we have almost 50% of our working capital as cash on hand.

items.statement: Functional foods adding 42 variants; Jain variant performing well in pockets; cat biscuits launching in 6-7 months; Wagr pet platform beta live, full launch in 60-90 days
items.quote: We are also coming up with cat biscuits. I think we will be the second or the third one to have cat biscuit treats coming in, in the country. So that is also coming in, and we are creating a functional line even for the cats in the coming 6 to 7 months.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue expected INR 11,000-13,000 crores, EPS INR 8.75-9.5 per share
items.quote: So far as our F Y27 outlook is concerned, our company expects F Y27 consolidated revenue to be in the range of INR 11,000 crores to INR 13,000 crores, that is growth of around 35% and above and also expects the FY27 EPS to be in the range of INR8.75 to INR9.5 per share, which is based on the proposed post corporate action face value of INR10 per share.

items.statement: Cost base front-loaded investing in AI infrastructure, international expansion, financial services
items.quote: Our cost base remains front -loaded as we invest in AI infrastructure, international expansion and our new financial services capabilities.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guardrail set at ~15% of gross revenue; Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 68% of net revenue
items.quote: The guardrails that you can establish is about 15%. That's like a guardrail, if you ask me. We always want to have guardrails, which is we never want to go below that certain amount rather than going into how much EBITDA we can improve and so on and so for th, we want to set up certain guardrails that enable us to ensure that we continue reinvesting into our future and maintain certain profitabili

items.statement: Transaction processing volume grew 74% YoY to INR 1,479 billion in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our transaction processing volume for the quarter grew 74% year -on-year to INR 1,479 billion with continued strength across utility payments, government payments, retail, B2B and hospitality.

items.statement: RediffPay exiting CUG this month into production; RediffOne expanding into commerce, compliance, intelligence
items.quote: RediffPay is progressing well as our UPI -based consumer payments platform. It will be out of CUG this month and into production. RediffOne is evolving into an operating platform for businesses bringing together commerce, communication, compliance and intel ligence.

items.statement: UPI MDR monetization expected on large merchants/high-value transactions; 22% of transactions on UPI
items.quote: Today, almost 22% of our transactions are on UPI. So any kind of monetization on that UPI will add additional revenues definitely to our platform. Right now, as we stand, the act has been passed by the Lok Sabha. It still awaits Rajya Sabha and still awaits President's approval and then the gazette and then we will know what kind of pricing and monetization that NPCI and RBI is allowing to be done

items.statement: Enterprise AI demand for on-prem SLMs ($1-10B params) for data sovereignty; revenue impact expected in 9-18 months
items.quote: In terms of impact to our business is concerned, I think it's about anywhere from 9 to 18 months out, where you'll have -- you'll start seeing some good impact, we believe.

items.statement: Net revenue declined 3% YoY due to take-rate compression and competitive payments; core profitability focus with reinvestment
items.quote: Yes, typically, first quarter is a slightly low quarter. Second, third quarter is slightly better because of festival season than others. And we believe that as more and more transactions happen through our platform, we have slightly compression as far as our margins are concerned. If you look at our take rates, they have compressed slightly and that has impacted our net revenue.

items.statement: Strategic investments up to 2.5% in RatnaFin Capital NBFC and up to 7% in Online PSB Loans platform
items.quote: We have progressed well in proposed investments of up to 2.5% in RatnaFin Capital, which is an RBI registered NBFC with a very strong SME lending franchisee. We also approved a strategic investment of up to 7% in online PSB loans, India's largest public sector-backed digital credit platform.

items.statement: Neuromind AI subsidiary merging into AvenuesAI; share face value reverse split from INR 1 to INR 10
items.quote: First, Nueromind, which is our fully owned AI-based subsidiary is being merged into AvenuesAI. This will give us synergies and seamless operations and lead to cost benefits and data consent also. The second we are doing is a reverse split, which is a face value of share, which was INR1 now is being increased to INR 10 per share.

items.statement: UAE Central Bank in-principle approval for Retail Payment Services Cat III license; RBI authorization for PPI issuance
items.quote: We received in-principle approval from Central Bank of UAE for Retail Payment Services, which is a Cat III license for Avenues. UAE is already one of our strongest international markets. The license will allow us to broaden our customer reach and product suite and strengthen our long-term international payment strategy. In India, RBI authorized AvenuesAI to set up payment system for issuance and o

items.statement: PayCentral agentic payment platform launched on Google Agent Payments Protocol; early commercial traction
items.quote: Through Phronetic AI, we launched PayCentral, which we believe is India's first agentic payment platform built on Google's Agent Payments Protocol. It enables AI agents to transact directly with one another without requiring a person to manually initiate every payment.

items.statement: AI infrastructure strategy avoids large data center capex; focuses on SLMs, transaction intelligence scores, application layers
items.quote: We may invest selectively in smaller capacities, but not the large ones. So that's one. As far as the -- we've recently, in our release, mentioned that we want to build out transaction intelligence score and think of it as, in some ways, alternative risk score.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of INR 2,000 crores maintained with growth weighted to second half
items.quote: Based on current customer discussions, our receipt order visibility, expected capacity ramp-up and planned utilization levels, we remain confident of achieving our previously stated consolidating revenue guidance of INR 2,000 crores for FY27.

items.statement: Garment division EBITDA margin guided above 15% for full year including Sri Lanka
items.quote: See, with respect to margins, we have already guided for a consolidated like garment division that is between Young Brand and S.P. Apparels put together, we will be anywhere above 15% for the whole year. Even including Sri Lanka business, we should be 15% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Standalone adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 17.5% in Q1 FY27 from 15.2% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA margins improved to 17.5% compared to 15.2% Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 15.3% in Q1 FY27 from 13.1% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA for Q1 FY27 stood at INR 61.4 crores compared to INR 52.9 crores in Q1 FY26, reflecting a growth of 15.9% year-on-year. EBITDA margin improved 15.3% compared to 13.1% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Young Brand adding luxury bra products as value-added line; customers encouraging expansion into molded bras
items.quote: Young Brand being in intimate wear, we do a lot of underwear, which is the bottoms for the existing customers. And it's a value add in terms of doing the luxury products. And all the customers have been encouraging and pushing Young Brand for a while to do those value-add products.

items.statement: Consolidated interest cost FY27 guided INR 30-35 crores excluding exchange loss; Q1 higher due to INR 1.75 crore exchange volatility hit
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, we should be anywhere between INR30 crores to INR35 crores. Bhavin Chheda: For the full year? V. Balaji: Yes, for the full year. Yes, correct. Without the exchange loss

items.statement: Board approved INR 3 per share dividend and stock split from INR 10 to INR 2 face value
items.quote: I'm pleased to inform our shareholders that the Board has approved a dividend of INR 3 per share for the year and has also proposed a stock split of the company's equity shares from a face value of INR 10 per share to INR 2 per share, subject to the necessary approval.

items.statement: Revenue visibility strong for next 3-5 years in smart metering and 12-18 months in C&I with high double-digit growth expected
items.quote: If you look at smart metering they have a you know a a strong visibility. If you look at this year Next year, the next 3 to 5 years seem to be a strong visibility.

items.statement: Order book stands at 3,200 crores as of 7th August 2026 with metering and systems accounting for more than 96% of total orders
items.quote: Our order book stands at 3,200 CRS as on 7th August 26 with metering and systems accounting for more than 96% of the total orders.

items.statement: EBITDA margins moderated to 12.26% in Q1 FY27 due to input cost volatility and changing revenue mix; pricing actions initiated to progressively improve margin quality
items.quote: On profitability, EBITDA grew during the quarter although EBITDA margins moderated to 12.26%.

items.statement: Price increases being passed on in wire and cable and lighting; design changes and alternative materials being pursued in smart metering to offset cost inflation
items.quote: Plus the prices are the price increases are also getting passed on to the consumer. So like we've just had couple of increases in the wire and cable.

items.statement: C&I demand diversified across builders, industrial OEMs, solar, telecom, retail and institutional customers; wire and cable volumes up 1.5-2x year-on-year
items.quote: Demand remains diversified across builders, industrial OEMs, solar, telecom, retail and institutional customers.

items.statement: Capex mainly maintenance for metering; automation investments ongoing with 7-8 new machines commissioned including MCB automation; ROI 3-4 years
items.quote: Right now I think from a metering perspective it is going to be more on the maintenance part because we have the capacities now.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflicts driving metal and industrial plastic cost volatility; minimum wages in Haryana up 40% in May adding to manpower cost
items.quote: This reflected an input cost volatility volatility particularly across metals and industrial plastics due to the geographical disruptions.

items.statement: Smart metering 2.0 replacement cycle and export opportunities (Middle East utility approval) seen as long-term growth vectors beyond current order book
items.quote: We are also in export we are also looking at certifications. In fact you just mentioned Middle East one of the the utilities in Middle East has just approved our metering.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target is double-digit, dependent on geopolitical situation and overseas demand
items.quote: See consol business, we are trying to achieve double-digit EBITDA margin, and it all depends on how the geopolitical situation stand and overseas demand stand with us.

items.statement: Mag carbon brick and casting flux new lines can add INR150-200 crores revenue at peak capacity
items.quote: What I said that in past, we have spoken about the addition of two new product lines, mag carbon brick and casting flux, we can add around INR150 crores to INR200 crores on account of these two new product lines at the peak level.

items.statement: Hofmann Ceramic order book maintained at similar levels to corresponding periods
items.quote: At Hofmann Ceramic, we have been able to maintain order book at similar levels compared to corresponding periods.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA declined 17% YoY to INR31 crores due to higher raw material and LPG costs
items.quote: EBITDA for the standalone business stood at INR31 crores in the current quarter, a decline of 17% year-on-year.

items.statement: Price increases implemented across customers and products but time lag in passing on cost increases; benefits expected progressively over coming quarters
items.quote: To mitigate these pressures, we have implemented appropriate price increase across customers and product categories. However, given the nature of our business, there is typically a time lag in passing on cost increases with some of the elevated costs being absorbed in near term.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties, supply chain disruptions, elevated LPG costs, and British Steel blast furnace issues impacted Q1; Liberty Steel dues unlikely to be recovered
items.quote: We faced multiple challenges in FY26, including geopolitical uncertainties, supply chain disruptions, delays in capex spending and rising input costs.

items.statement: Hofmann Ceramic targeting breakeven by end of FY27; Monocon UK moving towards breakeven; Sheffield Refractories expected to normalize in Q2 with British Steel blast furnace restart
items.quote: Turning around the business remains a key priority, and we are taking multiple measures to improve performance with the objective of reducing losses and achieving breakeven by the end of financial year '27.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 11% to 13% and EBITDA margin target of 11.5% to 12.5% for FY27
items.value: 11% to 13% revenue growth; 11.5% to 12.5% EBITDA margin
items.quote: So, for the revenue growth, it would be somewhere between 11% to 13%. That is the kind of growth we are looking forward to during this fiscal. And at EBITDA level, it would be somewhere between 11.5% to 12.5%.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit volume growth for FY27, aiming to close the fiscal with 11% to 12% overall growth
items.quote: So, that is our internal target as well. So, we are very hopeful and aggressive towards the fact that in the next three quarters coming ahead, we will be, overall at a company level, we will close this particular fiscal with a double-digit growth, which will be a combination of volume plus value growth. And so, this year, we are targeting to grow at around 11% to 12%.

items.statement: Implemented 4% to 5% price hike in Q1 FY27; no further price hikes planned as yarn and cotton prices have stabilized
items.quote: So, till date, we have taken just 4% to 5% of price hike. And no other price hike is in picture right now. And the yarn prices and the cotton market is also stagnant, and they are stabilized right now. So, we don't see any reason why we should need to have a price hike again.

items.statement: Quick commerce channel grew 59.4% value and 15.1% volume YoY, contribution increased to 5% of revenue in Q1 FY27 from 3.1% in Q1 FY26
items.value: 59.4% value growth; 15.1% volume growth; 5% revenue contribution
items.quote: The quick commerce channel sustained its strong growth trajectory, recording 59.4% value growth and 15.1% volume growth year-on-year, with its contribution to revenue increasing to 5% in Q1 FY '27 from 3.1% in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: No major capital expenditure commitment in near term; focus on improving free cash flow generation and reducing debt
items.quote: Given that we have no major capital expenditure commitment in the near term, our capital allocation strategy remains clear. We stay focused on improving free cash flow generation and reducing debt.

items.statement: Thermal season booking conferences in July show good traction for upcoming season
items.quote: The conferences that we do in the month of July, pan-India basis and the booking that we got for the thermals is really, it shows the trajectory for this year as well.

items.statement: Export business grew 16.2% value and 15.5% volume YoY to INR 19 crore across 15 countries; contribution increased to 4.9% from 4.2%
items.value: INR 19 crore; 16.2% value growth; 15.5% volume growth; 4.9% contribution
items.quote: Our export business also continued to perform well, recording 16.2% value growth and 15.5% volume growth year-on-year, with its contribution increasing to 4.9% in Q1 FY '27 from 4.2% in Q1 FY '26. During the quarter, we generated export revenue of INR 19 crore across 15 countries and will continue to focus on expanding our international footprint.

items.statement: Internal business plans pegged at 25% growth; external stakeholders modeling at around 20%
items.quote: When we execute all our business plans, internally they are pegged at 25% growth and we are convinced and seeing the right kind of momentum on the ground to realistically peg ourselves internally on that.

items.statement: Combined entity expected to deliver at least 20% growth and be accretive on bottom line after larger M&A
items.quote: I would only sign on the dotted line and invest if I am convinced that under the Affle leadership, the existing business as well as the new inorganic acquisition would continue to deliver combined at least 20% growth and will deliver a meaningful bottom-line performance.

items.statement: Aim to close larger M&A by early 2027; targets to accelerate Developed Markets expansion
items.quote: We aim to close the larger M&A by early 2027 and the identified targets shall accelerate our expansion across Developed Markets by providing deeper and differentiated access to customers and verticals.

items.statement: Expect better margin expansion within this financial year, especially in Developed Markets
items.quote: I believe you will see that within this financial year, we will see better margin expansion, especially in Developed Markets.

items.statement: EBITDA margins stable at 22.4% in Q1 FY2027, up from 22.3% sequentially
items.quote: Our EBITDA margins also improved from 22.3% to 22.4% q-o-q.

items.statement: 95% of revenues grew over 25% y-o-y on adjusted basis, excluding RMG and FinTech headwinds
items.quote: On an adjusted basis, 95% of our revenues have actually seen over 25% growth y-o-y.

items.statement: Encouraged by demand environment across key markets for upcoming festive quarter
items.quote: As we look ahead to the upcoming festive quarter, we remain encouraged by the demand environment across our key markets.

items.statement: Direct advertiser revenue contribution at 79% in Q1 FY2027 vs 74% in FY2026; 100% of business has direct advertiser technology integration
items.quote: What is most important for us is that whether the advertiser is having a billing relationship with us directly or through its agency, it must have a direct Affle 3i Limited August 10, 2026 21 technology integration with us

items.statement: Category E and F robust across board; Category G (RMG) in recovery; Category H (healthcare, hospitality) doing well in India/EM; Developed Markets led by E and G
items.quote: Overall, in categories E, F, G and H, I would say you can order it as category E, F, H and G in terms of qualitative ranking on how we are doing in India and Emerging Markets.

items.statement: Activating over 100,000 mobile apps to reach over 500 million connected devices in Developed Markets this year via AdColony assets
items.quote: We aim to unlock significant competitive advantage by activating over 100,000 mobile apps to reach over 500 million connected devices in Developed Markets this year.

items.statement: Bobble investment (INR 136 crore) under insolvency; impairment testing pending NCLT appeal outcome; decisive step expected in next few quarters
items.quote: We will be very prudent. We will take a decisive step in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Raised appropriate funding to prepare for larger M&A; third-party due diligence advisors appointed
items.quote: We have also raised the appropriate amount of funding to get ourselves ready for that. We have given you a consistent timeline that now we have third-party due diligence partners working on it.

items.statement: OCF to PAT ratio expected to normalize to 80-85% by Q3 FY2027 after 110% in FY2026 due to upfront cash collection in March
items.quote: You will see about 80%-85% OCF to PAT ratio by Q3.

items.statement: Currency impact stable this quarter; 72% business from Emerging Markets/India with cross-currency ROI adjustments; 20% US dollar-to-dollar
items.quote: This quarter had a stable USD to various currencies, not only INR. So we didn't see any additional impact what we had in Q4 or Q3.

items.statement: No impact from slowing smartphone adoption; consumer time spent on digital content increasing across markets
items.quote: No, we are not seeing any impact. I believe what we are seeing instead is a lot more time that the consumers are spending on their devices.

items.statement: Developed Markets growth expected at 20%+ consistently; US is largest focus area both organically and inorganically
items.quote: We see that we will be growing at least at 20%+ in Developed Markets consistently.

items.statement: INR3,000 crore revenue target by 2030 remains the endeavor
items.quote: The INR3,000 crore target continues to be our endeavor and we will update you on that progress.

items.statement: Bharat Seats revenue target of INR3,500 crore by 2030
items.quote: That should be about INR3,500 crore for Bharat Seats by 2030.

items.statement: Order book of INR650 crore to ramp incrementally till 2030
items.quote: So, the INR650 crore order book should come incrementally till 2030.

items.statement: Order book dominated by seat frames and covers; new products include seat insert, latch, seatbelt reminder, ambient lighting
items.quote: Most of the products are from the seat frames and the seat covers. In addition to that, we are also going to set up a plant for seat insert, so that is going to be there. There is going to be seat latch and there is going to be a new plant for seatbelt reminder system. In addition to that, there are some new ambient lighting orders that we have received, but that is a smaller part of the order boo

items.quote: If you talk about the debt, our company is actually debt-free. We have only taken exposure of debt in acquisition of Netcom, and their effective cost of around 9%.

items.statement: 12 live ResolX deployments across 7 enterprise clients in insurance, aviation, banking, automotive and digital assets with 30-40% human deflection
items.quote: We've already deployed this. We have 12 live engagements which are going on across six enterprise clients. The overall deflection or absorption to human is close to about 30-40% depending upon the use case where we've deployed this.

items.statement: AI revenue contribution expected to become sizable in 12-18 months; ResolX launched in May 2026 with 6-7 projects live
items.quote: We should be able to see a good amount of revenue showing up in a horizon for about 12-18 months or probably even slightly more.

items.statement: ResolX platform evolving into full CX platform over 12-24 months targeting 60-70% agentic automation with human-in-the-loop for 20-30%
items.quote: Eventually, what we envision to do is build this as an entire CX platform, which means right from the time of creating a requisition to onboard something, screening of that particular candidate, onboarding of that candidate, training that candidate, assess ment of that candidate, servicing of that using human in the loop, generating insights, doing quality monitoring, doing exception management, a

items.statement: ESOP issued at current market price with 1-year vesting post L5 level; zero cost to company
items.quote: We are issuing ESOP at the current market price, not at a discount. If you talk about the costing part, then cost to company is zero.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance of 25% for FY27 based on new plant ramp-ups and auto sector growth
items.quote: The 25% is our definitely our internal targets. We have invested in two plants at Tirupati and Odisha which are ramping up and also some brownfield expansions and also the growth of our existing customers. So everything put together we definitely believe that yes we should be able to achieve the 25% growth

items.statement: EBITDA per kg guidance maintained at INR12 on sustainable basis despite current INR12.40
items.quote: While internally we do target increase in this EBITDA margin but for the guidance to the street we are maintaining INR12 as the EBITDA margin on a sustainable basis.

items.statement: Invested INR53 crores in Q1 FY27 for greenfield projects at Shoolagiri and Bawal
items.quote: During the quarter we invested Rs. 53 crores in greenfield projects at Shoolagiri and Bawal, while also advancing brownfield projects and technology led initiatives at Tirupati and other locations.

items.statement: Installed recycling capacity expected to exceed 7 lakh tons per annum by end of FY27
items.quote: These projects are progressing as planned and are expected to take our installed recycling capacity beyond 7 lakh tons per annum by the end of FY27

items.statement: Hindalco Odisha plant at 48,000 tons per annum ramping up, produced 6,000 tons in Q1
items.quote: With Hindalco we have put up a plant in Odisha with a capacity of 48,000 tons per annum. That plant is ramping up as I had explained in my earlier talk that now this quarter the production has gone to about 6,000 tons for the three months.

items.statement: EBITDA per kg improved to INR12.40 in Q1 FY27 from INR12.00 in FY26
items.quote: And the EBITDA with all this improved slightly to INR12.40 per kg or INR12,400 per ton.

items.statement: Aluminium prices are pass-through; EBITDA per ton is better metric than percentage margins
items.quote: Since aluminium prices are largely a pass through in nature, we believe that EBITDA per ton or per kg is a more meaningful performance indicator than percentage margins.

items.statement: Automotive sector key growth driver with PV and 2W sales growing 26% and 20% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The automotive sector continues to be a key growth driver for CMR with passenger vehicles and two-wheeler sales growing nearly 26% and 20% year-on-year respectively in Q1 FY27

items.statement: Targeting volume mix rebalance from 66-10-24 to 60-20-20 (auto/non-auto/other metals) over coming year
items.quote: In FY26 our volume mix stood at 66% automotive alloys, 10% non-automotive, and 24% other metals. And we actually aim to rebalance it to 60-20-20 over the coming year creating a more diversified and resilient earnings profile.

items.statement: Liquid aluminium now over 50% of aluminium sales, growing faster than ingot sales
items.quote: Look, liquid aluminium today is forming more than 50% of our aluminium sales. Going forward we expect the liquid aluminium to contribute more so growth in liquid metal sales is going to be higher than growth in ingot sales.

items.statement: Scrap sourcing becoming challenging due to export restrictions by some countries; expanding domestic and import sourcing base
items.quote: Look, sourcing of scrap is getting challenging. There are countries which are putting restrictions on export of scrap from those countries. So it is becoming more challenging. How we are doing is that we have expanded our sourcing base

items.statement: Working capital negative in Q1 due to 40% price increase; expect cash flow positive as prices stabilize
items.quote: My cash flow from operation is negative during this quarter also because prices has been moved drastically during the quarter. Average sale price was nearly around INR226/kg to INR230/kg in last quarter and in this quarter INR 350/kg. So around 40% prices has been increased. Therefore, the working capital requirement also increased.

items.statement: Reduced inventory days from 45 to 40 QoQ; cash conversion cycle improved from 69 to 65 days
items.quote: We have gone to about 40 days of inventory from 45 days that we recorded in the previous quarter. And we have actually reduced our cash conversion cycle to 65 days in this quarter from about 69 days in the last quarter.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio currently 0.86, targeting historical 0.5 as prices stabilize and working capital improves
items.quote: Working capital cycle and another is a debt equity ratio. So historically we maintain the 0.5 debt equity ratio and we also in future will maintain the same ratio. But currently it is around 0.86. So definitely it will come down when the prices have got stabilized.

items.statement: Exports 3.4% of turnover; focus on niche products to Japan, Europe, Southeast Asia, China
items.quote: about 3.4% of our turnover came from exports in last year. So, we concentrate on a lot of niche product exports and our concentration will continue to be to export more and more niche products to niche markets

items.statement: Hindustan Zinc MOU signed but no definitive agreement; plant construction not yet started
items.quote: As far as Hindustan Zinc is concerned, we have signed an MOU with them but there is nothing definitive which has still been finalized. So, no activity for construction of a plant has yet started.

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY27 maintained at INR 1,200-1,250 crores
items.quote: We had given a revenue guidance of 1,200 to 1,250. We'll still hold to that as of today because the pipeline looks good.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 expected to remain muted; growth hoped for in second half
items.quote: Next quarter is also looking, you know, muted, I think second half of the year, we are hopeful of seeing some growth.

items.statement: No significant improvement seen in Q2; client spending not normalizing
items.quote: It's been a tough quarter, you know, and I don't see anything significantly improving in quarter 2.

items.statement: Pipeline increased to USD 28 million from USD 25 million last quarter
items.quote: Vikas, the number is 28 million.

items.statement: Shifting from headcount-based to outcome-based managed services deals
items.quote: We are deliberately staying away from headcount deals. Traditionally tech services has been where headcount is linear or coupled linearly to revenue growth. We are trying to break that, you know, by moving more towards managed services and outcome based deals.

items.statement: Employee and resource costs expected to decline as percentage of revenue over time
items.quote: Percentage of overall employee and resource costs vis-a-vis revenue, we do expect it to decline in terms of percentage to revenue over a period of time.

items.statement: Emerging verticals, BFSI, and logistics to drive growth; digital commerce facing headwinds
items.quote: Out of the four verticals, three will drive growth. We are I think we are seeing the maximum headwinds in digital commerce. So emerging verticals will lead, then BFS and then logistics.

items.statement: US revenue contribution target increased to 65% in next 2-3 years from current 52%
items.quote: we get about 55% of our revenue from the US. Niraj Ganeriwal: 52. Aditya Krishna: 52% of our revenue from the US. You will see that growing, and our objective is to get that to at least 65% in the next two or three years

items.statement: Top 10 client concentration reduced from 58% to 56%; voluntarily letting go marginal accounts
items.quote: top 10 is 58 to 56. Aditya Krishna: 58 to 56 is the top 10. So you will see client concentration go down, revenue is flat. So that's one plus

items.statement: Investing in AI capabilities, accelerators, solutions, talent, and industry-specific solutions
items.quote: Parallelly, we continue to make focus investments in our artificial intelligence capabilities, accelerators, and solutions.

items.statement: AI-driven productivity gains of 30-50% in engineering and 20-30% in managed services
items.quote: Today rule of thumb is 30% to 50% I can be more efficient than I could before AI happened. You know, that's on engineering. Managed services, maybe not to that extent, but at least 20% to 30% efficiency is coming because of AI.

items.statement: Employee count declining due to AI productivity in engineering, managed services, and support operations
items.quote: Combination of two factors, Rahul, one is AI-driven productivity in engineering, AI-driven productivity in managed services, and second, very importantly, efficiency in our support operations.

items.statement: All projects now have AI component; no separate AI revenue tracking
items.quote: We don't break up our revenue into AI because every project that we do today has AI.

items.statement: AI enabling participation in larger RFPs previously inaccessible
items.quote: Now, because of AI, we are able to bid for much larger projects because AI has leve lled the field vis-a-vis smaller companies like us and the larger

items.statement: PLA plant commissioning expected: lactic acid in October, PLA in December; target ~40% average capacity utilization in Jan-Mar FY27
items.quote: So, Sanjay, as far as commissioning goes, it looks, you know, lactic we should be able to commission in October and PLA in December.

items.statement: PLA plant target ~40% average capacity utilization in Jan-Mar FY27, assuming plan proceeds
items.quote: So, we expect that from January to March we will have quality production which will be sold. The quantification of it would be little bit difficult to give today, but a safe expectation maybe around 40% on average capacity utilization we should be able to achieve.

items.statement: PLA project capex spend ~INR 2,180 crore by end of July; total project capex INR 3,000-3,200 crore
items.quote: We have spent about INR 2,180 crore by the end of July.

items.statement: PLA plant capacity 80,000 tonnes; construction in full flow with civil, equipment arrivals, erections ongoing
items.quote: On our strategic initiatives, the 80,000-tonnes PLA plant, continues to progress well and remains on track.

items.statement: Season 2025-26 tighter than anticipated with lower production, healthy domestic consumption, ethanol diversion drawing down inventory
items.quote: The season 2025-26 has turned out to be tighter than anticipated, with lower than expected production, healthy domestic consumption and diversion towards ethanol resulting in a drawdown to inventory.

items.statement: Domestic sugar prices firming up due to tight demand-supply, providing relief and offsetting higher cane and distillery costs
items.quote: This tighter demand-supply balance has led to firming up of domestic sugar prices, providing relief to millers and helping offset higher sugarcane costs and other costs & margin pressures in terms of distillery, especially.

items.statement: Sugar price base has moved up firmly and sustainably; average realization higher
items.quote: So we know the sugar price base has moved up. All our assumptions, as I said, when we know. We know cane price might go up. We know distillery may be banned from making B-heavy or juice.

items.statement: Company assumes no diversion to B-heavy or juice next season; only C-heavy allowed; equipped across all units
items.quote: Hence, going into next year, though nothing has been done, it is reasonable to assume that there will be no diversion allowed towards B and juice. So that is a reasonable assumption today, that is our personal view, again, company's view.

items.statement: Expect government to announce broken rice price and availability by Sep-Oct; broken rice use in food basket to drop from 25% to 10%
items.quote: Come September-October, we would see, I think, the Government very clearly giving the price and creating availability for broken rice as well. You know, broken rice will be taken from the open market, but they will create availability by reducing its use in the food basket.

items.statement: Sugar inventory 45.67 lakh quintals at avg carrying cost INR 37.19/kg as of June 30; firm prices provide favourable base for upcoming quarters
items.quote: As of June 30, the Company was carrying sugar inventory of 45.67 lakh quintals at an average carrying cost of INR 37.19 per kg.

items.statement: Distillery margins resilient in Q1 due to B-heavy and maize feedstock; juice-based ethanol sales minimal; transfer pricing impact explained by Maizapur distillery costs retained in sugar division
items.quote: In the quarter gone by, it was largely B-heavy and the maize-based ethanol. There was hardly any sale on account of juice-based ethanol. That is the reason margins are at a good level.

items.statement: Net impact of higher sugar prices vs distillery diversion ban and cane cost hike expected positive net-net
items.quote: If you do not make B-heavy, you will not lose sugar. You will make more sugar. Because what is B-heavy? Sugar is converted into ethanol, sugar (having starch). So you will make more sugar, if you make more sugar, you will make more money on sugar sales in both quantity and price.

items.statement: Country sugar balance: market assumes ~30 lakh tonnes closing stock, actual likely ~35 lakh tonnes; 2 million tonne variance called nonsense
items.quote: I am just giving a figure, assume market is thinking closing stock is 30 lakh tonnes, it will be 35 lakh tonnes.

items.statement: Brazil sugar production expected ~40 million tonnes; ethanol more profitable so lower sugar diversion; EU production contracting; global deficit 1-2 million tonnes
items.quote: Brazil is expected to be at around 40 million tons. As of now, ethanol is more profitable in Brazil, so the diversion towards sugar will be on a lower side. EU, we are seeing some contraction in the sugar production. Overall, there may be a deficit of 1 to 2 million tonnes.

items.statement: Cane sowing good for company; area flat but yield much better for 2027 season
items.quote: We have had a good sowing season. We do not see any problem s. We can’t speak for the whole country, but for our Company we have had a good sowing season

items.statement: Rainfall ideal for cane in Balrampur area; less rain in East UP improves recovery; El Nino impact overstated for cane crop
items.quote: For Balrampur, the rainfall witnessed till date, which is as we speak, has been absolutely ideal for cane. And there is no El Niño in our area, because a little less rainfall in East UP improves the recovery only.

items.statement: PLA trials successful for pan masala/gutka packaging; opportunity large, could absorb entire capacity; also progressing in banned plastic items (straws, garbage bags, carry bags) and flexible packaging
items.quote: The mandate is at a good advanced stage. There have been trials which have been positive at the consumers end as well. The opportunity is large. It will all scale up and become larger.

items.statement: PLA cost competitive; viable for banned goods and flexible packaging where PLA is small fraction of product cost; aluminium price rise helps PLA viability
items.quote: We are cost-wise quite competitive now, so we do not see cost being much of a barrier. Definitely, for banned goods, their cost is not that much of a barrier either.

items.statement: FSSAI notification on plastic-free pan masala packaging dynamic; PLA qualification unclear (yes and no); clarification awaited
items.quote: This is something which is in a bit of a dynamic stage. Yes and no is the answer, which is what we are getting clarification on.

items.statement: Sugar stock normalization: if no diversion next year, 31 mt production, 29 mt consumption, ~3-5 mt closing stock by Oct 2027; prices expected north of INR 43-46/kg
items.quote: Probably in one year, because if they do not allow diversion next year, and assume the gross production is 31 million tonnes, consumption is 29 million tonnes and 3-odd million tonnes is the closing stock.

items.statement: Management requests patience on PLA business; do not model quarterly numbers before operations begin; mid-to-long term 100% utilization possible
items.quote: So do not attempt, please, and this is a humble request, do not please attempt to put quarter one on it, at least.

items.statement: Internal evidence positive on PLA production and marketing; but first attempt so some tolerance needed
items.quote: As I did say, internally all evidence gathered till now is all looking positive, both on the marketing front and on the production front.

items.statement: Maizapur distillery now ready to produce sugar; previously not ready for sugar production
items.quote: Yes, now it is ready. We had planned for this anyway.

items.statement: Q1 is off-season for sugar; profitability influenced by carrying cost and realization of previous season inventory; quarterly dynamics: Q1 off-season, Q2 no production, Q3 partial, Q4 full production
items.quote: As most of you are aware, the first quarter is an off-season for sugar production. Profitability during the quarter is therefore influenced by the carrying cost and realization of sugar inventory from the previous crushing season, with largely no production during the quarter.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance maintained at approximately INR 300 crores
items.quote: Overall capex for the year will still be what I mentioned in the May call, approximately INR 300 crores for the year.

items.statement: Draw tower expansion accelerated from phased 4-6-8 million km to direct 4 to 8 million km in one go
items.quote: But in the meanwhile we have decided to go ahead with the complete expansion right from four to eight in one go, seeing that there is a shortage of fiber across the globe and that shortage is likely to continue for some time more.

items.statement: Preform production commenced, targeting stability in next couple of months; draw capacity to reach 8 million km by end of Q2 FY27
items.quote: On the expansion side, I had mentioned in the last call that the preform production has commenced. We are on the way to stability. Hopefully in the next couple of months that should happen.

items.statement: Communication cables revenue INR 176 crores in Q1 FY27, up 62% YoY, with INR 35-40 crores from exports to US and Europe
items.quote: Communication Cables delivered a particularly strong performance during the quarter with a revenue increase from INR 109 crores to INR 176 crores, which is a growth of approximately 62% with margins close to 30%.

items.statement: Communication cables margin near 30% in Q1 FY27 due to low-cost opening inventory; expected to normalize to low-double digits as inventory depletes
items.quote: On the communication cable side, as I mentioned in my opening remarks, so long as the old raw material is available for use, the margins will be high-double digits. But as that stock gets depleted, you will see a correction in the margins. I still believe that at the end of the year provided the demand situation remains similar to what it is today, I still believe that you should have a double-dig

items.statement: Electrical cables margin around 10.5% considered sustainable
items.quote: On the domestic front, the margins at electrical cable side should be sustainable. We are at about 10.5% I think, and those should be sustainable.

items.statement: Fiber prices (G.652.D) peaked at USD 17-18/km, now settling at USD 11-13/km; premium fibers up to USD 50/km
items.quote: The standard fiber, which is the technical term there is G.652.D, was somewhere around USD 5 to 6 back in December last year, had climbed up to USD 17 - 18 over the last six, seven months. I think currently is settling at about between USD 12 and USD 13 per kilometer that's where it is today.

items.statement: Helium cost fluctuated from INR 1,600 to INR 5,000 per cubic meter, now at INR 3,400-3,500; Germanium tetrachloride availability tight with long lead times
items.quote: If you look at the inputs that go into it, let's say fuel, helium, for instance, was selling at approximately INR 1,600 per cubic meter. It had gone up to INR 5,000 per cubic meter when the disturbances started in the Middle East. It is now around INR 3,400- INR 3,500 levels, so there is a little bit of fluctuation, stability is still not there.

items.statement: Auto cables, solar cables, agricultural cables, flexible wires posted high double-digit volume growth; building wires low single-digit growth with channel destocking
items.quote: On the electrical cables side, automotive cables, battery cables, flexible wires, solar and agricultural applications, all of them did extremely well posting fairly high double-digit growth numbers and this is just not a price growth, it is also volume-led growth.

items.statement: Data center and AI-driven fiber demand booming globally; India consumption at 25 million km/year vs China 400+ million km, potential to reach 50-60 million km
items.quote: Our overall consumption in the country is still around 25 million kilometers per year compare that with China at 400 million plus or even higher than that, so there is still a long way to go. I'm not saying that we will reach 400 million, but given the size of both our geographies, a factor of 20 million is not something that we should aspire for, I think our 25 million consumptions can easily go

items.quote: Typically, our numbers have been like this. Approximately two-thirds is construction related and the balance has more or less been equal between automobile, agriculture, and industrials. items.statement: JV (Finolex J-Power Systems) revenue INR 87 crores, profit INR 7 crores in Q1 FY27, continuing FY26 trend of INR 24 crores profit
items.quote: The additional information that I would like to share with you is that I had mentioned that the JV was doing well and had posted a profit of INR 24 crores last year that trend continues in the current quarter. items.statement: Sachin Naik joined as CFO effective 1st June 2024

items.statement: BharatNet project stalled due to high prices; winners waiting and watching
items.quote: No, not really. I think with the prices as high as they are, the winners are waiting and watching.

items.quote: But the target of INR 5 billion by 2028 still remains and we are sure that we can get over there.

items.statement: FY27 steel segment EBITDA per ton guidance of INR 4,600-4,700 for full year
items.quote: And we are fully committed that full year of FY27 guidance of INR4,600 to INR4,700 per ton EBITDA will be achieved.

items.statement: FY27 lighting volume growth target of ~25% and value growth of 22-23%
items.quote: We remain fully on track to deliver our FY27 guidance of about 22% to 23% value growth and about 25% of volume growth in lighting.

items.quote: our EBITDA was INR 120 crore in Q1. So, we are expecting around INR 150 crore in Q2.

items.quote: I think we'll be doing around 3 lakh tons of export.

items.quote: So, this will gradually improve because now fresh orders are coming, so I feel compared to last year's INR5,500–INR5,700 per ton, I feel we will take it up to INR5,000.

items.quote: targeting overall capacity of about 16 lakh ton in FY2 7 and approximately 2 million ton of capacity by FY '28-'29.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 steel capacity utilization at ~82% across all five factories
items.quote: The capacity utilization stood at approximately 82%.

items.statement: Professional lighting order book of ~INR 150 crore providing near-term execution visibility
items.quote: Professional lighting ended the quarter with an order book of approximately INR150 crore, providing healthy near-term execution visibility.

items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at about INR84 crore, up 63% year -on-year, with EBITDA per ton to INR4,006 against INR2,922 in Q1 of FY26.

items.statement: Lighting Q1 FY27 revenue INR 456 crore (+15% YoY), broad-based growth across LED bulbs, battens, downlighters, appliances, professional lighting
