items.quote: So we are aligning with our group's strategy to ensure that we have same auditors. So this mandatory rotation for group also it made sense for us to have a productive discussion with our auditors and they had said that they also had intent to resign and we will be adopting Sensitivity: Internal the same auditors in the upcoming AGM to ensure that we get the right governance and also synergies alon

items.statement: Goodwill impairment of Dalmia business complete; no further impairment expected, non-cash item below EBITDA
items.quote: So, goodwill was one time and all we can confirm is that all the goodwill of Dalmia is already off our balance sheet now. And by the way, just to kind of remind everybody to the investor, these are non-cash goodwill, non-cash impairment, no impact on our profitability. It is below EBITDA line.

items.statement: Export share reduced from last quarter; targeting flow control/isostatic product exports growth in coming months
items.quote: But the current performance, Sahil, it's actually reduced from last quarter to this quarter. So it's actually reducing at the moment for us.

items.statement: Industry production grew 22% YoY to 93.6 lakh units in Q1 FY27 with broad-based momentum across segments
items.quote: Overall, industry performance during the quarter reflected broad-based momentum with domestic automobile production increasing over 22% year -on-year to 93.6 lakh units, underscoring strong OEM activity and healthy demand visible across automobile value chain.

items.statement: No formal guidance provided; growth drivers identified as lightweighting orders, export SOPs, temperature-controlled tubes, and domestic OEM volumes
items.quote: The key contributors to FY27 growth include the full year benefits of previously announced lightweighting order s, ramp -up of additional lightweighting programs, the temperature-controlled tube adjacencies, SOPs of North American export orders and the supportive outlook for domestic OEM volumes.

items.statement: North American export orders worth $10.7M annual value and $58.5M lifetime value with SOPs expected in Q3 and Q4 FY27
items.value: US$10.7 million annual, US$58.5 million lifetime
items.quote: Our previously announced 3 orders from a North American engine and genset manufacturer with a combined annual value of approximately US$10.7 million and a lifetime value of approximately US$58.5 million remain aligned to revised customer schedules.

items.statement: Most direct materials on pass-through basis; one-time premium RM procurement due to geopolitical situation absorbed in Q1 gross profit
items.quote: Most of the direct materials are on pass -through basis. And there was small impact of premium RM procurement, which is built into the gross profit growth of 8% because of the geopolitical situation.

items.statement: Uttarakhand facility investment of ~INR 20 crores progressing per customer plan; Chakan 3 lightweighting facility commenced SOP with modular capacity
items.quote: Our new Uttarakhand facility is progressing in line with the customer implementation plan. The project involves an investment of approximately INR 20 crores and has been planned closer to customers' manufacturing location to improve logistics, responsiveness and JIT alignment.

items.statement: Chakan 3 lightweighting facility commenced SOP and ramping up; Uttarakhand facility to support relocation and co-location of existing business
items.quote: Our Chakan 3 lightweighting facility has commenced SOP and is ramping up in line with customer schedules. The facil ity has been designed with modular capacity, allowing investment to remain linked to confirmed programs and future customer demand

items.statement: Diversifying across products, powertrains, geographies; expanding lightweighting portfolio beyond control arms into subframe and torsion beams via Donghee partnership
items.quote: technology licensing agreement with Donghee expands our lightweighting portfolio beyond control arms into subframe and torsion beams

items.statement: Export strategy focused on CV emission components, temperature-controlled tubes, genset emission components, small agri genset exhaust systems; RFQ pipeline across focus areas
items.quote: Our export market strategy essentially is focusing around CV emission components, temperature-controlled tubes, genset emission components and small agri genset exhaust systems.

items.statement: Built M&A capabilities and disciplined framework; ready to be more assertive in strategic acquisitions while maintaining ROCE and integration filters
items.quote: Having established these capabilities, we believe we are now ready to be more assertive in pursuing strategic acquisitions. However, this does not mean compromising on discipline. Any transaction must continue to meet our filters of strategic fit, customer and technology relevance, valuation, integration feasibility and ROCE.

items.statement: Lightweighting addressable market estimated at INR 8,000-9,000 crores in 5 years; targeting mid-to-high teen percentage share
items.quote: Our internal assessment on this portfolio is around 5 years from now, it can be between INR8,000 crores to INR 9,000 crores. And we firmly believe that we can actually build a mid -teen to high-teen percentage share in that portfolio.

items.statement: Mindful of risks from evolving geopolitical conditions; premium RM procurement impact in Q1 due to geopolitical situation
items.quote: As we move ahead, the operating environment remains supportive, although we remain mindful of certain risks arising out of evolving geopolitical conditions.

items.statement: Filed 2 additional patents in Q1 FY27; total patent filings 24 with 4 awarded; R&D supporting WLTP, Euro-7, hybrid, flex fuel, temperature control tubes, lightweighting localization
items.quote: During Q1 FY2 7, we filed 2 additional patents. This takes the total number of patents filing to 24 with 4 patents awarded. Our R&D team are also supporting WLTP, Euro-7 benchmarking, hybrid solutions, flex fuel readiness, temperature control tubes and the localization of lightweighting technology.

items.statement: Raw material pass-through timelines vary by customer; no vacuum in numbers due to lag as previous quarter recovery occurs in current quarter
items.quote: For this quarter, I will get next quarter. So, there will be a lag. But that lag doesn't create any vacuum for a particular quarter because you get for the previous quarter. So therefore, you won't see any vacuum because of this reason in the numbers.

items.statement: Lightweighting market share was 14% at end of FY26; expected to increase with current order visibility and SOPs in Q3 FY27
items.quote: We have given the market share of 14% in the last financial year. We do market share analysis every year. We don't do it every quarter. So, it was 14% at the end of the financial year. With the SOPs and what visibility we have, which we see now happening even in the third quarter, this market share will certainly go up.

items.statement: Purem JV program started Q4 FY26, ramping up in FY27; JV provides technology access but limited PAT share; evaluating deeper participation in CV >4L segment
items.quote: So, Manpreet, as far as that program, which we mentioned last time, that program is concerned, it started in Q4 last year and it will gradually ramp up during the course of FY27. So that's very much on track.

items.statement: Received 600+ orders from Vodafone Idea in mid-June; converted 95 towers (150 tenancies) in June; 700+ tenancies in pipeline for Q2
items.quote: We had declared on the exchange also that we got around 600-plus orders from Vodafone, out of which we converted 95 towers which is equal to 150 tenancies in month of June itself.

items.statement: Targeting 3,000 additional tenancies from Vodafone Idea in FY27 on conservative basis; 80% new towers, 20% on existing
items.quote: We are planning 3,000 sites for Vodafone Idea with an average revenue of INR31,000 without EV, around INR50,000 with EV.

items.statement: Expect quarterly revenue of INR100 crore by Q4 FY27; annualized INR400 crore; PAT margin target 22-24%
items.quote: We can see it from Q4.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 59.3% with electricity reimbursement in top line; expect to maintain ~59% EBITDA margin and ~20% PAT margin
items.quote: We will have the same EBITDA margin with EV, which I have shown right now which is around 59%. We will maintain the same EBITDA margin for coming quarters also.

items.statement: Zinc battery (100% made in India) ready for launch by mid-September at INR33,000 per 100H vs lithium at INR48,000; will reduce CapEx and operating cost
items.quote: Zinc battery is ready. It's under production right now and we should get first batch for around 10, 15 sites in by mid of September. And pricing of zinc battery is similar to old pricing of lithium battery.

items.statement: Lithium battery prices doubled in 2.5 months from INR33,500 to INR48,000 per 100H due to China subsidy removal and rupee depreciation; all cells imported from China
items.quote: The battery which was purchasing at the rate of INR33,500 for Grade H went up to -- current price is INR48,000. So, which is almost 50% increase in last couple of months.

items.statement: Revenue share: Airtel 48.1%, Vi 27%, Jio 22.6%, BSNL 2.3%; targeting Vi share to 30-32% after rollout
items.quote: Right now, we are saying we want to take Vodafone to 30%, 32%. We are eyeing around 32% of revenue from Vodafone once we are able to do these 3,000 or more sites from Vodafone.

items.statement: Vodafone Idea plans 45,000 site rollout in 18-24 months (3,000-3,500 sites/month); BSNL plans 2 lakh sites in 5 years (INR77,000 crore CapEx) but rollout delayed by Tejas equipment issues
items.quote: Vodafone has already declared close to 45,000 site rollout plan in next 18-24 months. They are targeting to do 3,000, 3,500 site every month which they have already started.

items.statement: Tenancy ratio 1.22x (7,468 tenancies / 6,103 towers); targeting 1.8x by early FY29 driven by macro site rollouts; Q1 rollout achieved 1.58x (150 tenancies / 95 towers)
items.quote: We are targeting to reach 1.8 in coming 3 to 4 years, so it should be a very decent risk for industry.

items.statement: No immediate fundraising planned; internal accruals sufficient for 3,000 tenancies; may consider if larger orders from Vi/BSNL materialize
items.quote: As of now, we have enough funds from internal accruals. We are not seeing any major fundraising right now. But depends if I get more orders than expected, then we may decide on fundraising.

items.statement: Revenue per tower (ex-EV) stable at INR31,000-31,500 for last 4 quarters; with EV ~INR50,000
items.quote: Revenue per tower has been constant at INR31,000, INR31,500 for us from last four quarters.

items.statement: 186 BSNL sites pending billing for 1-1.5 years; Tejas equipment issues resolving; expect billing to start in Q2
items.quote: Right now, it's 186. So, in this quarter, they have not added anything because they are busy resolving their Tejas issue. But yes, 186 site billing is still pending, which we are expecting now.

items.statement: FY28 target: additional 5,000 tenancies from Vodafone (total 8,000-10,000 over two years); visibility limited beyond FY28 due to industry dynamics
items.quote: If we go in FY28, we are eyeing another 5,000 sites from Vodafone. Out of 45,000 sites, we are saying we will do around 8,000 to 10,000 tenancies from Vodafone in two financial years.

items.statement: Fibre revenue 5-8% of total in FY27; no major jump expected as Vi rollout on microwave; EBITDA margin similar to towers
items.quote: In terms of revenue, it will be very marginal. Right now, we are focused on more of macro sites and more and more sites are coming to rural villages where they go on a microwave rather than fibre.

items.statement: BSNL rollout uncertain due to Tejas equipment issues and slow execution; Vi funding beyond INR6,400 crore not yet secured; company dependent on customer rollout pace
items.quote: Only challenge for BSNL, that I am not as confident as Vodafone is because we are yet to see resolution of Tejas equipment which they are facing issues with Tejas equipment due to which their entire rollout has been delayed from past 1, 1.5 years.

items.statement: Execution capacity and team ready; achieved 150 tenancies in 13-15 days in rainy season; confident of scaling
items.quote: Even in rainy season, we have been doing 100 sites frequency, 150 tenancies in mid-June, which was rainy for parts of India. We are very confident. We have execution capacity.

items.statement: Order book stood at INR990 crores at end of Q1 FY27, up from INR880 crores previous quarter after INR157 crores execution and INR143 crores fresh inflows.
items.quote: Our order book stood at INR990 crores at the end of quarter, providing a healthy base for the revenue visibility going forward.

items.statement: Fresh order inflows of INR143 crores secured during Q1 FY27.
items.quote: the quarter saw continued momentum in our order inflows, with the company securing fresh contracts worth INR143 crores during the period

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 505 bps YoY to 24.4% in Q1 FY27, driven by project delivery efficiency gains.
items.quote: EBITDA increased substantially by 27% on a year-on-year basis to INR39 crores, with EBITDA margins improving to 24.4%, representing an expansion of 505 basis points over the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Geospatial Engineering Services revenue grew 30% YoY to INR94 crores; Technology Solutions revenue declined 25% YoY to INR63 crores.
items.quote: our Geospatial Engineering Services revenue for the quarter increased by 30% year-on-year to INR94 crores, while Technology Solutions side, revenue declined by around 25% year-on-year to INR63 crores

items.statement: Management does not provide forward guidance on revenue, order inflow or margins as per company policy.
items.quote: We don't give the forward guidance because that's not within our policy.

items.statement: Approved investment up to INR25 crores in 50:50 JV with AI Fabric USA to build sovereign AI cloud for defense, cybersecurity and government; first INR5 crores for incorporation, then INR20 crores post due diligence.
items.quote: We have approved an investment up to INR25 crores in joint venture with AI Fabric USA to be incorporated to create a sovereign AI new cloud in India for Indian government, citizens and companies focused on cybersecurity, services and defense to offer GPU-as-a-service, model-as-a-service and AI service, to build or lease data center capacity.

items.statement: Working capital cycle at 164 days in Q1 FY27; expect meaningful improvement over next 2-3 quarters as Maharashtra government releases stuck IoT/JJM funds.
items.quote: On working capital cycle stood at 164 days during the quarter broadly in line with the levels seen over the previous 2 quarters. We expect recent – we have received recent government institution issued by Maharashtra government towards allocation of funds for the dues related to IoT and other projects to support collection and meaningfully improve the working capital cycle over the next 2 to 3 qua

items.statement: CFO expects INR100 crores of IoT debtors from JJM projects to be collected by end of Q3 FY27.
items.quote: We have IoT debtors and received from IP approximately UBR of around total amount of INR100 crores, and we are expecting to get these funds by end of third quarter, most probably.

items.statement: Order book execution timeline weighted average 12-18 months; some orders 3-6 months, O&M portions extend 2-5 years.
items.quote: On an average, the execution time line weighted average will be between 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: Received LOI from Madhya Pradesh Urban Administration for PMAY manpower agency contract worth ~INR67 crores over 3 years.
items.quote: We have received a Letter of Intent from the Director of Urban Administration and Development, Madhya Pradesh for the selection and appointment of a manpower agency for beneficiary led constant vertical under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana with a total contract value of approximately INR67 crores, which is going to be gained over the next 3 years.

items.statement: Received LOI from Bhandara Municipal Council for AMR water meters under AMRUT 2.0 worth INR17 crores, execution over 12 months.
items.quote: We recently issued a Letter of Intent from Bhandara Municipal Counsel for a supply, installation, commissioning of a consumer, domestic ultrasonic and electromagnetic AMR water meters under the Amrut 2.0 with an order value of INR17 crores.

items.statement: International geospatial orders from T Second worth INR30 crores for NVMe drives, AI-powered building/road extraction, BRYCK AI platform and enterprise geospatial imagery repository.
items.quote: our early engagement with T Second includes NVMe drive supply as well as AI-powered building and road extraction encroachment and asset monitoring through BRYCK AI platform, along with enterprise geospatial imagery repository and AI feature extraction capabilities. The aggregate value of these purchase orders was INR30 crores.

items.statement: Run-rate businesses (Mobility, Product Solutions) contributed ~INR130 crores (20-25%) of FY26 revenue and are not captured in order book.
items.quote: FY26, we had business, as I mentioned, are the 2 segments, which are without order book was INR130 crores, which includes Mobility and the Product Solutions business.

items.statement: Evaluating acquisition targets for vertical integration and margin expansion; INR238 crores raised (INR100 crores Sep'24, INR130 crores Mar'26) but no deals closed yet.
items.quote: We don't want to invest just for the sake of investing we want to see that investments are in line with what we are doing either it is vertical integration backward or vertical integration forward within our line of business so that it enables the margin expansion.

items.statement: Phaneesh Murthy resigned in April 2026 for personal reasons; management denies any link to share price decline.
items.quote: Phaneesh Murthy-ji has resigned in the month of April 2026 and not November 2025. So there is a correction in the date. And there is no relevance of share price and exit of Mr. Phaneesh Murthy. He has resigned because of his personal reasons.

items.statement: CFO rejects share buyback, stating funds raised are for growth investments not surplus cash; promoters invested confidently.
items.quote: Share buyback generally happens when you have cash surplus from operations. Whatever funds we have is the promoters who are invested in the company because they are confident about the growth and the future prospects of the company.

items.statement: International subsidiary (US) showed top-line growth and margin improvement in Q1 FY27; expect good traction in coming year.
items.quote: Top line has also increased for our overseas business in this quarter, even the margins have improved in that business. So, we foresee a good traction in the U.S. subsidiary also in this coming year.

items.statement: JJM project fund delays caused unbilled revenue pile-up of INR320 crores (50% of standalone revenue); expect billing conversion in next 2 quarters.
items.quote: this unbilled revenue, major portion is of JJM things and which we have clarified in our, just a few, in one of the calls that we have got the clarity from the department and this amount will be billed in this next 2 quarters and this unbilled revenue will automatically go down in next 2 quarters once we have this funds from the JJM projects.

items.statement: No specific debt discussion; working capital management focus on collecting government dues.
items.quote: whatever we are billing, we are collecting, so there is no additional buildup of working capital cycle.

items.statement: Mobility business (Allygrow) seeing improvement since Dec 2025; Grammer AG JV (Allygram) not consolidated but Grammer order book improving for CY2026.
items.quote: Grammer also has seen that there is an improvement in the order book for the calendar year 2026, and that is a general improvement overall in the Mobility business.

items.statement: Maharashtra government GR released for disbursement of stuck IoT/JJM funds; expect clearance of overdues before March 31.
items.quote: the Government of Maharashtra has issued a GR where they have said that the majority of the funds which was stuck earlier for the IoT-related projects under the Jal Jeevan mission, they have already resolved that the major funds will be disbursed.

items.statement: International geospatial mobility business showing meaningful improvement with new business development and contract awards gaining momentum.
items.quote: Our international geospatial mobility business showed a meaningful improvement during the quarter with new business development opportunities and contract awards gaining momentum.

items.statement: Margin improvement from 15-17% two years ago to 24% now driven by shift from data acquisition to enterprise solutions and better technology solutions mix.
items.quote: earlier, the margins were, let's say, when we began before 2 years, margins were around 15% to 17%, and we are now going up to 24%.

items.statement: Expect to surpass last year's order inflow numbers; strong funnel with several L1 positions awaiting final award.
items.quote: Funnel is pretty strong and we'll see, we are surpassing our last year's numbers. That's for sure that I will maintain it and reiterate it, we have a very strong funnel across our order book.

items.statement: Transport domain (ITMS/ATMS) capabilities built; partner tie-ups done; expect positive developments in next 1-2 quarters.
items.quote: we have already gathered the capabilities. In some of the cases where we did not have, we already tied up with the partners, and we are already in discussion with the government for some more opportunities. So, we expect some positive developments in the next 1 or 2 quarters on the transport domain.

items.statement: Large mission-mode projects (like JM INR350 cr) take 1-2 years to build; expect one such game-changer project this year or Q1 next year.
items.period: this year or Q1 next year
items.quote: We can anticipate to get one of those in this year, fingers crossed. I cannot put a number over there. But if not fourth quarter, first quarter of next year, we will definitely have one of such kind of projects.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target Rs 1,250-1,400 crore with PAT margin 8.5-9%
items.quote: If you look at a theoretical calculation, it would go somewhere to 2,000. But I believe once Unit 6 comes into operation, then 1,700 or so will not be a difficult task for us.

items.statement: FY28 revenue potential Rs 1,700-1,750 crore with full year Unit 6 operation
items.quote: Next year, we will have the full year for Unit 6, whereas this year we only have five or six months. So with a full 12 months, I see the possibility of crossing 1,700 to 1,750.

items.statement: Q2 demand becoming more apparent, expects better than Q1
items.quote: In Q2, the demand is becoming even more apparent. Also, Q1 being the start of the financial year and the beginning of the conflict, people were a bit slow in purchasing as they wanted to wait and see how things behaved.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 11.4%, PAT margin 8.2%, targeting 8.5-9% PAT margin for FY27
items.quote: EBITDA increased by 9.7% year-on-year to Rs. 31.9 crores with a margin of 11.4%, while profit after tax grew by 9.4% to Rs. 22.9 crores with a margin of 8.2%.

items.statement: Management expects PAT margin to return to 8.5-9% levels from current 8.2%
items.quote: No, sir, you don't expect 10%. I did not say 10%. I said that we will come to the level of 8.5%-9%. I hope so.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex Rs 20 crore, cumulative Rs 209 crore of Rs 512 crore planned
items.quote: Moving to our capital expenditure program, we incurred approximately Rs. 20 crores during Q1 FY27 across ongoing expansion initiatives. With this, cumulative capex incurred stands at Rs. 209 crores as of June 30, 2026, against the total planned capex of Rs. 512 crores.

items.statement: Land acquisition of 30,000 sqm at Lote Parshuram for Rs 9.33 crore
items.quote: During the quarter, the company acquired approximately 30,000 square meters of additional land at Lote Parshuram for Rs. 9.33 crores, located near the existing Unit 1.

items.statement: Meghnagar expansion progressing, adds 4,50,000 MT fertilizer and 72,000 MT chemical capacity
items.quote: Together, these projects are expected to add 4,50,000 metric tons per annum of fertilizer capacity and 72,000 metric tons per annum of the chemical capacity additionally, significantly expanding the company's manufacturing base.

items.statement: 10 MW DC solar project at Nanded nearing completion, total solar capacity to reach 20.6 MW DC
items.quote: The 10 megawatt DC solar power project at Nanded is nearing completion and once co mmissioned, we will take the company's total installed solar capacity to 20.6 megawatt on DC

items.statement: Sulphur prices reset from USD 250-300 to USD 1,100, acid plants on low load due to working capital stress
items.quote: Specifically, if I talk about sulphur, sulphur, which used to be in the range of USD250-USD300, in today's date, only sulphur is in the range of USD1,100. We do not expect that these prices will again come back.

items.statement: K-acid price moved from Rs 550 to Rs 700+, company is largest K-acid manufacturer in India
items.quote: Today, we are the largest manufacturer of K-acid in India. No one else is in K-acid. The price of the product has moved from Rs. 550 to Rs. 700-plus.

items.statement: Fertilizer 51%, Chemical 49% of sales value in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The fertilizer business recorded sales value of Rs. 142 crores, representing growth of 4% year-on-year basis, while the chemical business reported sales value of Rs. 138 crores, grown by 17.10% on year-on-year basis. Two businesses contributed 51% and 49%, respectively, to the sales value during the quarter.

items.statement: Acid plants on low load due to working capital stress - sulphur requires advance payment, acid sold on credit
items.quote: Secondly, 1 kg of sulfur makes 3 kg of acid. Today, sulfur requires advance payment, while acid is sold entirely on credit. If I am earning two cents, I will do it. When I am not earning those two cents, why should I block working capital?

items.statement: Rs 125 crore non-lien deposits as of June 30, 2026, funded through internal accruals and preferential issue proceeds
items.quote: From a liquidity perspective, the company continues to maintain a comfortable position with Rs. 125 crores in non-lien deposits as on June 30, 2026.

items.statement: Fertilizer volume 66,527 MT (down from 76,288 MT), Chemical volume 9,113 MT (down from 14,837 MT)
items.quote: The fertilizer business recorded the sales volume of 66,527 metric tons compared to 76,288 metric tons in Q1 FY26, while volumes in the chemical business were 9,113 metric tons compared to 14,837 metric tons in the corresponding period.

items.statement: Fertilizer sales value Rs 142 crore (+4% YoY), Chemical sales value Rs 138 crore (+17.1% YoY)
items.quote: The fertilizer business reported sales value of Rs. 142 crores, growing by 4% on year-on-year basis, while the chemical business recorded sales value of Rs. 138 crores, registering growth of 17.10% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: West Asia conflict and Hormuz closure caused raw material supply disruption, now improving
items.quote: Like ammonia is a major raw material into that, sulphur is a major raw material into that, and suddenly there was acute shortage of these two raw materials because of the closure of the Hormuz.

items.statement: DAP availability challenge limits farmer shift from NPK/SSP despite price hikes
items.quote: DAP import prices, sale prices, and availability. If a product is available, a consumer will shift. But if DAP is available, who would pay more for NPK or SSP? If he gets DAP at a cheaper price, any consumer would shift

items.statement: No plans for battery-grade phosphoric acid, focused on current expansions first
items.quote: No, sir. As of now, very honestly sp eaking, we are totally focused towards our goal and objective. So regarding the battery-grade and other things are not on our agenda as of

items.statement: Madhya Pradesh plant fully integrated with 800 TPD chemical plant for backward integration into NPK
items.quote: In Madhya Pradesh, the capacity is double that of Unit 6. There is also an 800-ton-per-day chemical plant there, but that will be used for backward integration into the finished NPK products.

items.statement: Management expects double-digit revenue growth for FY27 and EBITDA margin to return to ~30%
items.quote: As of now, we feel yes. Even this quarter, we lost around INR 10 crores because of the sales reversal, which will come in the next quarter. As of now, we think we should be able to grow in double digits.

items.statement: US business growth expected at 8-10% steady state
items.quote: We don't expect at least at this juncture beyond 8-10% of growth.

items.statement: FY27 capex of INR 123 crore; INR 20 cr maintenance, INR 50 cr R&D, balance growth capex
items.quote: INR 123 crores, you rightly said that we have explained in the AGM, correct? Abhishek Navalgund Yeah. Beni Prasad Rauka This is what we are going to spend

items.statement: Fermentation utilisation at 70-75%; capacity expansion decision next quarter
items.quote: We are close to 70-75%, and we will take the call in the next quarter, and we may start some of the CapEx expenditure for increasing our capacity.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 27% vs 30% YoY and 31% QoQ due to lower realisation, higher power/fuel, mix shift
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter came in at INR 510 million, down 10% YoY and 19% QoQ. Consequently, the EBITDA margin stood at 27% compared to 30% in Q1 FY26 and 31% in Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margin to normalise to ~30% for full year
items.quote: Yes. We expect that it shall come back to the normal level of about 30% of EBITDA.

items.statement: INR 100 million incremental sales reversal in Q1 due to goods in transit; already recorded as of call date
items.quote: On account of revenue recognition accounting principles, this quarter was impacted by an additional sales reversal amounting to INR 100 million over and above reversal of revenue generally being accounted in every quarter.

items.statement: Top 10 customers 23% of revenue vs 27% YoY and 26% QoQ; top 10 products 45% vs 45% YoY and 49% QoQ
items.quote: I would like to give you some numbers about our top 10 customer s. It is about 23% during this quarter as compared to 27%, last year Q1 and as compared to 26% in Q4 FY26. Our top 10 products has contributed about 45%, as compared to 45% last year and 49% in last quarter of FY26

items.statement: Power and fuel costs elevated due to global energy disruption; pricing better this quarter with some price increases
items.quote: Our consolidated margins moderated primarily due to three factors: lower top-line realization, elevated power and fuel costs driven by global energy disruption, and a temporary shift in the sales mix.

items.statement: Realisation improved vs Q4 and Q1 FY26 due to price hikes
items.quote: Pricing is better in this particular quarter because we have increased some prices. It's better in that sense. Realization is better than Q4 and Q1 of last year.

items.statement: Inventory INR 190 cr, receivables INR 131 cr, payables INR 41 cr; working capital cycle 125-138 days
items.quote: Inventory, 30th June 2026, was about INR 190 crores. We had a receivable of about INR 131 crores. Payables were about INR 41 crores. INR 280 crores was roughly invested in the working capital. In terms of number of days, generally our working capital cycle is about 125-138 days.

items.statement: Debt at ~20% of revenue vs 22% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our debt is about 20% of our revenue as compared to 22% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Board approved buyback of INR 697 million at ceiling price INR 500/share via open market; starts 14 Aug
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that the Board has approved a buyback of INR 697 million at a ceiling price of INR 500 per share via open market route.

items.statement: Acquired remaining 4.28% stake in JC Biotech for INR 79.79 million, now 100% owned
items.quote: The company has also announced the acquisition of the remaining stake of 4.28% for a consideration of INR 79.79 million in our existing subsidiary, JC Biotech, resulting in a total stake of 100%, making it wholly-owned subsidiary.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions, trade uncertainties, supply chain disruptions, energy/raw material volatility impacting US and global ops
items.quote: The global economy has been experiencing significant disturbance for quite some time, primarily driven by geographical tensions, trade and uncertainties, and continued disruption across global supply chain.

items.statement: R&D spend INR 90 million (4.75% of revenue) in Q1 FY27 vs INR 86 million (4.62%) YoY
items.quote: R&D expenditure, we have spent about INR 90 million in the Q1 of FY27 as compared to INR 86 million in Q1 of FY26. This is about 4.75% during this quarter as compared to 4.62% in the corresponding Q1 of FY26.

And this time, we see this cost, what have appeared is on a normal operational cost basis, which is there for our different subsidiaries.

Both leaders having decades of experience across strategy, governance, business transformation, renewable energy, infrastructure and organization leadership further strengthen the depth and capability of our Board as we enter the next phase of growth. items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 30-40% YoY for FY27, conservative vs earlier 40-50% due to geopolitical conditions
items.quote: if you see that the growth we have committed for the 30% to 40% year-on-year, that is something that which we will be able to maintain.

items.statement: PAT margin guidance of 16-18% for FY27 likely to be lower; full recovery expected in FY28
items.quote: it will be a little bit less, I thin k, compared to what we had shown in the past. But '27, '28 when the full plant is stabilized, it will again, we expect it to jump back to the older

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 37% in Q1 FY27 from 35% YoY; PAT declined due to higher depreciation and finance costs from new IPP capacity
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin has improved to 37% from 35%, reflecting the operating strength of our portfolio. Profit after tax for the quarter stood at INR95 crore as compared to INR111 crore in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: IPP segment EBITDA margin 85-90%; CPP margins impacted by geopolitical cost pressures on steel, cables, logistics
items.quote: my IP business gives me an EBITDA of 85% to 90%. Post EBITDA, there are not too much of cost. So it's depreciation and interest cost.

items.statement: CPP order book approximately INR5,000+ crore; IPP revenue trajectory strengthening as newly commissioned assets ramp up
items.quote: And the CPP also, I have an order book of approx imately INR5,000-plus crore. So going forward, there is enough order book in hand for the CPP side and the IPP revenue also, as I told in my initial talk that the IPP segment from here will show a be tter strong upward trajectory

items.statement: Portfolio reached 6.94 GW (up 71% YoY): 1.87 GW installed, 5.07 GW WIP; 2.57 GW IPP, 4.37 GW CPP; commissioned 0.85 GW and booked 2.88 GW fresh orders in past year
items.quote: As of June 30, 2026, our portfolio has reached approximately 6.94 gigawatts, up 71% year-on- year from 4.06 gigawatt a year ago. This comprises an installed capa city of 1.87 gigawatt and work in progress capacity of 5.07 gigawatts

items.statement: Q1 FY27 IPP generation grew nearly 4x YoY; single quarter generation exceeds 65% of entire FY26 generation
items.quote: It is also worth noting that our Q 1 FY27 unit generation under the IPP portfolio has grown nearly 4x year-on-year and the generation achieved in this single quarter already exc eeds 65% of the entire FY26 generation

items.statement: Long-term debt-to-net-worth expected to stay at max 3:1; INR670 crore green bond (8.5% coupon, 5-year, AA+ rated, 65% GuarantCo guarantee) listed; total debt ~INR5,000-6,000 crore projected for FY27-28
items.quote: going forward, I think the debt to equity will be in the comfortable position of 3:1 max to max, which will be long-term debt to net worth.

items.statement: Annual interest cost for full IPP capacity estimated at ~INR450 crore (8.5% rate on ~INR5,000 crore debt); interest during construction phase ending
items.quote: Annual interest cost would be at around our rate of interest is at 8.5% or som ething. So if I calculate 8.5 around INR450-odd crore should be the total full -- my capacity of INR5,000-odd crore of debt and something coming into picture

items.statement: Geopolitical conditions impacting costs: steel (MMS structures, evacuation towers), cables, logistics, cranes, diesel; some costs absorbed, some passed to customers
items.quote: If you understand geopolitical conditions, the major impact is from the fuel. Now you understand that a lot of components goes into a solar plant. You have cables, you have steel, you have other ROW issues, you have logistics. All these factors have got impacted.

items.statement: Inventory built up in FY26 due to geopolitical supply risks; has come down in Q1 FY27 and expected to decline further as projects complete
items.quote: It has come down to some extent in this quarter, and we expect it to go down further as we go on. The reason for building the inventory was 2, 3 factors. One w as that since the geopolitical conditions were getting worsened, a lot of material we had to pile up because we had the availability of material, we don't want it to create a delay in our execu tion capability

items.statement: Targeting IPP at ~20% of total revenue mix for long-term annuity revenue; IPP currently contributes 17-18% of revenue
items.quote: As we have earlier in our con-calls also said that we will try to maintain IPP at a level of 20-odd percent of the total revenue mix. The reason is that this is a long-term revenue, and it's a very strong revenue.

items.statement: Data center inquiries ongoing but not yet materialized; utility-scale projects with Coal India, Adani Group, Aditya Birla Group causing billing delays
items.quote: Yes, as a KPI, we are in touch with some of the data center people a nd some sort of inquiries going on. So I think it is a continuous process. As and when it is to be materialized, we will obviously it should be known to all the stakeholders

items.statement: Secured intrastate trading license from GERC and interstate trading license from CERC; energy trading on pilot basis
items.quote: We have also secured both an int rastate trading license from the GERC and interstate trading license from the CERC. And energy trading is being undertaken on a pilot basis, creating wider market access and better realization opportunities

items.statement: Total IPP investment may reach INR5,000-6,000 crore by FY27-28 in phased manner; 565 MW/1,130 MWh BESS project executed, financial closure underway; 142 MW floating solar EPC at Kadana Dam; 150 MW wind for GUVNL (PPA signed, financial closu
items.quote: The total investment migh t go upwards of INR5,000 - 6,000 crore in the asset side as we go forward in '27, '28 . But it will go in a phase- wise manner

items.statement: IPP segment expected to generate >390 crore units annually at full run rate; IPP revenue target >INR1,000 crore in FY28 (conservative), upwards of INR1,000 crore in FY27
items.quote: Our expanding IPP portfolio is expec ted to generate more than 390 crore units annually at a full run rate, strengthening the com pany's recurring revenue base and improving the long-term visibility of earnings

items.statement: Sun Drops IPO planned; promoter increasing stake via warrants (Quyosh purchased shares); promoter holding ~51%+
items.quote: And as you are aware that we are coming with the Sun Drops IPO. So we have a strong order book. And Sun Drops, I think this year on the IPP and the CPP side, if I look at, we will cross INR1,500-odd crore of top line in this year.

items.statement: Geopolitical conditions creating cost hurdles (steel, cables, logistics) and execution delays; seasonality (monsoon) impacts Q2 generation; stabilization period for new IPP plants ~1 year per lenders
items.quote: See if you look at the lender's point of view, they give a stabilizat ion period of 1 year, okay? Now if you see that in spite of stabilization period, in this quarter, we ha ve done 65% of what we have done in the entire last

items.statement: Auditor changed to BDO (top 5 firm) for better governance; promoter stake increasing; institutional investors (Vanguard, Abu Dhabi Investment Fund, Okoworld, pension funds, BlackRock) remain invested
items.quote: we have hired now BDO, which is one of the top 5 as our auditor. So this is a very p ositive action which has been taken to increase the confidence of the stakeholders of th e lenders and everything. And this, I think, will go a long way to increase the -- and at the same time, Promoter is also increasing the stake

items.statement: Kapil Kriplani welcomed as new CFO; Salim Yahoo thanked for contributions and stepping down for personal family commitments
items.quote: At the same time, it gives me great pleasure to welcome Mr. Kapil Kriplani as our new Chief Financial Officer. Kapil brings with him rich experience and deep financial expertise, and we are confident that he will play a key role in supporting the company's next phase of growth and value creation.

items.statement: Online business full-year cumulative growth expected to steady around 25%
items.quote: we'll see growth rates -- full year cumulative growth rates on that business, which will steady at around 25% as far as the online business is concerned.

items.statement: Spencer's offline business growth expected at mid to high single digits
items.quote: I think on the offline business, it will probably be mid to high single digits on the Spencer's offline business.

items.statement: Nature's Basket expected to see early double-digit growth from Q3/Q4 after reset
items.quote: Nature s Basket because, clear ly, last year was not really a very strong year. I would say from quarter 3, quarter 4, we will start seeing early double -digit growth as far as Natures Basket is concerned once we finish the whole reset and the optimization.

items.statement: Internal target to reach Rs. 2,000 sales per square foot in festive quarter
items.quote: I would set the target as reaching to Rs. 2,000 SPSF in the festive quarter, and that is the internal target.

items.statement: Short-term aspiration to reach 7.5% to 8% store EBITDA for Spencer's
items.quote: We are making good progress towards what we have publicly stated our short-term aspiration of reaching to about 7.5 % to 8% store EBITDA.

items.statement: Spencer's delivered 18% YoY and 8% QoQ growth in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Spencer's had a quarterly growth of 18% year -on-year and 8% versus quarter 4 of the last year.

items.statement: Spencer's achieved eighth consecutive month of YoY growth
items.quote: it is the eighth consecutive month where we've been able to deliver growth over the previous year.

items.statement: Offline business grew 14% YoY driven by consumer retention and repeat
items.quote: The offline business also did well, grew at 14%, strong double digit. Again, largely driven with improvement in consumer retention and repeat and frequency.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margins steady at same percentage level, absolute gross margin Rs. 93 crores vs Rs. 86 crores YoY
items.quote: Gross margins were at the same percentage level, at an absolute level, of course, they were higher, Rs. 93 crores at a consolidated level versus Rs. 86 crores in quarter 1 last year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA doubled to Rs. 9.4 crores (2% of sales) vs Rs. 4.7 crores (1% of sales) YoY
items.quote: EBITDA at a consolidated level for the quarter was Rs. 9.4 crores, which is roughly 2% of sales versus Rs. 4.7 crores or 1% of sales in quarter 1 of last year.

items.statement: Spencer's EBITDA Rs. 18 crores (4.4% of sales) vs Rs. 15 crores YoY, excluding non-operating income
items.quote: EBITDA for Spencer's was Rs. 18 crores, which is 4.4% of sales, versus the previous year quarter 1 where it was Rs. 15 crores, but that Rs. 15 crores had a non -operating income of about Rs. 7 crores.

items.statement: Spencer's like-for-like margins steady at 19%
items.quote: If I look for like -for-like, margins are steady at 19%.

items.statement: Nature's Basket margins flat, EBITDA negative Rs. 2.5 crores vs negative Rs. 4.5 crores QoQ
items.quote: Margins were flat. Expenses were marginally lower. And therefore, the financial EBITDA was -- negative Rs. 2.5 crores versus negative Rs. 4.5 crores in quarter 4.

items.statement: No new store openings for Nature's Basket; capex focused on refurbishing existing stores
items.quote: We will spend our limited capex on renovating stores, driving a higher level of throughput. We will not see too many additional stores.

items.statement: No large store addition plan for Spencer's in FY27; only relocations and few stores in existing clusters
items.quote: No, not in this fiscal, we are not ad ding. I mean it's not a large plan. I mean we are opening -- so what we are doing is we are opening stores where we have to kind of relocate a few stores, plus we are trying a couple of stores within existing clusters.

items.statement: Spencer's sales per square foot reached Rs. 1,850, typical of festive quarter levels
items.quote: our sales per square foot is Rs. 1,850 a square foot, which is typically what we get in a festive quarter. We don't get that in quarter 1.

items.statement: Spencer's category mix stable; staples up 100 bps, liquor up 100 bps, non-food down 100 bps, fresh flat
items.quote: Staples has gone up by 100 basis points. Fresh has been the same level. So, it's neither gone up or down. Our contribution, we sell liquor. Liquor has gone up by 100 basis points. And our non -food portfolio which is apparel, E&E and GM has kind of gone down by 100 basis points.

items.statement: Membership program has 125,000+ members (25% of active base), contributing 1/3 of monthly sales
items.quote: Our membership program, which we launched in July of last year, has now -- we've got more than 125,000 members, which is roughly 25% of our active monthly customer base. So, one in four customers are reward members, and they contribute 1/3 of our monthly sales.

items.statement: Members have 2x retention, 3x average monthly spend, and ~5x frequency vs non-members
items.quote: These members have a much higher retention rate. And when I say retention is what percentage of people come back and shop in the next mont h. That's about 2x of what is there for non -members. The average monthly spend by members is also roughly 3x what a non -member would spend. So overall -- and the frequency is almost touching 5, which is, again, 2x of what non-members have.

items.statement: Target 200,000 members shopping at least 5 times a month
items.quote: I would love to have 200,000 members who shop with us at least 5 times a month. That's the number.

items.statement: Focus on continued discipline in working capital allocation and inventory optimization
items.value: discipline in working capital allocation and inventory optimization
items.quote: We are looking at continued discipline when it comes to our working capital allocation and inventory optimization, focusing on availability of the right SKUs.

items.statement: Consolidated debt Rs. 1,266 crores (SRL Rs. 1,019 crores, NBL Rs. 237 crores)
items.quote: So, at a consol level, we have a total debt of Rs. 1,266 crores, SRL is Rs. 1,019 and NBL is Rs. 237.

items.statement: Debt refinancing process started, expected to conclude this month
items.quote: The process has started and it will kind of in the next -- in this month itself, we will get some.

items.statement: Nature's Basket management changed ~45 days ago; complete reset plan initiated
items.quote: We've had a change in management at Nature s Basket about 45 days ago, and we've kind of drawn u p a complete reset plan.

items.statement: Online unit order economics turned positive: Rs. 18 contribution per order vs loss of Rs. 18 YoY
items.quote: Last year, quarter 1, we were making approximately, we were losing Rs. 18 on every order. And now we have actually turned the tide where in quarter 4, we were around Rs.12, now we're making Rs. 18 per order.

items.statement: Online ABV sustained at 780+
items.quote: Our ABVs continue to be 780 plus, which is pretty good.

items.statement: Nature's Basket turnaround depends on execution of inventory availability, assortment focus, and category optimization
items.quote: I would be more focused on what was the year-on-year growth, which was negative. I think we are in the process, like I said, in terms of just resetting a few fundamental basics and those few fundamental basics are more around our own execution.

items.statement: Targets INR 20,000 crore new work orders for FY27, with INR 5,000 crore already received in Q1
items.quote: The company is targeting work orders of around INR 20,000 crore during this year , in addition to the existing order book , out of which approximately INR 5,000 crore has already been received during Q1.

items.statement: Expects top line growth of around 15% and bottom line growth of 15-20% for FY27
items.quote: Further, the company expects its top line to grow by around 15%, while the bottom line is projected to increase by approximately 15 -20%, reflecting continued business momentu m and a positive growth outlook.

items.statement: Order inflow of INR 5,417 crore in Q1 FY27; total order book stands at INR 93,492 crore as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: During the quarter ended April to June 2026, the order inflow stood at INR 5,417 crore. As on June 30, 2026, the company's total order book is stood at an impressive INR 93,492 crore.

items.statement: Order book composition: Railways INR 58,000 crore, S&P INR 12,000 crore, Ports/Roads/Highways INR 3,651 crore, Metros INR 5,700 crore, Power/Transmission INR 4,000 crore, Hydro/Irrigation INR 1,626 crore
items.quote: Order book is primarily driven by railways with INR 58,000 crore, followed by S&P at INR 12,000 crores, ports, roads and highways at INR 3,651 crores, metros at INR 5,700 crores, power and transmission at INR 4,000 crores, and hydro and irrigation projects at INR 1,626 crore.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin improved to 3.99% in Q1 FY27 from 2.08% in Q1 FY26; consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 4.41% from 1.66%
items.quote: Standalone EBITDA stood at INR 171 crore as compared to INR 81 crore in Q1 FY26, which is higher by almost 110% on a YoY basis, while EBITDA margin also improved to 3.99% from 2.08% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Management work margins 8-10%, PMC work ~7%, domestic bidding 5-6%, overseas bidding targeting 15-20%
items.quote: For the last two quarters, we are focusing on the works which give us better margins, and those margins are more than 5-6% for the bidding works. And for management, it is from 8-10%. For PMC work, which we have got from PSU is almost 7%. And we are trying with other state governments and PSUs to get the same PMC margins, fixed margins. For bidding, I will again repeat that our margins will vary f

items.statement: Focusing on port, hydro, highway, and green energy sectors for new orders; targeting INR 20,000-25,000 crore business development for FY27
items.quote: Our target for business development or increasing the order book is almost INR 20,000-25,000 crore for this year, out of which already INR 5,500 crore of works have been entrusted to us. And we are trying in all the sectors. Right now, we are focusing heavily on port sector, hydro, and highway. So, these are the three sectors , and plus green energy also.

items.statement: 42% of railway work awarded on management fee basis; INR 6,500 crore PMC work from NMDC; discussions ongoing with other PSUs
items.quote: It is almost 40%. 42% to be precise , is the railway work, which has been awarded on a management fee basis. And we are also trying with other state government and PSUs to get the work on nomination basis for PMC. And we have already got almost INR 6,500 crore works from a PSU called NMDC.

items.statement: Contracts generally covered by price variation clauses; inflation impact limited though some impact always exists
items.quote: Vishal, generally, all the contracts are covered by price variation, which generally covers the price inflation. So, I think it does not have a very big impact, though some impact is always there.

items.statement: International focus on Central Asia, Middle East, Eastern Europe, Southeast Asia, Africa; bidding for power transmission, railway, road, hydro, metro projects in Africa, Nepal, Israel, Georgia, Serbia
items.quote: RVNL is focused on many parts of the world, and our primary focus is in Central Asia, the Middle East, and Eastern European countries, and Southeast Asia also, in Africa also, and we are in process of bidding in all these areas. And we have submitted bids in parts of Africa for power transmission lines for railway projects, and road projects.

items.statement: Railway receivables outstanding ~INR 2,500 crore; payments received within 30 days of billing; regular follow-up with Railways
items.quote: No. This is actually railway receivable or outstanding is a dynamic process. And presently, our outstanding railway is almost INR 2,500 crores. And we keep on receiving the payment on a monthly basis. We raise our bill to them, and within 30 days, the payment is received.

items.statement: No external debt currently; internal resources sufficient for next 2-3 quarters; working capital lines at 5.5-5.9% if needed
items.quote: Currently, we are not looking for any debt from other sources. We are able to maintain from our internal resources only, but we have our working arrangement s with some banks for working capital if required. So, in next two, three quarters, we are not looking for any assistance on part of that.

items.statement: Dividend policy follows DIPAM guidelines: 30% of PAT or 4% of net worth, whichever is higher
items.quote: We generally follow DIPAM guidelines, which is 30% of the PAT or 4% of the net worth, whichever is higher. So, we'll give that dividend.

items.statement: Key risks: geopolitical situation, labor availability, client payment delays; risk assessment done before quoting overseas projects
items.quote: Definitely. As you know, the present geopolitical situation is a challenge that we faced during Q1 also. And if the similar situation persists, this is a big challenge for us. And definitely, we are facing some challenge of labor availability from the market. Labor is not available for works, we have to make extra effort to get the labor for execution of our works. Payment from the client is also

items.statement: All provisioning for onerous projects completed; no further loss provisions anticipated
items.quote: So, we have already provisioned for the onerous project, and we are not anticipating any further provision of the losses.

items.statement: Revenue per employee increased from INR 4.29 crore to INR 4.97 crore QoQ, reflecting improved operational efficiency
items.quote: During the quarter, employee productivity also showed improvement, with revenue from operations per employee increasing from INR 4.29 crore to INR 4.97 crore on a QoQ basis. This growth reflects enhanced operational efficiency and better utilization of human resources.

items.statement: Rishikesh-Karnaprayag rail project at 78% overall progress, 97% tunnel excavation completed, targeted completion December 2029
items.quote: The Rishikesh-Karnaprayag rail project is also project of national importan ce in Uttarakhand, being developed at a cost of INR 37,000 crore. The 125-kilometer project has achieved 78% overall progress , with around 97% tunnel excavation completed. Targeted for completion by December 2029.

items.statement: Execution to pick up speed as weather improves; priority to convert L1 positions and LOAs into active projects
items.quote: As weather conditions improves over the coming months, our priority will be to pick up execution speed, maintain margin discipline, and convert our healthy pipeline of L1 positions and LOAs into active projects.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected at lower single-digit
items.quote: We are expecting that Q3 and Q4 will be better , so it will be lower single-digit kind of growth this year.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 15-18%
items.quote: Sir, we feel that we should be able to get around 18%. 18% if things go alright otherwise at least 15%, 16% we should be able to continue on a sustainable basis.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 15.4% vs 18.4% YoY
items.quote: We registered EBITDA of INR 39 crores with an EBITDA margin of 15.4% compared with EBITDA of INR 52 crores and EBITDA margin of 18.4% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: One-time export receivable write-off INR 2.5 cr and higher job work charges INR 6 cr impacted operating margin
items.quote: Other expenses included onetime write-off of export receivables of INR 2.5 crores. And secondly, our other expenses also included increased job work charges paid for conversion of raw material that is also higher by around INR 6 crores.

items.statement: Domestic demand subdued due to erratic monsoon impacting paddy herbicide Pretilachlor
items.quote: During the quarter, the industry continued to experience subdued demand conditions, particularly in paddy and other crop protection segments.

items.statement: Pretilachlor demand subdued due to irregular rains damaging crops and delaying sowing
items.quote: Pretilachlor is the key molecule of course is right. But this year the demand has bee n slightly subdued because of the irregular rains across the country

items.statement: EU Technical Equivalence approval for fungicide to add INR 30-40 cr revenue
items.quote: at least we feel that we should be able to get another INR 30 crores, INR 40 crores of revenue from this molecule in European Union in addition to what we are already doing.

items.statement: Hamirpur facility expected INR 50-60 cr revenue in FY27
items.quote: Maybe it's not INR 70 crores to INR 80 crores, but it will be somewhere around INR 50 crores to INR 60 crores. It will be there, no doubt about it.

items.statement: Hamirpur facility long-term potential INR 1,000 cr in 3-4 years
items.quote: Overall potential, sir, when we put up roughly 8 to 10 blocks, we comfortably should get almost INR 1,000 crores from our Hamirpur facility. It will take three to four years from now.

items.statement: Annual capex INR 100 cr across Sandila and Hamirpur
items.quote: Every year we are doing a capex of about INR 100 crores at Sandila and Hamirpur together.

items.statement: Hamirpur capex INR 70-100 cr per year, Sandila INR 25-30 cr for add-up systems
items.value: INR 70 crores to INR 100 crores at Hamirpur and INR 25 crores to INR 30 crores at Sandila
items.quote: The capex we already told that we are doing a capex of INR 70 crores to INR 100 crores per year at Hamirpur facility and we are doing some capex at our Sandila about INR 25 crores to INR 30 crores for our add up systems there.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization around 70%
items.quote: Our capacity utilization currently is around 70%.

items.statement: Hamirpur 2 of 10 blocks operational, adding herbicide and fungicide blocks
items.quote: Development at our Hamirpur facility continues to progress as planned with 2 out of 10 blocks currently operational. The facility provides a clear pathway for future capacity expansion and will support incremental growth opportunities across specialty products.

items.statement: New fungicide production at Sandila using existing plant with INR 2-3 cr balancing equipment
items.quote: We are trying to adjust it in the existing with some balancing equipment. We will not put a whole new plant for this. In the existing plant, we will have to put a little balancing of INR 2 crores, INR 3 crores and with that we will be able to produce this so that our overall capacity utilization will improve.

items.statement: Plan to launch 3 new products in FY27 including fungicide and herbicides
items.quote: Yes, 3. Including what we already produced, 3 products.

items.statement: New fungicide import substitution targeting 2,000 tons of 4,000-5,000 ton market at INR 500-600/kg
items.value: 2,000 tons capacity, INR 500 to INR 600 per kg
items.quote: we are trying our best. And the import what we saw from the data last year, it is around 4,000 tons to 5,000 tons and we should be able to get from this at least 2,000 tons of our capacity. Yogansh Jeswani: And what would be the price of this molecule, sir? D. K. Jain: Price is about INR 500 to INR 600 per

items.statement: Q1 FY27 volume down 13%, price up 4% YoY
items.quote: Volume decline was around 13% and price rise was around 4%.

items.statement: Raw material prices moderated, finished goods prices also moderated
items.quote: Currently, the raw material prices has gone down as well as finished goods prices have moderated. So we are confident that we will be able to make reasonable margins in this quarter.

items.statement: Inventory days increased to 200 from 170, expected to normalize to 170 by Q3
items.quote: Inventory days have gone up from 170 days to around 200 days. They will come down in Q3 to around 170 days.

items.statement: Receivable days stable at 120 days
items.quote: Our receivable days has been around 120 days. So that will remain at 120 days.

items.statement: No term loans planned, capex funded through internal accruals
items.quote: Our object has been not to take any term loan in India Pesticide for its expansion and we have already a very healthy cash balance . So we will be funding our capex through internal accruals only.

items.statement: Received EU Technical Equivalence approval for fungicide product
items.quote: A key milestone during the quarter was the receipt of Technical Equivalence approval from the European Union for one of our fu ngicide products

items.statement: Export revenue INR 89 cr (35% of total), slightly higher YoY
items.quote: Export revenue during FY27 quarter 1 was at INR 89 crores contributing approximately 35% of total revenue.

items.statement: EU approval sales expected to commence from November
items.quote: Sales should commence most probably from November onwards because they will take some time because what happens once, we get equivalent, they have to add that as a source.

items.statement: Facing Chinese import price pressure, improving operational efficiency and R&D to compete
items.quote: Of course we know that the market has become very competitive and Chinese products are coming at relatively much lower prices. So we are trying to improve our operational efficiency and trying to compete with Chinese imports and that is where our R&D team is working regularly to optimize further the process conditions and we are also optimizing in engineering to reduce the overall project cost.

items.statement: Erratic monsoon creating demand uncertainty, but long-term strategy intact
items.quote: Sir, as of today, it is going on like this. very well the overall situation of the monsoon and erratic monsoon is there, but it is very erratic. So that's why it is disturbing a lot. Maybe this quarter can be a bit subdued but I think there should be some improvement in the future. But long term strategy point of view, we are intact.

items.statement: Expect to submit SFB operational readiness to RBI by end of Q4 FY27 within 18-month timeline from Dec 2025
items.quote: We continue to expect that all required milestones will be completed within the prescribed 18-month timeline, and we remain on course to submit our readiness to the Reserve Bank of India by end of Quarter 4 FY27.

items.statement: Technology stack for end-to-end customer loan journey expected ready by Feb 2027
items.quote: Technology stack for the end-to-end customer loan journey is under development and is expected to be ready by Feb '27.

items.statement: B2B UPI P2M segment relaunch tentatively in Q4 FY27 depending on ecosystem developments
items.quote: We are preparing to relaunch our high-growth B2B UPI P2M segment. However, this would depend on the ecosystem and other developments, which could result in the relaunch tentatively in Quarter 4 FY27.

items.statement: Expect blended portfolio yield of around 14% for SFB secured lending portfolio
items.quote: And second, what we are looking at is 90% secured book of lending for our SFB portfolio with an average portfolio yield of around 14%.

items.statement: Expect NIMs in range of 8% to 9% for SFB, highest in industry
items.quote: So from an SFB perspective, with the kind of asset products which we are looking at, we expect our NIMs, and that may not answer your ROE question fully, but at least NIMs, which is highest in the industry, which we are looking at anywhere in the range of 8% to 9%.

items.statement: Anticipate INR 10 crores SFB-related opex impact on FY27 P&L
items.quote: So, in terms of the burden on opex this year, we are anticipating anything around INR10 crores on this year's P&L in terms of the SFB opex which includes hiring, which includes all the other related opex for the bank.

items.statement: Plan to open 40 new branches in year 1 of SFB operations
items.quote: So we intend to open in year 1, 40 new branches as well, and that is part of our plan as well.

items.statement: Target credit-deposit ratio of around 70% and CASA ratio of around 65% for SFB
items.quote: One is the credit deposit ratio, we are looking at around 70%. So we are not looking at aggressive lending book right now as per the plan for the first 3 years. That is one. Second, we are looking at, as Ketan mentioned, our core book is stable. So 90% of our current CASA is the core. So we are looking at a CASA ratio of around 65%.

items.statement: Referral loan disbursements surged 214% YoY to INR 628 crores in Q1 FY27, nearly 50% of FY26 total
items.quote: Referral loan disbursals surged 214% on year-on-year to INR 628 crores, nearly 50% of the total disbursals in FY26, indicating growing demand for credit in our banking ecosystem and our target customer segment.

items.statement: Digitally active customers increased 22% YoY to 64.6 lakhs, FinoPay app customers grew 38% to 8.4 lakhs
items.quote: Digitally active customer s increased by 22% year -on-year to 64.6 lakhs, while active FinoPay, which is our app customers, grew even faster at 38% to 8.4 lakhs

items.statement: UPI throughput grew 14% YoY to INR 60,000 crores, digitally active customers for June 2026 at 65 lakhs
items.value: INR 60,000 crores UPI throughput, 65 lakhs digitally active
items.quote: UPI throughput grew 14% year-on-year to INR 60,000 crores and digitally active customers for the month of June '26 stood at 65 lakhs, a significant growth of 22% year-on-year compared to June '25.

items.statement: Net revenue margin expanded to highest quarterly value of 42.8%, up 275 bps sequentially and 925 bps YoY
items.quote: One of the key highlights for the quarter was a continued improvement in our net revenue margin. Despite lower revenues, our net revenue margin expanded to its highest quarterly value of 42.8%, improving 275 basis points sequentially and 925 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Added 8.4 lakh new accounts in Q1 FY27, total account base 1.83 crore, merchant network ~20 lakh
items.quote: Customer acquisition remained healthy, and we added 8.4 lakh new accounts in this quarter, taking our total account base to 1.83 crore. Our merchant network, which is close to around 20 lakh continues to be one of the biggest competitive strengths.

items.statement: Large part of technology investment done with Finacle core banking migration, adding lending modules (LOS, LMS) for SFB
items.quote: In terms of the investment, yes, a large part of investment is already done by moving the core banking from FIS Global to Finacle. We have to add a few modules relating to our lending business, which is like LOS, LMS other related modules in terms of the technology.

items.statement: Technology transition for SFB first 3 phases expected complete by end of FY27
items.quote: And as you rightly said, after FY27, we should be completed by our entire technology transition in terms of the SFB as well, at least for the first 3 phases of our SFB.

items.statement: Appointed PwC for SFB implementation and operational readiness, onboarded technology partners for LOS, LMS and lending applications
items.quote: We have appointed PricewaterhouseCoopers to support the implementation and overall operational readiness of SFB. We have also onboarded technology partners for our loan origination system, loan management system and other lending applications that will for m the backbone of our lending platform

items.statement: RBI stipulated 18-month timeline from Dec 5, 2025 (ends June 5, 2027) for SFB transition, must submit operational readiness before that
items.quote: RBI has given us 18 months on 5th December 2025, which ends on 5th June 2027. Before that, we need to submit an application to RBI showing that we are operationally ready to launch the SFB.

items.statement: Current FY30 plan is organic, but will evaluate inorganic opportunities to accelerate lending and digital capabilities if they arise
items.quote: As regards to the inorganic opportunities in terms of acquisition, etc., with our kind of a liability franchise, we will keep our eyes and ears open. And if anything interesting comes across, we will be looking at it as and when it comes and if at all, it comes through. So at current stage, our plan, which we have put for our FY30 is an organic plan.

items.statement: B2B UPI P2M business paused since Feb 2026 event, will take at least couple of quarters for relaunch
items.quote: Besides the event of Feb '26, one of our most profitable B2B business has been paused for recalibration, and it will take at least next couple of quarters for the relaunch.

items.statement: Traditional transaction business (remittance, micro ATM, AePS) saw 13% sequential revenue decline due to digital adoption headwinds
items.quote: Our traditional transaction business, which forms of remittance, micro ATM, AePS saw 13% sequential revenue decline as it continued to face industry headwinds due to grow ing digital adoption in Bharat

items.statement: Fee-based income contributes over 75% of revenue, stood at INR 234 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our USP, the existing fee-based income, which contributes over 75% of the revenue stood at INR 234 crores in Q1 FY27, and it remains our distinct advantage over other SFBs once we transit.

items.statement: Revenue target of Rs. 1,000 crores for FY27 and EBITDA margin guidance of 33-35% reiterated
items.quote: In summary, we would like to reiterate that our trajectory towards the Rs. 1,000 crores revenue by FY '27 remains firmly on track, supported by a robust product pipeline and a sustained demand across key therapeutic segments including anesthetics, anti-diabetics, anti-anxiety, vitamins, and ADHD. We remain confident of our guidance of EBITDA margins in the range of 33% to 35%.

items.statement: CAGR of about 20% year-on-year expected to continue beyond FY27
items.quote: So, we have already said that we would be growing at a CAGR of about 20% year-on-year. I think the same trend would continue.

items.statement: Strong demand in Q1 but water shortage deferred Rs. 35 crores of sales
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter stood at Rs. 190 crores, reflecting a 31% year-on-year growth. Demand remained strong during the quarter, but water shortages led to a deferment of sales of around Rs. 35 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 25% in Q1 FY27, down 8.1% YoY due to water shortage and solar policy change impacting Rs. 8 crores
items.quote: During the quarter, EBITDA stood at Rs. 47 crores, a decline of 8.1% year -on-year with EBITDA margins at 25%. Before we move forward, let me explain the reasons for the decline in margins during the quarter. It was a combination of factors that coincided during the period and are mostly temporary in nature.

items.statement: Excluding one-off impacts, margins would have been within guided 33-35% range
items.quote: Excluding these one-off impacts, margins would have remained within our guided range. We believe these are temporary disruptions and with operations stabilizing, we expect performance to improve in the coming quarters while remaining firmly on track to achieve our FY '27 growth and margin objectives.

items.statement: Solar policy change increased fuel and power costs by Rs. 8 crores at EBITDA level in Q1
items.quote: Second, Maharashtra government changed the solar power policy, which led to increased fuel and power costs during the quarter. This alone had an impact of Rs. 8 crores at EBITDA levels.

items.statement: Retrospective solar subsidy payment of Rs. 4.5-5 crores is one-time; ongoing power cost increases will be passed to customers
items.quote: See, this would be somewhere around Rs. 4.5 crores - Rs. 5 crores at this stage. So, in fact, the matter is also sub judice. There is a case which is running on around in that wherein all the Solar Power Association members have come around, and they have filed a case against the MSEDCL.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex of Rs. 16.58 crores for maintenance, smaller projects, formulation plan and Isambe project
items.quote: Our CapEx for Q1 FY '27 stood at Rs. 16.58 crores driven by spend on maintenance CapEx, smaller projects, formulation plan requirements and Isambe project.

items.statement: Patalganga Phase-1 capex earmarked at Rs. 200 crores for two API advanced intermediate blocks and two formulation blocks
items.quote: On Patalganga land, as our Joint MD has updated, we have received all necessary clearances and will be developing the facility in phases. The project will include two API but advanced intermediate blocks and two formulation blocks. The total CapEx earmarked for this facility is around Rs. 200 crores for Phase-1.

items.statement: Boundary wall construction started at Patalganga; API blocks with utilities to be built first, targeting 40% completion in ~2.5 years per MIDC norms
items.quote: We would be looking at the API block to start with. That would be the first thing which we would be building along with the utility blocks. I think these would be the ones which would be coming up for Rs. 200 crores. I don't think formulation can start immediately. Say, right from the acquisition, around 2.5 years, we should have a 40% completion as per MIDC.

items.statement: Block F at Lote not started yet; will begin in next couple of quarters
items.quote: We haven't started it yet. We will be starting it in next couple of quarters.

items.quote: We launched two new anesthetic liquid inhalation products in Q2 FY '27 from our Ambernath facility and we expect them to scale up over the coming quarters. On the contrast media opportunity, we remain on track with development and continue to progress as planned. We

items.quote: Our cardiovascular product launched in Q3 FY '26 has ramped up well. The ADHD product continues to scale up, supported by healthy demand from LATAM and Europe and we expect the momentum to continue. Our liquid anesthetic product remains on track with steady monthly supplies.

items.statement: EU audit for Ambernath facility scheduled for second half of November
items.quote: So, we have already received the dates for audit from EU at Ambernath facility. The audit is scheduled for the second half of November.

items.statement: Close to signing term sheet for large anesthetic CDMO contract; qualification and quality approvals completed
items.quote: We have made good progress specifically on one of the large anesthetic CDMO contract that we are looking at. We are very close to signing a term sheet. items.statement: DSM vitamin project at stable peak volumes; pharma validation completed; dedicated facility operational
items.quote: Yes, we have. So, I think DSM has now reached a very stable state where we are very close to their peak volumes. Pharma validation is completed. Like I mentioned in the previous calls, we have set up now a dedicated facility for DSM. So, that is now up and running. So, things are moving very positively in the DSM project.

items.statement: Exports 81% of revenue in Q1 FY27; Asia 39%, Europe 35%, LATAM 20%
items.quote: Exports continued to be a key growth driver contributing 81% of revenue in Q1 FY '27. Within exports, Asia contributed 39%, followed by Europe at 35% and LATAM at 20%.

items.statement: North America exposure small (~3%); Europe and LATAM remain largest markets; limited tariff impact currently

items.quote: On borrowings, we would like to report that for the full year, we have not utilized any working capital limits, except for letter of credits and bank guarantees.

items.quote: Somewhere around Rs. 230 crores to Rs. 240 crores. It is on the higher side. items.quote: Cash reserves. See, we have around Rs. 150 crores in FDs and mutual funds.

items.quote: So, as we speak in the last, I think, two, three years, our R&D strength has gone from, about 20-30 to almost 70 people now. So, we have added people in R&D and we have also added new verticals like finished formulation in our R&D.

items.statement: SAP implementation underway, going live in 4-5 months; TrackWise QMS software implemented; automation at site level including gravity flow and DCS systems
items.quote: As we speak, we are actually under SAP implementation, so we will be live in another four to five months, we should be live with our SAP, which will further strengthen our internal system. items.quote: Ambernath alone I think would contribute somewhere around Rs. 14 crores to Rs. 15 crores on depreciation. So, that you can add up to a regular I think should be somewhere around nearing to Rs. 35 crores to Rs. 40 crores should be the overall depreciation.
