items.quote: Our policy count up to Q1 now has touched 3.1 crores.

items.statement: Claims settled exceeded INR 26 crores with 1.5 lakh+ servicing requests handled in Q1 FY27
items.quote: During Q1, we helped policyholders settle claims amounting to more than INR 26 crores, there would have been some complexity delay or rejection. We handled around 1.5 lakh plus unique servicing requests during this quarter.

items.statement: Take rates remain stable; revenue mix shift toward renewables drives margin expansion
items.quote: Take rates are more or less similar of what it was before.

items.statement: AI handles 55% of support tickets; 2M documents processed via AI; 75% of new code AI-generated in Q1 FY27
items.quote: AI also now handles 55% of our support tickets. Nearly 2 million documents were fully processed using AI last quarter. AI not just is improving efficiency, but also it improves customer experience.

items.statement: Voice AI renewal calls achieve 500 bps higher renewal rates vs non-AI calls
items.quote: These AI-called customers show a renewal rate that is higher by 500 basis points, primarily due to stronger follow ups and use of local language by the AI.

items.statement: Turnaround times reduced 50-60% across processes through AI adoption
items.quote: Across various processes, we have seen our tATs reduced by 50-60%.

items.statement: Cross-sell activation: motor-only DPs selling health grew 40%+ YoY
items.quote: we have been able to grow motor -only digital partners starting to sell health by 40 plus percent

items.statement: Supreme Court TP reserving judgment impact uncertain; insurers await GIC appeal outcome before provisioning
items.quote: Other insurance companies are waiting for the GIC's appeal (GI counsel's appeal) in the Supreme Court and waiting to hear the outcome of it before they look at their provisioning.

items.statement: Potential fuel denial for uninsured vehicles could create massive demand tailwind as seen with 2019 two-wheeler fines
items.quote: What we have seen in the past is when th is two-wheeler fines were implemented in 2019, the awareness of this requirement for a TP policy goes up significantly and the demand shoots up

items.statement: Disciplined cash management keeps cash conversion from profitability very high
items.quote: Disciplined in cash management and working capital management that keeps our cash conversion from profitability very high.

items.statement: ESOP cost modest at INR 7 crores in Q1 FY27; minimal gap between adjusted EBITDA and PAT
items.quote: Our ESOP costs are modest, which I guided for this quarter, for example, the ESOP cost is about INR 7 crores and that's it.

items.statement: DP attrition stable: 28-30% in first 24 months, then 2-3%; 65% retention at year 5-6
items.quote: Basically, over the years, we know that in the first 18 months, there is a learning curve. And you see some attrition of about 28 -30% in the first 24 months. Then the attrition rate drops to 2-3% where basically 95% of the people after 18 months retain on the platform.

items.statement: Commission regulation changes speculative; health GST commission reset passed through but volumes grew
items.quote: The way we had operated that time was whatever reset happened in the market, that reset was passed down, but we also saw increase in the volume in terms of how much business started happening on the platform, and that led to growth in both the categories of product that were impacted life and health.

items.statement: Management expects 35% top-line and EBITDA growth in FY27 versus FY26, with similar growth continuing in FY28 and FY29
items.quote: I think we're expecting 35% growth in our top line in this financial year. And similarly, EBITDA also, we'll see the same growth coming up in this financial year as compared to last financial year.

items.statement: Management expects at least 30% top-line and bottom-line growth in FY27 and FY28, with visible growth through FY29
items.quote: Both for top line and bottom line, you can expect a decent growth, 30% plus in coming year. And same growth will continue in FY28 also because these capex's, what are coming on a stream, this year where 2 have come on stream, 1 is coming up in the first half.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margin was 15.5% in Q1 FY27; management expects 14%+ EBITDA margin for full FY27
items.quote: As of now, what we can perceive that, that will happen. But if things remain as good as they are currently and no untoward incident happens on the geopolitical front, we'll give you better results than this.

items.statement: Management confident of holding current margins throughout the year despite potential price corrections
items.quote: We are confident that we will hold those margins throughout the year.

items.statement: Capex cycle for FY27 is ~75% complete; remaining new capex estimated at USD 80-100 million for FY27-28
items.quote: From this, you can see our capex cycle for this financial year is almost 75% done. And whatever capex's are remaining, which are new capex's of around, if you put total all this will be around USD 100 million or less USD 80 million capex, we'll be doing going forward.

items.statement: Noida 39,000 MT recycling plant commissioned April 30, 2026; Mexico 80M unit WPP bags plant commissioned July 31, 2026; Egypt 12B pack Aseptic plant on schedule for H1 FY27 commissioning
items.quote: 39,000 metric tons per annum recycling plant at Noida Sector 155 was successfully commissioned on April 30, 2026. 80-million-unit WPP bags plant in Mexico was commissioned on July 31, 2026. Work on our Greenfield Aseptic project in Egypt, 12 billion packs remain on schedule for commissioning in FY27.

items.statement: Egypt Aseptic plant targeting 30% utilization (2B packs) in first year, 60-70% in second year, 100% by third year
items.quote: Out of 12 billion packs, which is the annual capacity, we can do 30% in first year. Second year, certainly, we'll reach around 60% to 70%. And third year, we'll reach around 100% capacity there.

items.statement: Management expects to double volumes from current ~173,000 MT to ~346,000 MT by FY29 as new capacities ramp up
items.quote: If you add up the capacities what are coming up, if I can add up, we should double our quantity in next 3 years' time.

items.statement: BOPP prices up 25-32% and BOPET prices up 30-35% from February 2026 levels; prices currently stable with no major correction expected while West Asia crisis continues
items.quote: BOPP prices have gone up by 25%, and BOPET prices have gone up by almost 30%-35% from, to be specific from February '26 level to now, it is 25-32% higher on BOPP and BOPET rate is around 30-35% higher.

items.statement: Raw material prices rising but less than finished goods prices; spreads normalizing
items.quote: See raw material prices are also moving up, but not to that extent what the finished good prices are moving up because it is being normalized now and prices are, I think, getting normalized as of now.

items.statement: Overseas operations drove 80% of incremental revenue; Egypt, Mexico, Nigeria and India PET chips key profitability drivers
items.quote: With 80% incremental revenue contributed by overseas operations and 20% by India, our incremental revenue was RS. 14,753 million in Q1.

items.statement: Americas volumes up 18% YoY supported by US onshoring push; Middle East & Africa up 14.9% YoY on supply chain derisking; Europe flat YoY with seasonal moderation expected next quarter
items.quote: Americas sales volume increased 18% Y-o-Y to 31,724 metric tons. This was supported by the U.S. government push for domestic production and onshoring amid evolving trade policies.

items.statement: Strategic shift to high-margin products in India flexible packaging; Aseptic volumes soft due to duty-free imports but value growth maintained; 60-70% of future capex allocated to value-added products
items.quote: Whatever capex we do going forward, at least 60% to 70% will go into value-added products only and balance can go into maintenance or regular products.

items.statement: Debt/EBITDA reduced from 4.5x in FY26 to 3.5x in Q1 FY27; targeting below 3x by FY28 as capacities reach full utilization
items.quote: Our Debt-EBITDA margin was around 4.5x, which you would see in this quarter itself, it has come down to 3.5. And going forward also, we'll ensure that we retain the same kind of leverage what we have as of now. And this leverage will come down by end of FY28 much lower once all these capacities, what are not utilized to the 100% becomes 100% capacity utilization, then you will see our leverage goi

items.statement: Interest cost reduced 0.3-0.4% in Q1; targeting further 1% reduction over next year
items.quote: we should reduce our interest costs by 1% in next 1 years' time. And you will see that even if you reduce by 1% going forward, there will Q1 FY27 EARNINGS CONFERENCE CALL: AUGUST 17, 2026 Page 23 | 25 be a great reduction. That's why you can see the reduction of 0.3% -0.4% in this quarter itself

items.statement: Company does not carry significant inventory due to price volatility; pricing gains passed through to customers
items.quote: In our business, we don't carry much inventory in our books of accounts because prices fluctuate too often here. Whatever gain you are seeing in our volume as well as in our prices, they are the prices which have been passed on to the customers.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue grew 38% YoY to Rs. 53,972 million; EBITDA rose 92% YoY to Rs. 9,198 million with margin expanding 480 bps to 17% (highest in 21 quarters)
items.quote: Consolidated revenue for Q1 FY27 grew 38% Y-o-Y to Rs. 53,972 million. EBITDA rose 92% Y-o-Y to Rs. 9,198 million with EBITDA margin expanding 480 basis points Y-o-Y to 17%, marking our highest EBITDA performance in the last 21 quarters.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA (ex forex derivatives) grew 78% YoY to Rs. 8,373 million at 15.5% margin; PAT Rs. 4,233 million at 7.8% net margin vs 1.5% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Normalized EBITDA post adjustment of Rs. 825 million on forex derivative transactions reached Rs. 8,373 million, which is 78% growth year-on-year, expanded to 15.5%.

items.statement: Overseas customers prefer local/regional sourcing to derisk supply chains; UFlex's geographic diversification and integrated model commands premium pricing
items.quote: We are derisking our top-line model in such a way that where we are present at least 75% of our turnover should come from near to our customer policy, that is what we are adopting.

items.statement: Aseptic packaging facing duty-free imports from Indonesia under trade treaty; India consumer market growing 5-8% annually supporting long-term demand
items.quote: What has happened in Aseptic, we are getting a lot of duty-free imports from Indonesia, where India has signed a treaty where duty-free imports keep on coming. But Indian consumer market is growing at least 5% to 8% each year now.

items.statement: Articles of association amended to include paper, electronics, software, hardware, infra to enable commercialization of R&D in value-added packaging products
items.quote: We are also adding the value-added products now, which can be paper, which can be other materials, so just to enable that whatever R&D is doing, and it should not remain in the R&D, it should come as a commercial thing for us, so we are enabling those things.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks (West Asia crisis, Bab-el-Mandeb) could disrupt shipping; quarter-on-quarter fluctuations possible due to shipment timing; no major price correction expected while crisis continues
items.quote: But if everything normalizes, you may see some correction in the prices, but our raw material sourcing and our finished selling prices will have the same margin what we have now, so we are not much concerned on the pricing front.

items.statement: Management prioritizes wealth creation through growth over buybacks; surplus cash to go toward debt reduction; no dividend/buyback guidance given
items.quote: Our policy is that we should reward shareholders by increasing their wealth, which you see in the next 3 years, I think wealth creation will happen, so that shareholders will not have any point to complain about that.

items.statement: No management changes or key hires mentioned; focus on operational execution across geographies
items.quote: Building on the momentum established in Q4 FY26, this performance reflects the resilience of our integrated global business model and operational execution.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected around 20% for FY27, higher than previous 12% guidance
items.quote: See, 27% is obviously very good growth, but we expect the revenue growth to be in the range close to 20%, right, much better than the 12% guidance we had given earlier, around 20% something.

items.statement: EBITDA margin around 17% considered normalized and expected to sustain for next 2 years
items.quote: Lastly, this 17% margin that we are seeing, this is a largely normalized margin, right? This is the range in which we expect the margin to be for the next 2 years or so, right? Shailesh Sharma: Yes, this is what we expect

items.statement: Capex of INR 170-180 crore planned for FY27, part of INR 500 crore total capex largely completing by FY28
items.quote: See this plan, I wouldn't right now comment on the capex for Q1, but it's largely this year, we are expecting to have a capex of about INR170 - 180 crores at least in the current financial year.

items.statement: Capacity expansion underway via cycle time improvements (5 million pieces unlocked) and new channels at Haridwar factory
items.quote: We have already unlocked about 5 million pieces this year by doing some technological upgradation of our assets, which are in ramping up stage. On top of it, we are also putting channels in our Haridwar factory.

items.statement: OEM sales mix: 2-wheeler ~54%, passenger vehicle ~31%, commercial vehicle ~15% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: So our OEM basically, it contributes about 62%, as you have seen it, out of which our 2-wheeler is about 54%, passenger vehicle is around 31% and commercial vehicle is about 15%.

items.statement: Vehicle aftermarket volumes plateaued or slightly declining; new strategy over next 5 months to recover volumes
items.quote: So vehicle aftermarket business has a certain different set of challenges. So far, it's kind of plateau or a small decline in our revenue. The next 5 months, we have some different strategy to cover up or recover our volume.

items.statement: OEM contracts have commodity inflation pass-through clauses; current round of price negotiations work in progress with 1-2 quarter lag
items.quote: On price and commodity inflation, if you see our OEM contracts usually have a clause around the commodity inflation linked to the index in which we keep working along with the OEMs. And even currently, it's the work in progress for the recent round of commodity inflation.

items.statement: Gross margin 1% lower YoY but 6.5% higher QoQ due to mix and inventory revaluation (FIFO); 51% in Q1 vs 42.5% in Q4
items.quote: Our gross margin for the quarter is about 1% lower year-on-year while quarter-on-quarter is higher by about 6.5%. This variance in gross margin from previous quarter is a composite impact of price, mix and inflation.

items.statement: EV bearing programs in development phase; full production ramp-up expected mid-2027 with revenue visibility in 2028
items.quote: These are the businesses that will come on stream during 2028, more precisely towards the last quarter of the calendar year, 2028.

items.statement: Haridwar capex primarily for 2-wheeler traction motors and some driveline; reduces dependency on industrial sourcing
items.quote: I would say much of the investments that are happening in Haridwar primarily for the 2-wheelers, I would say, to begin with and some of the driveline, as you were asking previous question, a little bit of that, but majorly it is for the traction motors coming for the 2-wheelers.

items.statement: Sales to SKF Industrial not a growth priority; expected to decline over next few years as capacity shifts to automotive
items.quote: As far as the volume is concerned, as Shailesh mentioned, it's not a priority for growth. This is something which over the next few years is expected to come down. And we focus that capacity towards serving our automotive customers.

items.statement: All three plants achieved >98% renewable energy sourcing; Bangalore and Haridwar sites water positive (2x and 2.57x)
items.quote: Now our all the 3 plants have been achieved more than 98% renewable energy sourcing. And group has given the certificate as decarbonized plant for all the 3 plants of SK India Limited, Pune, Bangalore and Haridwar.

items.statement: Aftermarket discounts given in last 2 months will not continue; no further price mix decline expected
items.quote: We needed to give some discount in last 2 months, but which will not be continued now. So there will be no decline in price mix.

items.statement: Portfolio rationalization involves factory-level portfolio shifts for economies of scale and exiting unprofitable businesses; no major FY27 impact
items.quote: One is what we make and where we make. We have 3 factories. So to use economy of scale and bring some synergy, we just change our portfolio in different factories. That is one part of it. Another is, of course, our sales mix where there are certain businesses which are kind of not so profitable or loss makers, we would like to do something about it.

items.statement: Exports at 8% of sales; not a strategic focus, expected to remain in current range
items.quote: So our main focus is on our domestic demand. Export is not a very big pie of our strategy also as of now. So it will remain in this range only.

items.statement: Gross margin fluctuations within normal historical range due to commodity pass-through lag of 1-2 quarters and mix changes
items.quote: See, even historically, this has been the normal gross margin range, right? It could be based on the mix or certain timing gap, due to which there could be certain movements within quarter because even what happens is when you see the commodity inflation realization, it doesn't happen immediately in the same quarter, right?

items.statement: Commodity cost pressure expected to peak in Q2 FY27, with softening from Q3 and turnaround in Q4 FY27
items.period: Q2 FY27, Q3 FY27, Q4 FY27
items.quote: Respite from that we think will come in Q3 and Q4 only. So it will be a challenging quarter, but then we are accelerating a few things internally, looking again at those levers that I just described, product mix and business mix.

items.statement: Industry MHCV growth expected at high single digit for full year FY27; LCV outlook slightly better
items.quote: even if we take a conservative outlook for the second half of the year, let us say, October, November onwards, we still believe that the industry has potential to grow by high single digit. This is for MHCV. And for LCV, the LCV outlook is actually slightly better than this, yes.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA flat at INR970 crore, margin 10.1%, down 100 bps YoY due to rising material costs
items.quote: Despite record revenues, the EBITDA was flat at INR970 crores as compared to same quarter last year. EBITDA margin was 10.1%, 100 basis points lower on Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Material cost at 71.5% of revenue in Q1 FY27, up 90 bps YoY but flat sequentially; inventory absorption and cost savings offset half of commodity impact
items.quote: As a percentage of revenue, the material cost stood at 71.5% for the quarter, higher by 90 basis points Y-o-Y, but in line with Q4.

items.statement: Price increase of 1.2%-1.25% taken in Q1 FY27; additional hikes in July: >1% MHCV, >2% LCV; cumulative FY27 hikes ~2.25% MHCV, >3.5% LCV
items.quote: Price increase during the quarter was about 1.2% - 1.25%. That also helped us in negating the commodity cost increases.

items.statement: Domestic MHCV industry grew 13% YoY in Q1 FY27; LCV VAHAN industry grew 17% YoY; June and July MHCV industry growth >20% YoY
items.quote: Overall, in Q1, the domestic MHCV industry volume grew by 13% on Y-o-Y basis, while the domestic LCV VAHAN industry grew by 17%.

items.statement: Switch Mobility order book at 2,100 e-buses after 650-bus order; delivered 225 e-buses and ~300 e-LCVs in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our EV subsidiary, Switch Mobility India, recently bagged an order of 650 electric buses. With this, Switch Mobility has a healthy order book of 2,100 e-buses.

items.statement: Hinduja Leyland Finance AUM grew 20% YoY to INR60,310 crore; Hinduja Housing Finance AUM grew 13% YoY to INR16,157 crore
items.quote: Hinduja Leyland Finance, our vehicle financing subsidiary, delivered robust growth in the quarter with its AUM expanding by 20% year-on-year to INR60,310 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex INR153 crore; full-year FY27 capex expected to continue in INR900-1,000 crore range and increase over next 2-3 years
items.quote: Capex for the quarter was at INR153 crores. New products, including future technology development, alternate powertrain technologies and EVs remain the focus areas for the new capex.

items.statement: RAK UAE plant halted in April-May, produced 600 units in June, targeting 700 in July, 800 in August; Saudi plant timeline accelerated from 18-24 months
items.quote: last month, we did 600 units there. This month, we are expecting to do 700. And next month, we will come to our peak production of 800.

items.statement: Launched industry-first air suspension in multi-axle trucks; HIPPO tractors and TAURUS tippers gaining momentum; focus on premiumization and higher horsepower segments
items.quote: the highlight of the quarter was introduction of new air suspension technology in multi-axle trucks, which is an industry first and provides our customers industry best payload

items.statement: Added 33 touch points in Q1 FY27; total network 2,137 (1,177 MHCV, 960 LCV); North market share improved from ~15% to ~27% over 4-5 years
items.quote: During the quarter, we added 33 touch points in our MHCV and LCV businesses. The focus of new additions continues in North and East region, where we have a higher headroom.

items.statement: Air suspension launch not a reactive move; project started 2.5-3 years ago; offers 4-ton extra payload vs competitor's 2-ton; expect competitors to follow in 6-12 months
items.quote: this is not like a quick reaction response from our side. This project was started about 2.5, 3 years ago. And now fortunately, when this launch happened, we were quite ready with this new product.

items.statement: BS7 implementation not expected before 2031-2032; regulatory burden high but focus on positive TCO impact for customers; AC mandate example shows customer acceptance of value
items.quote: my personal opinion is BS7, we should not see in India in CV before 2031, and it could also be 2032.

items.statement: Optare debt GBP 50 million remaining; plan to repay GBP 25 million in FY27 and GBP 25 million in FY28 to avoid interest cost
items.quote: We had debt of about GBP 80 million. We paid about GBP 30 million last year. And now we have about GBP 50 million debt, which is there, and we don't want to incur interest cost.

items.statement: HLF and HHF consolidated net NPAs at 2.1% on book basis; HLF pre-provisioning operating profit up 56% YoY to INR587 crore, PAT up 37% to INR123 crore
items.quote: Both HLF and HHF maintained healthy asset quality with consolidated net NPAs at 2.1% on book basis.

items.statement: Opening inventory 6,500 vehicles, increased to 8,500 at Q1 end; absorbed one-fifth to one-fourth of commodity cost increases via inventory; overheads also capitalized
items.quote: For us, we carried about 6,500 vehicles at the opening level. And again, this 6,500 level of stock at the opening level, it got increased to about 8,500 level as at the quarter end.

items.statement: Manpower cost to increase 4-5% QoQ in Q2 FY27 due to July increment cycle; centralized commercial negotiation team created to control admin overheads >INR50 lakh
items.quote: you will see a marginal increase in the manpower cost because our increment cycle, it starts from July of every year, every financial year, so you will see a marginal 4%, 5% increase in the manpower cost over the previous quarter.

items.statement: Key risks: elevated commodity prices (steel, natural rubber), regulatory cost increases; mitigation via price hikes, cost savings (Achieve 2K project), mix improvement, inventory management
items.quote: We remain mindful of the key risks, particularly the elevated commodity prices, but shall continue to put all efforts to achieve better price realization and mix, higher cost savings and enhanced operational discipline.

items.statement: Net cash position strengthened to INR2,252 crore, up INR1,431 crore YoY; aftermarket revenue up 12.7% YoY, Power Solutions up 51%, Defense up 64% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our cash position, net of debt, has got stronger on Y-o-Y basis. We had net cash of INR2,252 crores at the end of the year, an increase of more than INR1,431 crores on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Management guides INR900 crore profit repatriation from St. Regis Dubai project in FY27, with INR142.58 crore already received in Q1.
items.quote: We have always given a guidance that we should expect to complete a repatriation of about INR900 crores in the current financial year.

items.statement: Zuari Envien Bioenergy secured ethanol orders until October 2026.
items.quote: Our ethanol joint venture, Zuari Envien Bioenergy Private Limited, stabilized its plant operations during the current quarter and has secured orders until the month of October 2026.

items.statement: Simon India executed INR30 crore projects in Q1 with INR70 crore orders under execution.
items.quote: During the quarter we executed projects worth about INR30 crores with approximately INR70 crores worth of orders currently under execution.

items.statement: Zuari Infraworld has gross development value of INR4,900 crore in hand, targeting INR10,000 crore GDV.
items.quote: I think the gross development value of the projects Alok, that you have in hand is closer to INR4,900 crores. Alok Banerjee: Right. Athar Shahab: And we did mention that our aspiration is to have a GDV of INR10,000 crores

items.statement: Sugar margins pressured by 8% SAP increase to INR400/quintal and lower ethanol recovery from molasses route.
items.quote: Despite the improvement in sugar volumes and realizations, margins remained somewhat under pressure, substantially due to about 8% increase in the SAP, which was INR30 per quintal for the last season, as well as somewhat lower recovery from ethanol, which was manufactured through the molasses route.

items.statement: Sugar realizations improved to INR4,116/quintal in Q1 FY27 from INR4,036/quintal in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Average sugar realizations also improved to INR4,116 per quintal from INR4,036 per quintal last year.

items.statement: Ethanol realization static at INR60.70/liter, weighing on margins; management expects government price revision soon.
items.quote: As regards our ethanol business, the realization, the prices continue to be static and therefore they weigh on the margins. However, we remain optimistic about the sector's outlook and expect the government to consider a price revision in the near term.

items.statement: Domestic sugar prices risen 10% over past month to record highs; UP prices at INR4,860-4,920/quintal.
items.quote: Indian sugar prices have risen 10% over the past month to record highs. Prices in Uttar Pradesh are currently at INR4,860 to INR4,920 per quintal, with Maharashtra also registering reasonably high prices.

items.statement: Festival demand expected to support sugar realizations; global prices at 16.6 cents/pound near yearly highs.
items.quote: With festival demand expected to gather pace, the pricing environment is expected to support sugar realizations. The global sugar market has also remained supportive with prices at around 16.6 cents per pound, close to their highest levels in over a year.

items.statement: Sugar mill operated at 100% capacity utilization in previous season; no capacity addition unless ethanol blending policy changes.
items.quote: On the sugar side, we are now operating a facility at 100% capacity utilization. It has demonstrated robust performance. And while we hope to continue our performance in the ensuing season, we remain open to the idea of acquisitions, should they present themselves.

items.statement: Ethanol capacity expansion on hold due to overcapacity; last tender saw 1,800 crore liter offers vs 1,050 crore requirement.
items.quote: We had to take a pause because of the substantial overcapacity that came to ligh t during the last tenders against the INR1050 crore s of tenders, INR1800 crore s worth of offers were received. So obviously we have put our capex plans on hold

items.statement: External debt (excl. working capital) reduced to INR1,888 crore from INR1,909 crore QoQ; targeting further reduction via Dubai repatriation and Zuari Agro loan repayment.
items.quote: Friends, we are making decent progress on our deleveraging exercise, excluding working capital, the aggregate external debt of the company and its subsidiaries was INR1,888 crores as against INR1,909 crores at the end of the fourth quarter.

items.statement: Average borrowing cost declined 56 bps YoY to 9.73% in Q1 FY27; INR1,100 crore debt repayment could save ~INR100-110 crore annual interest.
items.quote: The average cost of borrowings declined by 56 basis points year-on-year to 9.73% in Q1 financial year '27 from 10.29% in Q1 financial year '26.

items.statement: Approved ICD to buy shares of Zuari International for INR150 crore to consolidate listed investments into holding company.
items.quote: We have taken an ICD approval and the strategy behind this transaction is that we want to consolidate the investments which are there in our different companies at the holding group level.

items.statement: Expecting INR258 crore loan repayment from associate Zuari Agro Chemicals in current quarter.
items.quote: We are expecting, as I mentioned earlier, the entire INR258 crores outstanding debt to be repaid to us in the current quarter.

items.statement: Sugar recovery at 11.7% in Q1 FY27; mill operated only 6 days in April 2026 vs no crushing last year.
items.quote: Sugar recovery for this first quarter stood at 11.7%. Last year we had not operated the mill, we produced so the numbers cannot be compared with last year. The performance of the current quarter included six operating days in April '26, whereas there was no crushing operation in the last year.

items.statement: Ethanol production up 1% to 10,138 KL, sales up 5% to 10,248 KL in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Our ethanol business remained on a steady momentum with production increasing by 1% to 10,138 KL and sales grew by 5% to 10,248 KL.

items.statement: Power sales surged to 62.8 lakh units from 7.7 lakh units YoY in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Power sales for the quarter stood at 62.8 lakh unit compared to 7.7 lakh units for the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Ethanol export fee case (INR507 lakh exposure) not provided for; management confident law cannot be applied retrospectively.
items.quote: So we have not created the provisions, but we have given an indemnity and the court cannot make a retrospective change in the law bringing in an effective adjustment that you pay an export fees for the ethanol that you export out of Uttar Pradesh.

items.statement: Exports currently not allowed; management does not foresee export permission in current situation.
items.quote: As far as exports are concerned, currently the exports are not allowed, so we don't foresee that in the current situation exports will be permitted.

items.statement: St. Regis Dubai handovers commenced; 40-45% of customer collections outstanding, demand notes raised post completion certificate.
items.quote: In terms of our payment plan, the payment plan is 50-50%. So now we have raised the demand notes to the customer post receipt of the completion certificate. So we expect to receive the money from the customers in this current quarter.

items.statement: Furniture division losses minimal (maintenance, staff, ICD service); decision on revival or closure by end of FY27.
items.quote: We have been talking to people who could potentially revive that business. If something works out as part of the revival plans, we will revive it. But otherwise, we will make some decisions about this business by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Evaluating inorganic growth opportunities across businesses; open to sugar acquisitions if worthwhile.
items.quote: As I have been mentioning in the previous calls, we continue to evaluate inorganic growth opportunities across our businesses. We also continue to adopt digital solutions across businesses to improve efficiency and streamline our work processes.

items.statement: Simon India exploring digitalization and AI-led initiatives to compress engineering hours; early stage, not yet quantifiable.

items.statement: Target 140 Flurys outlets by end of FY27 and 400 outlets by 2030

items.statement: Plan to double hotels from 42 to 87 and keys from 2,667 to 6,719 over next four years
items.quote: Overall, over the next four years, we plan to double the number of hotels from 42 hotels with 2,667 keys to 87 hotels totaling to 6,719 keys.

items.value: 33 apartments sold, Rs.21 crores received, Rs.70-80 crores expected
items.quote: 33 of the 69 apartments available for sale have been sold in our EM Bypass Hotel and Residential project at Kolkata. This will lead to improved cash flow of Rs.70 to Rs.80 crores during the course of the year, of which Rs.21 crores is already received.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue Rs.172 crores (+10% YoY), EBITDA Rs.52 crores (+8% YoY), EBITDA margin 28.12%
items.quote: At the consolidated level, revenue achieved was Rs.172 crores up 10% and EBITDA at Rs.52 crores up 8% over last year.

items.statement: PAT declined 14% YoY to ~Rs.12 crores due to higher finance costs and deferred tax provision of Rs.2.2 crores
items.quote: PAT for the quarter stood close to Rs.12 crores, a decline of 14% year-on-year with PAT margin close to 7%. This decline is due to the impact of higher finance costs to propel expansion during this period as well as deferred tax provision of Rs.2.2 crores.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity 0.12, net debt-to-EBITDA 0.70; low leverage provides headroom for capex funding
items.quote: The debt-to-equity ratio remains extremely favorable at 0.12 and net debt-to-EBITDA at 0.70.

items.statement: Pipeline of 12 hotels (472 keys) for FY27; portfolio to grow from 42 hotels (2,677 keys) to 3,149 keys by FY27 end
items.value: 472 keys added, 3,149 keys by FY27 end
items.quote: Looking ahead to FY27, we now have a pipeline of 12 hotels comprising of 472 keys for this year. These additions are expected to take our portfolio from the current 42 hotels with 2,677 keys to 3,149 keys by the end of FY27.

items.statement: All-India ADR growth only 6% in Q1 due to flat domestic air traffic and West Asia crisis; expect improvement from Q2
items.quote: The All-India market growth in ADRs during the quarter has only been 6%. And again, as I'm mentioning, the reason for this is because the passenger, air traffic passenger growth has been quite depressed.

items.statement: Retained India's leading occupancy at 92% and RevPAR leadership in upper upscale segment despite headwinds
items.quote: Despite headwinds on account of West Asia crisis, near-flat air traffic growth during this quarter, high energy cost and supply chain disruptions, we have retained India's leading occupancy position of 92% and have maintained our leadership in RevPAR in the upper upscale segment.

items.statement: Shifted to new income tax regime; effective tax rate to drop from ~40% in Q1 to 30-35% in Q2-Q4, improving PAT
items.quote: So, at present our tax rate from next quarter will go down from 35 to 25% as we are coming under new regime. So, this time it does have a 40% tax rate but in future in Q2, Q3, Q4 our tax rate is going to come down to around 30% to 35%.

items.statement: West Asia crisis and oil price impact caused temporary disruption to international travel and flat domestic air traffic in Q1
items.quote: Geopolitical developments during the quarter created some temporary disruption to international travel and air connectivity. However, domestic travel remained largely resilient.

items.statement: Acquisition of Malabar House in Fort Kochi (17 keys) in progress, expected completion by Oct-Nov 2026
items.quote: The acquisition of the Malabar House in Fort Kochi is currently in progress. The property comprises of 17 keys on approximately half an acre of land and this acquisition is expected to be completed by October-November of 2026.

items.statement: Implemented SAP S/4HANA for Finance to strengthen controls, improve reporting timeliness and operational efficiency
items.quote: During the quarter, we completed the implementation of SAP S4 HANA for Finance. This will strengthen our financial controls, improve the quality and timeliness of reporting and enhance operational efficiency across the organization.

items.statement: Upcoming demand drivers: BRICS Summit in Delhi, ~40 wedding dates Nov-Mar, Aero Show Bangalore, Bharat Mobility Expo Delhi

So over the period of next year, the spend would be trending in the similar range of INR2.5 crores to INR4 crores per quarter.

items.statement: Investments of a few crores in sales & marketing, AI product development, talent; front-loaded in H1 FY27

items.statement: Uniware remains market leader with premium positioning; competitive intensity stable

items.statement: Courier aggregation has low switching costs; brands prefer multiple partners creating share-of-wallet opportunity
items.quote: in courier aggregation, the good part is that the benefit of the challenger is that courier aggregator is not very sticky. The switching costs are fairly low. Also, by design, a brand prefers to work with multiple courier aggregators or multiple logistics partners to diversify their risk. That's the nature of the market. Unicommerce e So there is always a fight of share of wallet in that space

items.quote: The partnership of Mahindra Logistics is with Uniware business. They have onboarded the OMS and WMS. Typically, the logistics players offer e-commerce fulfilment, which is e-commerce warehousing.

items.statement: Cash and bank balances grew 72.1% YoY to INR92.6 crore
items.quote: Our cash and bank balances increased from INR53.8 crores at end of the quarter 1 FY '26 to INR92.6 crores at the end of quarter 1 FY '27 with the growth of 72.1% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: No fund raise needed; cash flows sufficient for M&A and investments
items.quote: We are adding cash to our balance sheet on a regular basis. Cash balances increased to INR92 crores, 70% growth over last year. We will use -- we'll potentially use this cash for M&A, but Unicommerce e we don't foresee the need of doing a fund raise because we are adding cash flows to our balance sheet on a regular basis

items.statement: Actively evaluating a few start-ups for inorganic opportunities; criteria: customer fit, product/team quality, valuation, profitability path
items.quote: We continue to evaluate inorganic opportunities. We continue to explore start-ups in respective areas, which could be adjacent to us. The 3 criteria that we look for inorganic are: one, it should make sense for existing customers. Two, it should be a good product, good team. Three, it should be available at the right valuation. And sorry, fourth, one more is that it should either be profitable or

items.statement: Selectively strengthened leadership across functions; added talent with AI capabilities
items.quote: Over the last few quarters, we have selectively strengthened leadership across functions and added talent with AI capabilities. These investments will support faster execution, stronger customer relationships and more scalable systems and processes.

items.statement: Revenue grew 14.3% YoY to INR51.4 crore in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Revenue grew 14.3% year-on-year to INR51.4 crores, supported by continued double-digit growth across both Uniware and Shipway.

items.statement: PAT increased 20.2% YoY to INR4.7 crore due to tax benefits
items.quote: Profit after tax increased by 20.2% to INR4.7 crores compared with INR3.9 crores in the same quarter last year. The increase in PAT is due to tax benefits recognized during the quarter.

items.statement: E-commerce brand mortality high for long-tail brands; NRR protected as scaled brands grow
items.quote: See, normally, we've seen the mortality being high for long-tail brands who have not hit a certain scale. After a brand hits a certain scale on e-commerce, typically, they tend to survive and grow the business. So -- and that's why while in terms of number of logos, you may see a higher churn because of the mortality of those brands. But in terms of the GRR and NRR, it does not impact the metrics

items.statement: Product development cycle 18-24 months; pace accelerated with 3 modules launched in last 12-18 months
items.quote: Typically, every product development cycle has 18 to 24-month gestation period. And hence, we want to now see some of these investments play out. And as I mentioned, we are also front-loading some of the investments and a few of those investments are into AI-led product development. So you will see some of launches coming in that area as well.

items.statement: Mid-teens revenue growth with stable EBITDA margins guided for Belrise as a whole
items.quote: What we are guiding for is the business as a whole, which is for Belrise as a whole, which is mid -teens revenue growth with stable EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margins to remain broadly stable compared to FY26 levels
items.quote: We expect EBITDA margins to remain broadly stable as compared to FY26 levels.

items.statement: Chassis system order from fast-growing 2W/3W OEM with annual revenue >INR650M, SOP Q4 FY27 at Bangalore brownfield
items.quote: The program is expected to generate annual revenue in excess of INR650 million and will be added to our existing brownfield facility in Bangalore, with start of production expected in Q4 of this fiscal year.

items.statement: Suspension and braking systems order from Vietnamese 2W OEM entering India, project timelines confidential
items.quote: We have now secured an order from a fifth OEM, a leading Vietnamese two-wheeler manufacturer entering the Indian market. For this customer, we'll manufacture both suspension and braking systems for its upcoming models.

items.statement: Complete brake assemblies order from legacy 3W OEM in South India, SOP Q4 FY27, modest initial size but strategic entry
items.quote: We expect supplies under this program to commence in the Quarter 4 of this fiscal year. While the initial order size is modest, this is a strategically important win for us as it gives us an entry into one of the fastest growing three -wheeler OEMs in the south of India

items.statement: 59 unique assemblies for Indian 4W EV OEM localization program, expansion at Maharashtra facilities, plus tooling/fixtures/automation order
items.quote: We have been selected to manufacture 59 unique assemblies as part of their localization program for one of their highest-selling EV models. The localization program is progressing rapidly, and we expect to support this program through an expansion at our existing facilities in Maharashtra.

items.statement: 2W chassis order for existing model from largest 2W OEM for Sambhajinagar facility, ~INR500M annual revenue, ramp from Q4 FY27
items.quote: Supplies are expected to ramp up from Quarter 4 of this fiscal year, with the program representing an annual revenue potential of approximately INR500 million.

items.statement: Cumulative order book with fast-growing 2W/3W OEM at INR1,550M annual run rate (fuel tank, exhaust, chassis); suspension and braking wins additional, total ~INR2,000M run rate
items.quote: We have already won around INR1,550 million of orders in the fuel tank, exhaust system, and chassis system. The suspensions and braking wins are over and above these wins. So one can say that we are already at a INR2,000 million or a n INR2 billion run rate with this particular OEM

items.statement: INR17,000M QIP proceeds to be deployed significantly within FY27, primarily for inorganic opportunities and select organic growth
items.quote: With respect to our fund raise of INR17,000 million, we intend to deploy a significant majority of these net proceeds within this fiscal year, primarily towards high -quality inorganic opportunities and also towards select organic growth initiatives.

items.statement: 4W/CV M&A focus in India: targets with differentiated capabilities, strong customer relationships, product technologies to add new categories and increase content per vehicle
items.quote: In the four-wheeler and commercial vehicle segments, our acquisition strategy will primarily be focused on India. While we already work with almost all major four -wheeler and commercial vehicle OEMs in the country, we are looking for businesses that bring differentiated capabilities, strong customer relationships, and product technologies that would otherwise take us considerable time to develop

items.statement: H-One technology collaboration concluded, enabling high tensile steel applications up to 1,470 MPa (~3x India industry standard) for PV and CV segments
items.quote: We have also now successfully concluded our technology collaboration with H-One Japan during this quarter, thus strengthening our capabilities for high tensile steel applications up to 1470 megapascal, which is approximately 3x the industry standard today in India.

items.statement: 2W/3W business benefits from industry volume recovery and new platform launches at marquee customers; growing engagement with two marquee OEMs building robust order book
items.quote: Our two and three-wheeler business, which remains the largest contributor to revenue, continued to benefit from the industry-wide volume recovery and from new platform launches at our marquee customers. Our growing engagement with two m arquee OEMs where we previously had limited presence continues to build a robust order book for us.

items.statement: 4W and CV segments fastest growing in FY26, momentum continued in Q1 FY27 with 18% YoY revenue growth driven by new business wins across expanding customer base
items.quote: The four-wheeler and commercial vehicle business were the fastest growing segments of our portfolio in FY26 and this momentum has continued into Q1 FY27, with revenues growing 18% year-on-year driven by new business wins across an expanding customer base.

items.statement: Input costs (steel, polymer) elevated in Q1; back-to-back pricing model passes fluctuations to customers with slight lag; no material margin impact expected in FY27
items.quote: Input costs, particularly steel and polymer, remained elevated through Q1 FY27. As we have shared before, our back-to-back pricing model means these fluctuations are largely passed to our customers with a slight lag, and we do not expect this to have a material impact on our margin profile in this fiscal year.

items.statement: Worst of cost pressures behind; commodity, staff, energy/transport costs largely peaked; margins expected to improve in coming quarters to maintain FY26 EBITDA margin level
items.quote: We believe that we are largely through the cost pressure or cost pain that we felt in the first quarter, and we can expect our margins to go up in the coming quarters so that we are able to maintain our EBITDA margin as compared to FY26.

items.statement: Back-to-back pricing model passes input cost fluctuations to customers with slight lag; commodity cost cycle largely played out in Q1
items.quote: We do believe that the commodity costs pressure that was there in quarter one, we will get the pass -through of that in the coming quarters, which means that the commodity cost cycle f or us has largely played out.

items.statement: Content per vehicle rising fast with fast-growing 2W/3W OEM: fuel tanks, exhaust, chassis, suspension, braking systems; basket of products exceeded only by largest OEM
items.quote: So we are doing fuel tanks for them, we are doing exhaust systems, we are doing chassis systems, we are doing suspension systems, as well as braking systems. So in general, it's the basket of products that we have been able to penetrate with this particular OEM, which apart from say our largest OEM, we do not enjoy this type of content for vehicle across any other OEM.

items.statement: Hyva acquisition adds leading European CV OEM not previously served; opportunity to leverage broader portfolio and increase wallet share
items.quote: The business supplies to a leading European commercial vehicle OEM with whom Belrise has not worked historically. This gives us an opportunity and an immediate entry point into this customer and importantly, an opportunity to leverage our broader product portfolio and progressively increase our wallet share with this OEM as well.

items.statement: Target aerospace and defense to reach 10% of manufacturing revenue in short to medium term
items.quote: Sumedh, already mentioned in the last earnings call that we want aerospace and defense to get to 10% of our manufacturing revenue in a short to medium term.

items.statement: Trading business declined 19% YoY due to Middle East crisis impacting logistics and demand in African, Asian, Middle Eastern regions; worst behind, expect normalization
items.quote: Due to the ongoing crisis in the Middle East, there was a lot of pressure in terms of business scenario in the Middle East over this quarter. And since most of our trading business comes from outside India, and largely from the African, Asian and Middle Eastern regions, it was fairly muted due to everything that was ongoing in terms of logistics as well as demand over there from April to June.

items.statement: Plasan Sasa partnership for armored vehicle assembly in India; Hyva heavy fabrication capabilities seen as synergistic for defense/armored vehicles opportunity
items.quote: Belrise already has a strategic partnership with Plasan Sasa, the Israeli company under which we intend to assemble armored vehicles for the Indian defense market. We believe the heavy fabrication know -how, manufacturing processes, and capabilities that come with the Hyva business will be highly synergistic with this initiative.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue declined 11% YoY to Rs 168.5 cr due to delayed and uneven monsoon impacting Kharif sowing and crop protection demand
items.quote: On a consolidation basis, our revenue from operations stood at Rs. 168.5 crores in Ql] FY27 compared with Rs. 189.4 crores in Q1 FY26, representing an 11% year-over-year decline

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 28% from 22% YoY; EBITDA margin improved to 5.7% from 5.2% YoY
items.quote: Our gross margins improved meaningfully to 28% from 22% in QI FY26, while EBITDA margins improved to 5.7% from 5.2

items.statement: Capacity utilization increased to 70% in Q1 FY27 from 52% in FY26
items.quote: From an operational perspective, capacity utilization increased to 70% during the quarter compared with 52% in FY26.

items.statement: Capital work-in-progress stood at Rs 76.4 cr in FY26 vs Rs 57.1 cr in FY25 reflecting ongoing investments at Barwasni and DF facility
items.quote: Our capital work-in-progress stood at Rs. 76.4 crores in FY26 and compared with Rs. 57.1 crores in FY25, reflecting these ongoing investments.

items.statement: Management declined to commit to FY27 revenue growth figure; aims to perform to best capabilities
items.quote: We are looking forward and we are working aggressively for achieving good growth. And this quarter is an important quarter for us. We are looking forward to growth, but we don't want to commit for any figures.

items.statement: Current capacity supports peak revenue of Rs 1,100-1,200 cr; expanded capacity can support Rs 1,800 cr+ over 4-5 years
items.quote: With the existing capacity? Yes, sir. Yes, it should be around Rs. 1100 crores - Rs. 1200 crores, up to that

items.quote: In Q2, because of you can say a little lower demands and more availability, the prices of raw materials were corrected and they came down and I think now the things are almost stable but still a little incremental as compared to last year, especially the packaging material, which is almost 40% higher, the plastics and all these things that has an impact.

items.statement: Finance cost rose 19% YoY due to inventory buildup anticipating sales; expect reduction as inventory liquidates and collections improve
items.quote: We have bought the material anticipating that there will be a good sales, but you know as Sanjay Ji has explained the things that due to poor rainfall and shifting of crops also impacted the sales. But we are expecting near time we will liquidate this inventory, and the collections will be better and so we are hoping that we will be able to reduce the finance cost.

items.statement: Exploring M&A for new technology and market expansion globally; nothing concrete yet; focus on domestic brand expansion first
items.quote: We are in touch with some of the good consultants also for merger acquisitions across the globe, specifically for two areas, one is for some kind of newer technology which can add value and second is for any kind of market expansion where we can get some value addition. So, we are in discussion, but presently nothing concrete has happened so far.

items.statement: Industry attempted price hikes but weak demand and elevated Chinese supply limited sustainability; pricing could not offset volume impact
items.quote: However, the weak demand environment limited the industry's availability to sustain these increases. Prices of several molecules remained under pressure as global supply remained elevated, particularly with continued availability of intermediates and technical products from China.

items.statement: Expect better Kharif quarter closing; sustainability and growth in both Kharif and Rabi but very high expectations not possible this year
items.quote: But we are hoping for a better Kharif quarter closing. We are working towards that direction. And overall, we can see that very high expectations cannot be possible this year. But definitely, the sustainability and growth should be there in both Rabi and Kharif it should be there.

items.statement: El Nino declared; not expecting promising monsoons ahead; heat/drought resistant products under 3-year ICAR-IARI project
items.quote: We are not expecting very promising monsoons even in the coming days because this El Nino has already been declared. But yes, wherever there are opportunities, there are rains or there are no water issues, our team is working and we are able to grow the business.

items.statement: Two of three specialty products for FY27 already launched; new fungicide on track for Q2 launch subject to patent expiry
items.quote: Two of the three speciality products planned for FY27 are already in the market, while our new fungicide remains on track for launch this quarter, subject to the relevant patent expiry.

items.quote: We've traditionally been where, we're used to passenger traffic somewhere around 8% to 9% in normal years, and drive maybe 5% to 7% more of LFL growth over that to kind of reach an LFL percentage maybe around 14% -15%.

items.statement: Overall passenger traffic was flat YoY in Q1 FY27 due to a significant decline in international traffic, while domestic traffic registered modest growth.
items.quote: Domestic traffic re gistered modest growth, but a significant decline in international traffic resulted in overall passenger traffic being broadly flat year-on-year for the quarter

items.statement: Adjusted gross profit margin was around 81% in Q1 FY27, within guided range, after reclassifying INR223 million of lounge aggregation costs.
items.quote: Adjusting for this reclassification of INR223 million of lounge aggregation cost from other expenses to cost of sales, the adjusted gross profit stands at INR3.65 billion, translating into an adjusted gross profit margin of around 81%, which remains well within our guided range.

items.statement: EBITDA margin moderated to 35.8% in Q1 FY27 due to higher employee and operating costs from new airport commissions and ramp-up.
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR1 .6 billion, up 11% year -on-year, and EBITDA margin moderated to 35.8% for the quarter, reflecting the impact of higher employee cost and operating cost associated with recently commissioned airports and new business initiatives.

items.statement: 50 outlets are under development across the network, expected to open in FY27 and ramp over 12-24 months.
items.quote: We also have a strong pipeline of growth opportunities, with over 50 outlets currently under development across our network. As these locations open and then mature over the coming 12 to 18 months, they are expected to provide a meaningful uplift to both revenue and earnings.

items.statement: Net contract gains were 15.9% YoY at system-wide level and 20.2% at consolidated level in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: We sustained strong momentum in new outlet openings, backed by recent contract wins and a robust pipeline, which translated into net contract gains of 15.9% year -on-year at the system -wide level.

items.statement: Added 87 travel QSR outlets and two lounges over the last 12 months across Mumbai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Cochin, Navi Mumbai, and Noida airports.
items.quote: Over the last 12 months, we have added 87 travel QSR outlets and two lounges across the network, with significant additions at Mumba i, Delhi, Hyderabad, Cochin, Navi Mumbai, and Noida airports.

items.quote: Our system-wide footprint as of June end stands at 580 travel QSR outlets and lounges, while our brand portfolio has expanded to 153 brands.

items.statement: Commenced operations at Noida International Airport and launched passenger services under Elite Assist brand including meet-and-greet and porter services.
items.quote: During the quarter, we commenced operations at Noida International Airport, taking our system-wide presence to 21 airports.

items.statement: Bhogapuram Airport opening on 17th August 2026 with multiple outlets under JV GHL; pipeline includes Bangalore T1, Pune, and other AAI airports.
items.quote: The opening of Bhogapuram Airport on 17th August marks another significant milestone where we will operate multiple outlets under our JV, GHL.

items.statement: No significant price escalation in Q1 FY27; LFL growth driven by premiumization, bundling, and limited brand edits rather than pricing.
items.quote: we've not done a significant price escalation as well this year , with the challenge around it, we've been a bit tempered in that.

items.statement: Debt-free balance sheet with consolidated cash balance of approximately INR9.7 billion as of June 30, 2026.
items.quote: As of June 30th, we maintain a debt-free balance sheet and a consolidated cash balance of approximately INR9.7 billion.

items.statement: Company maintains a debt-free balance sheet providing headroom for airport expansions, lounges, highways, and passenger services.
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains a signi ficant source of strength. As of June 30th, we maintain a debt-free balance sheet and a consolidated cash balance of approximately INR9.7 billion.

items.statement: Delhi T3 contract expires 30th September 2026; GHL JV has bid for renewal but results not yet out. Chennai and Kolkata airports up for renewal end of March 2027 and early Q1 FY28.
items.quote: Delhi T3 which is a material subsidiary, the contract is till 30th September 2026. The JV GHL has bid for the contract, but the results are not out at this moment.

items.statement: System-wide sales grew 18% YoY to INR8.4 billion; consolidated revenue from operations grew 20.6% YoY to INR4.5 billion in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT increased 35.6% YoY to INR1.3 billion; PAT margin expanded to 28.5% from 25.3% in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Consolidated profit after tax increased by 35.6% year -on-year to INR1 .3 billion, and PAT margin expanded to 28.5% compared with 25.3% in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Consolidated LFL sales growth was 4.2% in Q1 FY27; excluding Mumbai, Guwahati, and South India markets, LFL grew around 7% YoY.
items.quote: As a result, system-wide LFL sales growth was 0.8% for the quarter. Importantly, excluding these specific markets, like-for-like sales grew around 7% year-on-year across our wider network.

items.statement: Employee cost increased due to annual compensation revisions, onboarding for new outlets at Noida and Cochin, and staffing for passenger services at Noida.
items.quote: employee cost increased during the quarter, primarily due to annual compensation revisions and the onboarding of additional manpower to support recently opened outlets at Noida and Cochin airports, both of which are currently in the ramp-up phase.

items.statement: New labour code impact minimal at INR8-10 crores; majority of 5,000+ employees on company roll.
items.quote: The impact of the new labour code is very minimal for us, which we had clarified earlier, and it was below like INR8 crores to INR10 crores kind of a number.

items.statement: International traffic decline impacted South India markets with higher Middle East exposure; domestic traffic hit record high in May 2026.
items.quote: certain South India markets given their relatively higher exposure to Middle East traffic.

items.statement: Majority of airports operate on direct concession model; JVs typical only for multi-airport operators. TFS wins contracts through execution discipline and brand portfolio.
items.quote: globally, more often than not , by a wide margin, they are direct concessions is the norm. JVs tend to be in these type of examples where you have, say an operator maybe running 5, 6, 7 airports.

items.statement: Middle East conflict caused international traffic disruptions in April and June 2026; recovery expected from September-October with airline route restorations.
items.quote: I think they've already come out and called that you start seeing from September & October, restoration of many of those long-haul international routes. And that's automatically where we expect to see that flow through.

items.statement: Contract renewal rate dipped from 94% to 92% due to non-renewal of smaller highway pilot outlets not aligned with WSA strategy.
items.quote: it was some highway outlets, which part of our strategy, which were some we entered earlier , which we didn't see a intention to renew.

items.statement: Launched passenger services at Noida Airport under Elite Assist brand (meet-and-greet, porter) integrated with EATS technology platform.
items.quote: Another important milestone during the quarter was the successful launch of our passenger services at Noida International Airport under our Elite Assist brand, including meet -and-greet and porter services.

items.statement: International expansion focus on Asia (Malaysia, Hong Kong, Indonesia) with entities in Dubai and Indonesia; Middle East on hold until normalization.
items.quote: We have set up an entity in Dubai to focus at the region. We set up another entity recently in Indonesia to look at opportunities there because you need those local entities to be able to bid for opportunities in the markets.

items.statement: ~5,000+ employees, majority on company roll; labour cost semi-variable with flexibility to move staff between international and domestic terminals.
items.quote: we roughly have around 5,000 plus employees and majority are on company roll.

items.statement: Highway wayside amenities (WSA) opportunity emerging with ~1,000 sites announced by government; TFS engaging with partners, brands, landlords, OMCs for medium-long term calibrated entry.
items.quote: there's about a thousand wayside amenity plan already announce d by the government. But that is to come. So what I've been announcing is that we will be targeting those as those come online.

items.quote: Sir, targeted turnover for the FY26-27 is almost INR 850 crores and for FY27-28 is INR 1,200 crores.

items.statement: Strategy to balance government and private EPC work; actively increasing private works to reduce concentration risk
items.quote: In terms of private works, we are actively trying to increase our private works to create a good balance between government and private. With government, this kind of portfolio will always help us going forward because it reduces the risk in any one front.

items.statement: Technology integration focus: leveraging AI, data analytics, BIM to improve project management efficiency, reduce manpower, and enhance margins across pan-India operations
items.quote: So, going forward in the future, let's say 5-10 years down the line, you will see that we will come out as a more technology -driven infrastructure company because that is very important. The machines are going to be the same, the way that we construct is going to be the same. But how do we manage all of this is very crucial.

items.statement: Temporary NHAI bidding restriction and voluntary surrender of unviable toll project due to geopolitical impact; does not alter long-term fundamentals
items.quote: A temporary bidding restriction from NHAI and the voluntary surrender of a toll project where economics had been unfavorable due to the same reason. These factors led to a short-term impact on profitability but do not alter the long -term fundamentals of the business.

items.statement: Renewable energy EPC (production and transmission) identified as future focus; active research underway but no bids yet; will take time to build capability
items.quote: So, like I mentioned in my previous calls, definitely renewable energy production and transmission is something that will be in focus in the coming years. The team and all of us are actively looking on how do we capitalize it, but it is very important to u nderstand that it will take some time

items.statement: Building internal technology team to develop proprietary systems for site management, resource optimization, and predictive analytics
items.quote: And simultaneously, we are also developing a good team internally to focus on that front and how do we leverage this technology to increase our efficiency on our core business as well, which is how do I reduce the manpower at the site. How do I increase efficiency in terms of how multiple sites are managed from one core location from the HO.

items.statement: Commissioned doubled crushing capacity from 825 to 1650 MTPD on 26 May 2026 alongside new liquid glucose (180 TPD), maltodextrin (50 TPD) and cogeneration expansion from 7.1 to 15.8 MW
items.quote: The centerpiece of this phase was the commissioning on 26 May 2026 of a doubling of a crushing capacity from 825 metric ton per day to 1650 metric ton per day alongside a new liquid glucose facility of 180 tons per day, a Maltodextrin powder facility of 50 metric tons per day, an expansion of a captive cogeneration power plant from 7.1 megawatt to 15.8 megawatt.

items.statement: Expect FY27 maize crushing above 400,000 tons versus 265,000 tons in FY26
items.quote: This year, we are expecting that the crushing will go up above 4,00,000 tons in the entire year.

items.statement: Target value-added products at 20-22% of turnover in FY27 versus 3% in FY26
items.quote: Last year, we had about 3% of our entire turnover as value -added products. This year, we are expecting it to go up to 20 %-22% of our entire turnover as value -added products.

items.statement: Value-added margin expanded to 39.8% in Q1 FY27 from 25.1% in Q1 FY26 driven by shift to manufacturing-led revenue
items.quote: Value-added grew 30.3% year -on-year to Rs. 80.53 crores, with value -added margin expanded to 39.8% from 25.1% in Q1 FY26 , driven by a decisive shift towards higher margin, manufacturing led revenue.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 540 bps to 15.3% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The operating EBITDA rose 26.6% year -on-year to Rs . 30.98 crores, with EBITDA margin expanding 540 basis points to 15.3%.

items.statement: Of Rs 664 crore total project outlay, Rs 552 crore incurred by 30 June 2026; major capex cycle substantially complete
items.quote: Of the total project outlay of approximately Rs. 664 crores, around Rs. 552 crores had been incurred as of 30 June 2026, with the major phase of CAPEX cycle now substantially behind us.

items.statement: Building additional 50,000 tons storage across two silos, 50,000 sq ft maize godown and 1.6 MW methane gas-based power plant in FY27
items.quote: In parallel, we are building out the supporting infrastructure for this growth, with an additional 50,000 tons of storage across two new silos, a 50,000-square-feet Maize godown and a 1.6-megawatt Methane gas-based power plant.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capacity utilization 71.4% due to planned shutdowns for integration; expect progressive improvement from Q2 FY27
items.quote: The capacity utilization of 71.4% for the quarter should be viewed in the context of commissioning and integration of the doubled capacity. Integrating the expanded plant, required planned shutdown days during the quarter which temporarily lowered utili zation.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle 130 days in Q1 FY27 driven by higher inventory for expanded capacity; expect normalization as utilization ramps
items.quote: The cash conversion cycle stood at 130 days, driven largely by higher inventory levels built to support the expanded 1650 metric ton per day capacity.

items.statement: Net debt Rs 735.32 crore at 30 June 2026; peak debt in H1 FY27, expected to decline in H2 as working capital normalizes
items.quote: On the balance sheet, the net debt stood at Rs . 735.32 crore s, reflecting the funding of our expansion program as well as seasonal procurement of raw material.

items.statement: All new capex debt qualifies for interest subvention under Bihar Industrial Investment Promotion Policy; subvention cap amended from Rs 20 crore to Rs 40 crore in FY25 but not yet cleared for this project
items.quote: Importantly, all debt raised towards the new CAPEX qualifies for interest subvention under Bihar ’s Industrial Investment Promotion Policy, meaningfully containing our effective cost of borrowing and supporting the economics of the expansion.

items.statement: Export contribution more than doubled to 10.4% in Q1 FY27 from 4.9% in Q1 FY26; targeting further geographic diversification
items.quote: Contribution from exports more than doubled to 10.4% in quarter 1 ‘27 from 4.9% in quarter 1 ‘26, reflecting growing acceptance of our products across international markets.

items.statement: Plan to launch Dextrose Anhydrous, Dextrose Monohydrate, Hydrol and specialized modified starches (cationic, carboxy methyl, pre-gel, spray starch) in FY27
items.quote: During FY’27, we plan to enter high value derivatives including Dextrose Anhydrous, Dextrose Monohydrate and Hydrol , while expanding beyond our existing Dextrin and edible starch range into specialized modified starches such as cationic starch, carboxy methyl starch, pre-gel starch and spray starch.

items.statement: Procure ~80% maize inventory during Rabi season (Apr-Jul) at FOR doorstep prices; currently getting maize at Rs 22.5-23/kg delivered versus market Rs 24/kg
items.quote: I’m still getting maize at my doorstep delivered at 22.5 or 23 at the most, a very, very good quality of maize, sweet quality at 23, first of all.

items.statement: Maize crushing volume 69,689 MT in Q1 FY27 versus 64,770 MT in Q1 FY26; Q2 FY27 expected 100,000-110,000 MT
items.quote: Operationally, maize crushing rose to 69,689 metric tons from 64,770 metric tons in Q1 FY’26.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 value-added revenue grew 30.3% YoY to Rs 80.53 crore; trading share fell to 3.3% from 19.5%
items.quote: value-added growing 30.3% year-on- year to Rs. 80.53 crores and value-added margin expanding by 1,477 basis points to 39.8

items.statement: White-label business expanding with existing and new MNC customers; 70-80% of new value-added products sold through existing dealer/institutional channels
items.quote: Yes, sir. It is completely on. White labelling base has increased. Few more customers have come in. Again, the India White brand has come in and the customers which we were doing earlier, they have increased their products.

items.statement: No new capex planned for FY27; focus on stabilizing current expansion, reaching 90-95% utilization, deleveraging before evaluating next phase
items.quote: Sir, at the moment, we want to stabilize because this is a very, very big expansion, which we have done. So, we want to consolidate and stabilize this, come to our experience of 90 %-95% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Liquid glucose at ~70% capacity utilization; maltodextrin powder needs 2-3 more months to reach target; modified starch trials online by September
items.quote: Talking about the value -added products, liquid glucose, one product which we are doing pretty, we have started now doing it about 70% odd we have reached of the entire capacity. And this again, on the increase only, maltodextrin powder, it is yet to because maltodextrin powder, all the samples and everything has to go to a lot of places and the MNCs and all.

items.statement: Employee count 719; sales/marketing team breakup not disclosed on call but available through IR team
items.quote: Since your employee count is 719, can you help me with the break -up of the marketing or sales team? Anil Kishorepuria: Sir, that’s a really detailed thing which you are asking. We don’t have this at the moment ready with us, but it will be available with you with the IR team

items.statement: Management targets crossing INR500 crores consolidated revenue in FY27 and INR630-640 crores in FY28.
items.quote: We continue to work towards our stated objective of crossing INR500 crores in consolidated revenue during the FY 27, while maintaining appropriate discipline on margins and working capital.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to increase by 1-2% over the next 2 years.
items.quote: I would expect at least an increase of about 1% to 2% in the EBITDA area over the next 2 years or so.

items.statement: Received orders worth INR45.71 crores from Reliance Group, INR1.94 crores from Nesco, and INR36.71 lakhs from West Bengal Public Department in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: We received 5 work orders from Reliance Projects and Property Management Services worth INR30.77 crores for housekeeping, MEP electrical, and ancillary services. In addition, we secured facility management contracts across 7 Reliance Group entities valued at INR14.94 crores, taking the combined value of orders from the Reliance Group to INR45.71 crores.

items.statement: CCTV project pipeline includes Mumbai traffic tenders worth INR15-18 crores, HDFC Bank command center worth INR1.5-2 crores, NKDA AMC worth INR6 crores, and SAIL Burnpur worth INR4-5 crores.
items.quote: We are also expecting 2 big projects of around INR15 to INR18 crores from the Mumbai police and traffic. So these are also around 25% to 30%. Then one of the banks, larger banks where we work with, HDFC Bank, has kind of asked us to set up a command and control center which is more CCTV driven.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 121 bps to 7.99%; net profit margin improved 81 bps to 5.54%.
items.quote: increased by 36.24% year -on-year to INR9.22 crores, while the EBITDA margin expanded by 121 basis points to 7.99%. Net profit stood at INR6.40 crores, growing 35% year -on-year with the net profit margin improving by 81 basis points to 5.54

items.statement: Healthy order inflows across private and government clients; opportunities in government tenders, private sector cross-selling, and industry formalization.
items.quote: We continue to see opportu nities across both the government and private sectors. In the government segment, our established credentials provide opportunities to participate in large tenders and expand geographically, while in the private sector, we see scope to deepen client relationships through a broader combination of security, housekeeping, facility management, and technical services

items.statement: Shifting contract mix toward technology (CCTV, access control, command centers) and mechanization (facade cleaning, AI-driven machines) to improve margins.
items.quote: we are already pretty well occupied with manpower deployment whether it is in the security guarding sector or in the housekeeping cleaning sector a nd such other labor intensive facility management sector. So that is one. Now what we have started doing is firstly, we have started adding more components to these 2 primary manpower elements

items.statement: Top clients: Reliance INR46-47 crores, HDFC Bank INR18 crores, Anjali Jewellers INR12 crores, Airports INR30 crores combined; client retention ~96-97%.
items.quote: Reliance is o ur top client. So that is we will be we are doing around INR46 crores to INR47 crores from Reliance itself. Like Reliance is our top client. And then we have HDFC bank which is at around INR18 crores and then Anjali Jewellers around INR12 crores. We have the airports which have a combined revenue of around INR30 crores annually speaking

items.statement: West Bengal contributes 72-73% of revenue; share not expected to decline significantly as West Bengal growth continues alongside diversification into Bihar and Odisha.
items.quote: Currently it's around 72% to 73% because see, right now what has in Gujarat and Maharashtra I think I had mentioned in either in some conference earlier or in some earnings call only, our Head of Marketing is based out of Bombay, right.

items.statement: Professional succession planning underway; management team ages 30-55; family members involved but not sole succession path.
items.quote: This company is looking towards a pretty professional succession instead of just a founder level, family level succession. But many in the family are involved and we are sir looking at a succession over the next few years and up to the decade with a pipeline where gradually at least four or five of the members will be able to take up the current senior positions.

items.statement: CCTV revenue target INR30 crores in FY27 vs INR13-14 crores in FY26; PAT target INR3.5-4 crores vs INR2.5 crores last year.
items.quote: By the end of this year ma'am we are expecting like I said around a INR30 crores revenue and with that we should be able to increase our PAT which was last year around INR2.5 crores to around INR3.5 crores to INR4 crores.

items.statement: Margin expansion dependent on project business growth; commoditized manpower business limits overall margin improvement.
items.quote: Fundamentally our margin growth that happens, happens from project businesses which is the CCTV project or the DDU-GKY projects et cetera. Whose revenue growth is not as at par with the kind of growth that we typically see in the security facility management sector because that is more commoditized and more manpower driven.
