items.statement: No seasonality in business; regular maintenance and surveillance demand irrespective of seasons.
items.quote: Very little, very little. Ours is a regular maintenance and surveillance requirement. You see our work has in fact I think our experience in the COVID also, it showed that if a particular facility continues to function, if it doesn't stop down, then it continues to require both the security, facility management and the surveillance verticals almost irrespective of the terms the seasons or even the

items.statement: Africa revenue share rose to ~32% in Q1 FY27 from ~4.47% in Q1 FY26, driven by capital allocation and Middle East challenges
items.quote: Africa accounted for approximately 32% of our revenue in Q1 FY27 compared with around 4.47% in Q1 FY26, a significant shift in the geographical mix of our busin ess that reflects the relationships we have built and the stronger presence we have established in the region

items.statement: Long-term revenue target of INR600-700 crores over next 2-3 years remains in place
items.quote: I believe that INR600 crores to INR700 crores figure long-term revenue targets are still in place.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT fell to INR2.2 crores from INR6.51 crores YoY due to higher freight, logistics and employee costs
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, PBT stood at INR3.04 crores compared with INR7.26 crores, and PAT stood at INR2.2 crores compared with INR6.51 crores.

items.statement: Shipping and logistics costs rose sharply on standalone and consolidated basis due to geopolitical factors
items.quote: Shipping and logistics cost increased to INR3.86 crores from INR2.36 crores on a standalone basis, while consolidated shipping and transportation expenses increased to INR4.72 crores from INR2.76 crores last year.

items.statement: Consolidated employee benefit expenses increased to INR3.83 crores from INR2.21 crores YoY as company builds international teams
items.quote: Consolidated employee benefit expenses increased to approximately INR3.83 crores from INR2.21 crores in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Consolidated inventory at INR96.8 crores with INR84.4 crores overseas; business cycle runs ~2 quarters for conversion
items.quote: As of June 30, 2026, our consolidated inventory stood at about INR96.8 crores, with around INR84.4 crores positioned at our overseas subsidiaries.

items.statement: Investments in inventory, manpower and marketing are transient and growing quarter-on-quarter, not fixed capex
items.quote: All the investments made are transient in nature. None of them are fixed investments or any plant machinery capex purchases, etcetera, which has a certain timeline of 3-year break even or whatever.

items.statement: HexL proprietary brand gaining momentum; long-term target is equal revenue split across new customized, used/refurbished and HexL segments
items.quote: In 2 years to 3 years, I think HexL should have larger share of the pie. And our used equipment business should also have the larger share of the pie. And I think if all the three verticals are equal in our revenue mix, I think we would be happy enough.

items.statement: Commodity inflation not fully passed through; partially absorbed and partially built into purchase/sales prices
items.quote: It is not expected to be fully passed through because the fluctuations in commodity prices are very, very wildly swinging right now. What we have tried to do is try to maintain a certain level of pricing and absorb certain costs in the interest of gaining long-term business.

items.statement: Geopolitical developments creating operational/logistical challenges, higher freight costs and longer shipping times
items.quote: The ongoing geopolitical developments across various regions have continued to create operational and logistical challenges, particularly for the businesses with significant international exposure, such as ours. These developments have contributed to an in crease in freight and shipping costs during the quarter

items.statement: International collections more sophisticated with documented timelines; challenges only during genuine geopolitical disruptions
items.quote: the challenges around customer collections are , I would say, internationally handled in a more sophisticated way than I would say domestically, because things are documented on record in writing, etc etera. So, I mean, the timelines which are there in the commercial negotiations, they are usually

items.statement: Inventory positioned overseas to improve availability and reduce delivery timelines for used/refurbished equipment business
items.quote: Availability is the key differentiator, and having machines positioned closer to our customers allows us to respond faster to requirements, improve product availability, and reduce delivery timelines.

items.statement: Standalone revenue grew 37.4% YoY to INR51.29 crores; consolidated revenue grew 15.9% YoY to INR56.57 crores
items.quote: On a standalone basis, revenue from operations stood at INR51.29 crores for Q1 FY27, up 37.4% year-on-year compared with INR37.32 crores in Q1 FY26. On a consolidated basis, revenue stood at INR56.57 crores compared with INR48.82 crores in the corresponding quarter last year, representing a growth of 15.9%.

items.statement: Stronger capital base post-IPO and enhanced banking facilities provide capacity for higher volumes and international expansion
items.quote: The stronger capital base following the IPO, together with enhanced banking facilities, provides us with the capacity to support higher business volumes and continued international expansion.

items.statement: International markets across Africa, Latin America, Middle East targeted; each region large with project opportunities over next 3 years
items.quote: I think in the next 3 years, as a whole, each of these regions are very large on their own. Each of them are developing regions. Africa and Latin America are very populous regions of the world as a whole, and Middle East has a very high per capita spending capacity with a lot of infrastructure projects always going on and expected after the geopolitical situation settles.

items.statement: Meaningful improvement in returns from strategic investments expected in 3-6 quarters
items.quote: I think as the team sets in, as the system, processes, organization overall, the inventory and overall, our marketing efforts sets in, for the next 3 quarters to 6 quarters, I think we'll start seeing visibility and, you know, the increase in the numbers.

items.statement: Long-term PAT margin target of 12-15% maintained; HexL expected to become EBITDA positive as volumes scale
items.quote: We definitely plan as in the previous questions, I think we addressed that 12% to 14% PAT levels are estimated. But, of course, we are in the nascent stages, initial stages. Will require obviously a lot of marketing expenses, discounting, promotions, exhibitions, etcetera, which will not be viable at a smaller volume. As soon as the volumes pick up, all the capital goods brands or anything else ha

items.statement: Working capital cycles elongated due to geopolitical situation; inventory levels expected at similar levels plus/minus few percentage points in lower double digits
items.quote: I believe we are going to see some elongated levels of working capital cycles that we are seeing right now because of the obvious facts that geopolitical situations are in a hazy situation right now. So, we still like to keep inventory when the customers need them and availability is there, and we are seeing a healthy turnaround given the fact that we are literally in turmoil globally.

items.statement: Operational manpower costs to rise further over next few quarters to build sales, purchase and operational teams for scale
items.quote: We definitely plan to increase our sales team and purchase team and everything. Basically, operational manpower cost is going to rise over the next few quarters. And yes, the reason behind it is to get future operating leverage, which will give obviously higher revenue profitability and everything in the quarters and years to come.

items.statement: Taking substantial hit on margins from higher shipping costs; partially passing to suppliers at purchase and customers at sale
items.quote: We are taking the hit, but we are still able to grow on revenue. We are taking partial hit and we are taking -- where we are partially trying to supply, like, pass it on to the suppliers also, like, at the time of purchase, and partially trying to pass it at the time of sales. But we are taking a substantial amount of hit as well.

items.statement: New customized equipment customization seeing stronger demand due to faster availability and lower breakdown needs
items.quote: I think new equipment customization is more in demand right now because of various reasons and input prices for the end users as well. So, they are looking at faster availability and lower breakdown times, etcetera. So, I think growth can come from new customized equipment.

items.statement: Shipping cost outlook uncertain due to unpredictable oil prices and route closures extending shipping times
items.quote: But I think, I mean, it's just like that, do you know the next quarter oil prices? No one does, right? So, it's hard to know what are the oil prices, which will directly impact the shipping cost, to be, over the next few quarters.

items.statement: Debtor increase is planned strategy for overseas market penetration; longer shipping times also extending working capital cycle
items.quote: Well, I mean, the increase of debtors is a planned strategy of penetration in overseas markets. And as we are deploying manpower and people in those areas, so it is for the purpose to sell locally in those regions, achieve higher growth in sales. And I bel ieve that is the part of the reason of increase in debtors

items.statement: HexL differentiates by filling gaps in legacy brands with technological, performance and productivity features like automotive disruption
items.quote: The answer to that is we have filled a lot of gaps that international legacy brands which are old and their philosophy of making the equipment and worked in a traditional conventional way were doing. And similarly, like the automotive industry was di srupted by a few new upcoming players, we intend to do similar things by incorporating a lot of technological features or performance features and pr

items.statement: Historically H2 stronger than H1 but too early to project Q1 FY27 given geopolitical uncertainty
items.quote: I mean, we are still on quarter one. So, it's too early to comment on that and giving any forward-looking questions. But historically that has been the case. I am not able to give any forward projections on the second half right away.

items.statement: Standalone PBT INR4.15 crores vs INR4.52 crores YoY; consolidated PBT INR3.04 crores vs INR7.26 crores YoY
items.quote: Standalone profit before tax stood at INR4.15 crores compared with INR4.52 crores in Q1 FY26, while profit after tax stood at INR3.31 crores compared with INR3.76 crores. On a consolidated basis, PBT stood at INR3.04 crores compared with INR7.26 crores, and PAT stood at INR2.2 crores compared with INR6.51 crores.

items.statement: China contract manufacturing for backhoe loaders unaffected by natural calamities as production locations not impacted
items.quote: China is a very large country. I mean, in area much larger than India. So, the locations that we are presenting are not affected by any such issues.

items.statement: Africa growth partly driven by November 2025 partnership with Africa's largest equipment dealer
items.quote: It is partly due to that we have increased our efforts in Africa. And it is definitely one of the founding reasons for that.

items.statement: Full-year revenue growth guidance revised upward to 70% from previous 50%
items.quote: So, we would like to revise our guidance for the full year to 70% considering the robust demand which is there and the capacities that we are ready with in Ratlam.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at sustainable to improve from current 18.9% level
items.quote: So, we have reported a 18.9% margin, so we continue that guidance.

items.statement: Cumulative gross block including CWIP expected to reach Rs. 1,300 crores by end of FY27 from Rs. 800 crores at start
items.quote: When we start this year, we were close to 800 including CWIP and we are by the end of this year, it will be close to 1.300.

items.statement: FY27 incremental capex of Rs. 500 crores funded by Rs. 200 crores debt, Rs. 100 crores IPO proceeds, Rs. 200 crores internal accruals
items.quote: There would be no equity dilution as such in this year and so on the debt side out of this Rs. 500 crores, Rs. 200 crores will be from the debt side

items.statement: Commissioned 2 GW solar panel and 2 GW power electronics at Ratlam; total panel capacity 3.5 GW, power electronics 4 GW
items.quote: During the quarter, we commissioned 2-gigawatt solar panel manufacturing facility. With the addition, our total solar panel manufacturing capacity increased to 3.5 gigawatt. Additionally, we also commissioned 2-gigawatt power electronics manufacturing facility at Ratlam in August'26.

items.statement: 2 GW lithium-ion battery plant at Ratlam on track for commissioning by Q2 FY27
items.quote: Furthermore, the 2 gigawatt lithium-ion battery manufacturing capacity at Ratlam is also on track for commissioning by Q2 FY27.

items.statement: DCR solar cell plant operating at 80%+ utilization
items.quote: S, it is operating at 80% plus utilization right now.

items.statement: New 2 GW power electronics facility at Ratlam to start at 40-50% utilization (single shift)
items.quote: Initially, in terms of figure, you can take close to 40% to 50% utilization of the capacity of Ratlam.

items.statement: TOPCon facility building completed, machine orders placed, targeting commissioning in ~9 months (Q4 FY27/Q1 FY28)
items.quote: We have set a target of Q, sir. Coming year, I mean. After 9 months we can say. Now 7.5 months remaining basically.

items.statement: Distribution network expanded to 10,100+ channel partners (80+ distributors, 1,000+ dealers, 30+ exclusive Shoppes added in Q1)
items.quote: The distribution network recorded one of its largest quarterly expansions during the quarter. We added more than 80 distributors, over 1,000 dealers, and more than 30 exclusive Shoppes. This took a total channel partners network to over 10,100 as of June '26.

items.statement: Added coverage in Odisha and Uttarakhand (now have distributor in each district and service engineer)
items.quote: So, in this immediate quarter, we have added two new more states from growing category to covered, one is Odisha and the other one is Uttarakhand.

items.statement: Target 15,000+ network partners (distributors, dealers, Shoppes) by end of FY28
items.quote: At the end of 28, we believe more than 15,000 Network partaers including Shoppe?

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded to 18.9% from 17.7% in Q1 FY26 driven by scale, utilization, process improvements
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved to 18.9% from 17.7% in Q1 FY26. The improvement in operating profitability was supported by the significant increase in business scale during the quarter.

items.statement: Passed portion of efficiency gains to customers via competitive pricing but retained sufficient margin
items.quote: Importantly, we passed on a portion of these efficiency gains to customers through competitive pricing during the quarter. Despite sharing part of these benefits with the customers, we were able to retain sufficient efficiencies within the business.

items.statement: System realization Rs. 26-30 per watt including panel, inverter, battery (varies by DCR/non-DCR, battery type, on/off-grid)
items.quote: Generally, we sce it as a per-watt, how we measure it, we see it as a per-watt realization. So, for a system with battery, generally this cost comes to close to Rs. 26 to Rs.30 per watt.

items.statement: Increased stake in Zayo Energy and Zayo Cable from 19% to 50% each for backward integration of solar module components
items.quote: During the quarter, the company increased its stake in Zayo Energy Private Limited and Zayo Cable Private Limited from 19% to 50% in each company.

items.statement: Zayo Energy and Zayo Cable combined capex ~Rs. 180-200 crores; Fujiyama equity share ~Rs. 50 crores (50% stake, debt/equity mix)
items.quote: Just to give an approximate idea at this stage, I believe overall capex that will be needed for these plants will be close to Rs. 180 crores to Rs. 200 crores. That's an idea right now.

items.statement: Rooftop solar potential 630+ GW (Council of Energy); government target 90-100 GW rooftop by 2030 (of 300 GW total solar); ~30 GW installed so far
items.quote: overall potential level, sir, there was one report from Council of Energy where they gave a around more than 630 gigawatt of rooftop solar potential is there. That is the one number. And the another number that we are seeing is that overall target of solar set by the government is to have 300 gigawatt of solar capacity by F'30 and out of that 300, we believe that 90 to 100 gigawatt will come from

items.statement: PM Surya Ghar 2.0 under discussion, may include battery storage support, generation-linked incentives, community solar models
items.quote: While the framework is still under discussion and has not been formally notified, the proposed reports include support for the battery storage, incentives linked to actual power generation and wider access through community solar and other models.

items.statement: Bawal facility fire: Rs. 1,436 million exceptional loss recognized; assets fully insured, claim survey completed, expect settlement by end of FY27
items.quote: The incident resulted in damage to building structures, plant and machinery, inventories, and other assets with a net carrying value of Rs. 1,436 million. Accordingly, the company has recognized a provisional exception loss of Rs. 1,436 million during the quarter.

items.statement: BIS non-compliance on 15 SKUs (~Rs. 2 crores stock, <1% of inventory); certifications obtained post inspection
items.quote: We have almost 500 SKUs out of which, let's assume for a rough understanding, 250 fall in the BIS category and 50% do not. So when the team came to us, they identified 15 SKUS out of 500, 15 which according to them fell in the BIS category and according to us they did not as per their definition.

items.statement: 90% revenue from B2C channel; focus on residential rooftop (on-grid growing faster, off-grid sustained in rural)
items.quote: Yes, the primary focus s on that side as you can se that our 90% of our revenue is from B2C channel network only, so the primary target is on that side only.

items.statement: On-grid growth driven by DCR cell availability; off-grid still growing but slower; hybrid also expanding
items.quote: So definitely growth is more in on-grid now. In off-grid too it's definitely more because there we are, I mean, number one somewhere. So there is growth there too.

items.statement: Zayo Energy and Zayo Cable to supply as OEM to Fujiyama and other solar panel companies; production start next FY, target Rs. 400-500 crores top-line
items.quote: Production will start next year, sir. They have just acquired the land and building construction will start in the next 2-3 months; meanwhile, they will order machines, so they have st a target for themselves to start production within one year. In the next financial year, I think we can't expect too much, but we can expect a top-line of Rs. 400 crores, Rs. 500 crores.

items.statement: Tubular battery fire impact on gross margin <0.5% (tubular battery ~10% of revenue); renting operational plant for interim supply
items.quote: See, sir, tubular battery s generally 10% of our revenue, and we believe that at company level the impact at the gross margin level will be below 0.5%.

items.statement: Estimated ~10% market share in on-grid rooftop solar inverter segment
items.quote: Officially it's very difficult to confirm on the market share side, but we believe that in terms of inverters that we are contributing in the roofiop solar market, and now we are also supply DCR panel. So, we believe that as you rightly mention, we are we are having around 10% of on-grid market share.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance and PAT margin of 5-6% reaffirmed
items.quote: We remain aligned with the FY27 revenue guidance and PAT margin in the range of 5% to 6%.

items.statement: Executable order pipeline of INR845.84 crore targeted for execution by Dec 31, 2026
items.quote: Together, these orders represent an executable order pipeline of INR845.84 crore targeted for the execution by the December 31st, 2026.

items.statement: Total order book visibility stands at approximately INR3,400 crore across confirmed POs, signed MSAs, and advanced discussions
items.quote: On order book visibility, currently stands at approximately INR3,400 crore.

items.statement: Cell line capex revised to INR1,050 crore (INR700 crore debt, INR350 crore equity) for 2.2 GW first phase
items.quote: You can consider INR1,050 crore for the 2.2 gigawatt of cell line, that is the immediate expansion plan.

items.statement: 4 GW module capacity operating as planned; FY27 average utilization assumption of 55%
items.quote: For FY27, we are working with an average utilization assumption of around 55% across the year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 12.7% vs 16.4% YoY; PAT margin 3.1% due to softer volumes and full quarter depreciation/interest on expanded capacity
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR33.8 crore as against the INR42.7 crore in Q1 FY26, translating into an EBITDA margin of 12.7% for the quarter as compared to 16.4% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Indian TOPCon cell cost higher than imported Chinese cells; domestic cell prices will be same for all module manufacturers
items.quote: The Indian cell cost will be higher compared to the imported right now.

items.statement: ALMM-2 timeline clarified on May 25 with no extension; caused project delays and wait-and-watch mode; government later granted extension till December for commissioning
items.quote: On 25th May, it was clarified that there would be no extension. In the weeks that followed, a number of upcoming projects were placed on hold and the market as a whole moved into a wait-and-watch mode.

items.statement: Focus on G12R TOPCon modules; first Indian manufacturer to launch G12R TOPCon; facility fully automated with MES-driven traceability
items.quote: We were the first Indian manufacturer to launch G12R TOPCon module. Our facility is fully automated and MES-driven with complete unit-level traceability.

items.statement: Customer profile includes several largest IPPs; single largest order INR600+ crore; repeat business from quality-conscious buyers with pre-dispatch inspection
items.quote: Our customer profile, which includes several of the largest IPPs in the country, is a source of strength and not a concentration risk.

items.statement: Export focus on Middle East, Africa, Europe, and US; export revenue projection for FY27 very low; building European sales team
items.quote: Our focus is majorly as far as overseas market is concerned, it's a Middle East, Africa, Europe, and we are trying to establish on US market as well.

items.statement: Cell line debt component of ~INR700 crore at advanced discussion stage with lenders; working capital met more through fund-based limits increasing finance cost
items.quote: The debt component of approximately INR700 crore is at an advanced stage of discussion with our lender.

items.statement: Equity component of INR350 crore structured as NCDs and CCDs progressing through due diligence; shifted from QIP/pref to structured debt due to market conditions
items.quote: The equity component of INR350 crore structured as a combination of NCDs and CCDs is progressing through the due diligence stage.

items.statement: Onboarding experienced TOPCon cell manufacturer on KPI-linked basis for line design, commissioning, and operations to de-risk ramp-up
items.quote: We are also onboarding an experienced TOPCon cell manufacturer on a KPI-linked basis for line design, commissioning, operations, which significantly de-risks the ramp-up phase.

items.statement: 2.2 GW N-type TOPCon+ cell line (first phase of 5 GW) on track for commissioning by end of calendar year 2027
items.quote: The 2.2 GW N-type TOPCon+ cell line, which is the first phase of our planned 5 GW cell capacity, is on track for commissioning by end of calendar year 2027.

items.statement: Inventory buildup seasonal; finished goods pile-up due to H1 softness and monsoon; no obsolescence risk as manufacturing latest G12R technology
items.quote: is a seasonal impact and all the inventory, so last year also if you see, the same pattern was continued and similarly in the current quarter, the current half year, the same thing is going on

items.statement: Grid stability and connectivity challenges in Gujarat due to concentrated solar generation; expected to resolve with National Green Grid and BESS
items.quote: In Gujarat, yes, there is a situation majorly because the lot of generation which is happening in Gujarat and it is to be consumed in Gujarat. That's the reason there is some load curtailment issue is going on.

items.statement: Business inherently H2 weighted; Q1 softer due to ALMM uncertainty, monsoon, and seasonal patterns; H2 execution expected to cover shortfall
items.quote: Our business is closely linked to utility-scale solar project execution in India, and it is inherently H2 weighted. The first half of the fiscal year is seasonally softer, and the second half is when the bulk of module dispatches, EPC completion, and the revenue conversion happens.

items.statement: Chinese manufacturers aggressive on pricing overseas; Solex targets markets with preference for Indian modules; Indian modules at par or better on quality
items.quote: Chinese have their own business strategy and they are very aggressive in the overseas market. Solex is finding place where there is some preference for the Indian module manufacturer.

items.statement: No orders at risk from ALMM; timing shifts not cancellations; prepared for both ALMM compliant and non-compliant scenarios with domestic and imported cell supply
items.quote: These are the timing shifts and not cancellations. We do not currently see any orders at risk and whether ALMM is extended at any stage or not, there is no impact on our order book because we are prepared for both scenarios.

items.statement: BSE listing completed (existing shares, no fresh capital); now listed on both NSE and BSE with 11,000+ shareholders
items.quote: First, we have completed our listing on BSE Limited. Solex Energy is now listed on both the NSE and the BSE. Kindly note, this was a listing of existing shares on the BSE main board. No fresh capital was raised.

items.statement: Targeting VAS proportion of 50-60% over next 2-3 years
items.quote: Encouraged by the recent performance and positive outcomes of our strategic focus, we are targeting proportion of VAS products at about 50% to 60% over the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Expecting revenue of INR2,000-2,200 crores in next 2-3 years
items.quote: Yes. I think we are steadily marching towards that, and we should definitely be hitting there in next 2 years to 3 years.

items.statement: Specialty Polymers targeting 20% CAGR over next 3-5 years
items.quote: We are targeting growth at a CAGR of 20% over the next 3 to 5 years in the Specialty Polymer segment.

items.statement: ELITe facility targeted to become operational in CY 2028
items.quote: The facility is targeted to become operational in CY 2028 and will use Loop's proprietary depolymerization technology to convert 100% textile waste streams into virgin-quality monomers.

items.statement: Debt repayment target of INR100 crores for FY27
items.quote: So, this year, the debt repayment target is around INR100 crores.

items.statement: No major capex planned for FY27 beyond sustenance and maintenance
items.quote: No. So, apart from our sustenance and maintenance capex, we are not planning any major capex.

items.statement: Strong structural tailwinds from circular economy and plastic waste management rules
items.quote: We continue to see strong structural tailwinds emerging from the circular economy. The implementation of plastic waste management rules and the increasing requirement for the PET and BOPET films, which stipulate post-consumer recycled content, are creating additional demand opportunities for rPET and recycled content BOPET films.

items.statement: Regained lost US market share in Q1 FY27 after Supreme Court rejection of tariffs
items.quote: India now enjoys a favourable import tariff scenario for imports into U.S. This has resulted in regaining of lost market share in U.S. between Q2 and Q4 of FY26 in this quarter.

items.statement: Expecting sustainable good earnings for next 6-8 quarters due to favorable supply-demand balance
items.quote: So, all this give us confidence that we should have sustainable good earnings going forward, not only for the next 3 quarters, but I would go on to say, for next 6 to 8 quarters.

items.statement: Film segment EBIT margin improved to ~10% in Q1 FY27 from 2.4% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Consequently, EBIT margin improved to 9.8% from 2.4%.

items.statement: Specialty Polymers EBIT margin improved to 45.3% in Q1 FY27 from 31.7% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: segment EBIT stood at INR14.8 crores with EBIT margin improving significantly to 45.3% from 31.7%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded to 13.3% in Q1 FY27 from 8.3% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA increased 103.4% to INR58.9 crores with the EBITDA margin expanding to 13.3% from 8.3% in the corresponding quarter.

items.statement: Commodity BOPET spreads holding at INR28-30 per kg for 12-micron film
items.quote: So, spreads last quarter were in the range of INR28 to INR30. When I say spread, I mean VA, value-add over raw material for 12-micron film.

items.statement: Value-added products command premium of INR25 to much higher levels
items.value: INR25 to much, much higher levels
items.quote: Yes. So, value-added products range from, you know, INR25 to much, much higher levels because it's a mix. So, the more specialized the product, the more value add we are able to get out of it.

items.statement: ELITe secured LOI from leading global sports brand for up to 15,000 tons/year offtake
items.value: up to 15,000 metric tons per year
items.quote: our JV partner, Loop Industries has now secured a letter of intent from a leading global sports and athletic brand for the potential offtake of up to 15,000 metric tons per year of Loop PET fibre-grade resin annually under a multiyear commercial framework.

items.statement: Nike committed as anchor customer for ELITe project
items.quote: Following Nike's earlier commitment as an anchor customer, our JV partner, Loop Industries has now secured a letter of intent from a leading global sports and athletic brand for the potential offtake of up to 15,000 metric tons per year of Loop PET fibre-grade resin annually under a multiyear commercial framework.

items.statement: Consolidated film capacity utilization improved to 84% in Q1 FY27 from 82% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Consolidated capacity utilization also improved to 84% compared with 82% in Q1 FY 26, supported by the better market scenario.

items.statement: Ester Filmtech capacity utilization reached ~83%, highest level so far
items.quote: Capacity utilization reached approximately 83%, the highest level achieved so far, while sales volume increased 22.7% year-on-year to 9,807 metric tons.

items.statement: Expecting 2-3 new BOPET lines in industry over next 1.5-2 years but demand growth outpacing supply
items.quote: We are expecting another 2 to 3 lines coming up in the next 1.5 to 2 years. But again, if you look net-net, the supply-demand balance is going to only tighten because there is a very strong BOPET demand growth happening in India.

items.statement: VAS volume grew 23% YoY to 6,368 tons; contribution increased to ~29% from 24%
items.quote: VAS volume increased 23% year-on-year to 6,368 metric tons in this quarter, and their contribution to total film volumes increased to approximately 29% from 24% a year ago.

items.statement: Targeting up to 35% VAS contribution by exit quarter FY27
items.quote: See, we are seeing up to 35% contribution of VAS product out of our own -- up to the overall portfolio by the quarter end, I mean, in the exit quarter.

items.statement: Specialty Polymers focusing on mix of high-margin specialties and mid-margin VAP for growth
items.quote: The growth in Specialty Polymers will be driven by increase in volumes with a mix of high-margin specialties as well as mid-margin value-added products or VAP.

items.statement: Long-term contracts for PTA and MEG sourcing locally; no production loss due to raw material availability
items.quote: So we have long-term contracts, and we are sourcing all our requirement of PTA and MEG locally. So, we have long-term contract with the suppliers of PTA and MEG, which ensures that we generally don't run short of the requirement that we have.

items.statement: In discussions with GAIL for PTA supply starting end of calendar year; Indian Oil and Reliance capacities delayed
items.quote: we are already in discussion with GAIL, which is likely to start by end of this calendar. And the Indian O il will take some more time to start. Re liance is still some time away

items.statement: Plastic waste management rules driving brands to switch to BOPET and rPET content films
items.quote: Also, all brands, big and small, are gradually switching, not gradually, but rather rapidly switching from other substrate to polyester film substrate, so that they can keep the laminates ready. And in case there is a tighter scrutiny from the government and the compliance is enforced even more strictly, they can rapidly switch to rPET content-based films.

items.statement: Gross debt INR722 crores as of June 30, 2026; targeting reduction to INR620 crores by year-end
items.quote: As on 30th June 2026, the gross total debt of the company was INR722 crores and liquidity of INR236 crores. The company aims to gradually deleverage in the coming years by paring its debt on an overall basis.

items.statement: ELITe JV debt to be raised at JV level, not on Ester balance sheet
items.quote: as far as ELITe is concerned, as you are aware that it's a separate project other than Ester. It's a joint venture between Loop Industries Canada and Ester. So, there is going to be additional debt, which will be raised in the JV company, not in Ester balance sheet.

items.statement: Film volumes up 2.7% YoY to 22,120 tons; revenue up ~38% to INR399.5 crores
items.quote: Consolidated film volumes increased 2.7% year -on-year to 22,120 metric tons, whi le film segment revenue grew by approximately 38% to INR399.5

items.statement: Specialty Polymers volumes 725 tons vs 954 tons YoY; revenue INR32.7 crores vs INR48.1 crores
items.quote: The segment reported consolidated sales volume of 725 metric tons during the quarter compared with 954 metric tons in Q1 FY26. Consolidated revenue stood at INR32.7 crores compared with INR48.1 crores in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: rPET volumes up 19% YoY to 1,394 tons; revenue up 24% to INR17.5 crores
items.quote: Coming to the rPET business, consolidated volumes increased 19% year -on-year to 1,394 metric tons, while revenue grew 24% to INR17.5 crores during the

items.statement: Full-year guidance: edible oil margin construct 3-5%, volume growth 2-4%; food & FMCG 8-10% growth with beauty & personal care ~15%; FMCG vertical EBITDA growth 12-15%
items.quote: I want to reaffirm our full -year guidance range we h ave laid out for the business, edible oil margin construct between 3% to 5% volume growth for the year , food and FMCG 8% to 10% growth with beauty and personal care growing at around 15%, FMCG vertical EBITDA growth at 12% to 15% for the year.

items.statement: Expect FMCG revenue to cross INR12,500 crores in FY27, up from INR11,000+ crores last year, implying 10%+ growth
items.quote: last year our total sales from overall FMCG including the HPC was INR11,000 crores plus, and this year my estimation is that we should certainly cross increase it by 10% plus and we should be somewhere closer to INR12,500 crores in our revenues.

items.statement: Target to increase modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce revenue share from 15% to 20% over next 18 months
items.quote: We want to take that number up to 20%, and I'm confident that over next 18 months we will see our numbers reaching 20% of the overall revenue through these channels.

items.statement: Aim to reach INR2,500 crores annualized EBITDA over next 18 months
items.quote: in terms of the next trajectory level of moving closer to INR2,500 crores of EBITDA hopefully, I think over next 18 months on an annualized basis, I'm reasonably confident that we should be able to head in that direction.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin 4.80% (INR543 crores on INR11,337 crores revenue)
items.quote: Operating EBITDA for the period was INR543 crores with a margin at 4.80%.

items.statement: Edible oil segment EBITDA margin 5.22% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Quarterly EBITDA margin came in at 5.22%.

items.statement: FMCG segment EBITDA margin 6.45% in Q1 FY27 (INR190 crores on INR2,938 crores)
items.quote: the quarterly revenue stood at INR2,9 38 crores with EBITDA of INR190 crores and EBITDA margin of 6.45% in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Biscuits EBITDA margin 15.35% in Q1 FY27 vs 9.35% YoY
items.quote: with EBITDA margin of 15.35% versus 9.35% in the same period last year.

items.statement: Textured soya product EBITDA margin over 18% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: with EBITDA margin of over 18%.

items.statement: Home & Personal Care EBITDA INR122 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: for the HPCour overall HPC EBITDA was INR122 crores.

items.statement: Staples EBITDA negative INR59 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: For staples as a category we had negative INR59 crores.

items.statement: Ethnic foods EBITDA INR9 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: for ethnic foods our EBITDA was INR9 crores.

items.statement: TSP margin guidance 16-18% for the year, currently doing slightly better than 18%
items.quote: we will continue the guidance that we have always given that our margins will be 16% to 18% on the TSP. I think we will be able to maintain that. We are doing a little bit better than 18%.

items.statement: Staples volume growth ~5%, pricing inflation ~12% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The volumes have grown by 5% and the pricing inflation that came in was almost about 12%.

items.statement: Rural demand stress expected in staples this quarter; HPC expected to continue growing well
items.quote: The staples category is expected to see the most rural stress-related pressure this quarter, while Home and Personal Care overall should continue to grow well.

items.statement: Biscuits annual revenue ~INR1,300 crores (Doodh Biscuit INR5/10 packs)
items.quote: the brand of Doodh Biscuit that we have in the category of INR5 and INR10, we do almost INR1,300 crores of business annually.

items.statement: Nutraceuticals turned positive from marginal negatives, revenue INR18 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Revenue from nutraceuticals stood at INR18 crores with sports nutrition gaining significant momentum.

items.statement: Nutrela TSP market share ~40%, Q1 FY27 revenue INR160 crores (14% YoY, 50% QoQ)
items.quote: Nutrela is a strong brand, we nearly have 40% market share . And so this quarter, for example, we did INR160 crores of business.

items.statement: Calibrated price increases in edible oils; targeted discounts in FMCG; introduced smaller pack sizes
items.quote: We took calibrated price increases in the edible oil segment while using targeted discounts in our FMCG portfolio to remain competitive. We also introduced smaller pack sizes to address changing consumer needs and market requirements.

items.statement: Commodity inflation net positive for edible oils (long positions) but raises FMCG input costs; net impact smaller than pure-play FMCG
items.quote: On one hand, we carry long positions in edible oils, so the resulting commodity price inflation has actually been a net positive for the business. On the other, the same inflation raises input costs for several of our FMCG businesses, weighing on their profitability. Net-net, the impact on Patanjali as a whole is smaller than it would be for a pure-play FMCG company.

items.statement: Palm oil prices firmed from March 2026, dipped after de-escalation, then rose to 2-week high in mid-August; rupee depreciation 2.5% supported domestic prices
items.quote: On the input front, the palm oil prices ha s begun firming in March 2026, remained positive following the onset of the war, but turned marginally lower after de -escalation in the latter part of the quarter. Futures factored in the same and prices turned lower. Still, domestic prices were supported by rupee depreciation of 2.5% and again by festival period palm oil prices reached 2-week high in mi

items.statement: Soya oil futures up 40% by end-March, stabilized by end-June; FOB prices corrected 6% amid lower demand
items.quote: The soya oil price futures increased by 40% towards the end of March and then stabilized towards the end of June, the FOB prices corrected by 6% amidst lower demand, leading to a sharper decline in physical prices with further firming similar to palm oil price trend.

items.statement: Wheat prices stable; milk prices trending up on higher procurement costs; sugar firm on lower domestic production and tighter inventory
items.quote: Wheat prices have remained largely stable during the quarter, while milk prices trended upwards on the back of higher procurement costs. Sugar prices, too, stayed firm amidst lower domestic production and tighter inventory levels.

items.statement: Packaging, freight and logistics costs increased during the quarter
items.quote: In addition to all this, we saw an increase in packaging, freight, and logistics costs during the quarter.

items.statement: Oil palm cultivated area 1,15,861 hectares as of 30 June 2026 (37% in prime yielding phase 7-25 years) vs allocated 6.63 lakh hectares
items.quote: As of 30th June '26, the cultivated area stood at 1,15,861 hectares with nearly 37% of the area in the prime yielding phase of 7 to 25 years, against total allocated area of 6.63 lakh hectares.

items.statement: Launched Rose Kanti soap, Dant Kanti Sensitive toothpaste, Super Dishwash liquid, Sweet Lime pickle, Almond & Chyawanprash cookies, mango chutney, mango panna juice, orange juice in Q1 FY27
items.quote: During the quarter, we launched several new products including Rose Kanti soap, Dant Kanti Sensitive toothpaste, Super Dishwash liquid, Sweet Lime pickle, Almond and Chyawanprash cookies, in addition to our summer-focused launches.

items.statement: Micro-segmenting Dant Kanti portfolio by population, choice architecture, Gen Z requirements
items.quote: We are increasingly micro-segmenting this portfolio by population, by choice architecture, and specifically to address the Gen Z requirements for the toothpaste.

items.statement: E-commerce & quick commerce growing 25% YoY; currently 15% of revenue (modern trade + e-com + quick com); target 20% in 18 months
items.quote: we're g rowing at 25% year-on-year on the both quick commerce and e-commerce. Currently, if I were to put those numbers together, we right now do close to about 15% between modern trade and e -commerce, quick commerce.

items.statement: Dishwash category expanding; no intention to exit or slow down despite MNC exits; market share not disclosed
items.quote: the dishwash is actually a fairly strong both as a category and as a line that we have, and it has done exceedingly well. Yes, so we have no intention of either exiting or slowing down on that.

items.statement: Biscuits: unique positioning as only atta biscuit player; competitors at odd price points (INR4.5, INR9) mostly exited
items.quote: one of the good success stories of our brand has been that how we have kept the quality part exceedingly in control, kept the unique positioning being the only atta biscuit player in the marketplace and have grown that consistently.

items.statement: Acquired Patanjali Ayurved HPC business via slump sale in Nov 2024 for INR1,100 crores; business generated ~INR600 crores EBITDA last year on INR2,900 crores revenue
items.quote: on a slump sale basis in November '24 on the business which has generated almost INR600 crores of EBITDA margin last year. So, we if my numbers are right, Rajesh ji, what we paid INR1,100 crores or INR950 crores? Kumar Rajesh: INR1,100 crores… Sanjeev Asthana: So, it is a business of, you know, it was INR2,900 crores. It was generating a margin of INR600 crores, and we have paid INR1,100 crores wh

items.statement: All three acquisitions (biscuits, foods, HPC) done on slump sale basis at asset/inventory value; no valuation multiple; approved by shareholders
items.quote: All the three businesses we acquired on a slump sale basis, which is basically just the assets that we paid for and the inventory that they carried at that point of time. There was no valuation methodology, there was nothing.

items.statement: CFO Kumar Rajesh awarded Best CFO of the Year at Asia Business Leader of the Year Awards
items.quote: Our CFO, Kumar Rajesh, was honored with the Best CFO of the Year award at the Asia Business Leader of the Year Awards.

items.statement: Cautious on staples due to El Nino uncertainty, rural income stress, potential policy interventions (commodity control orders, essential commodities)
items.quote: One is that this El Nino impact is still very unclear in the way how markets are going to react both on the production side and the availability side, and very direct impact of that could be on the food inflation, which is there number one. Number two is the rural incomes and the rural market demand side, we'll have to watch with great deal of care as to how they play out if at all we see some str

items.statement: Inventory markdown on pulses due to quality issues; higher input inflation (packaging, commodity) impacting food business margins
items.quote: other than one or two blips that we have on the food side, which is also by way of abundant caution in terms of some inventory markdown in case of certain quality issues that we saw in pulses in the stocks that we had, and the higher the input inflation in terms of packaging, in terms of commodity and otherwise, which has had some impact on our overall food business.

items.statement: Oil palm plantation revenue INR740 crores in Q1 FY27 (25% YoY); highest-ever quarterly revenue
items.quote: On the oil p alm plantation front, the company generated highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR740 crores in Q1 FY27. Revenues grew by 25% year-on-year.

items.statement: Edible oil segment revenue INR8,505 crores in Q1 FY27 (highest-ever quarterly revenue); mustard oil led growth
items.quote: our edible oil segment delivered quarterly revenue of INR8,505 crores, marking the highest -ever quarterly revenue with growth led primarily by the mustard oil.

items.statement: FMCG segment revenue INR2,938 crores in Q1 FY27 (26% of revenue, 30% of EBITDA excl. unallocable)
items.quote: the quarterly revenue stood at INR2,9 38 crores with EBITDA of INR190 crores and EBITDA margin of 6.45% in Q1 FY27. The segment contributed nearly 26% of revenues and nearly 30% of EBITDA, excluding unallocable income during the quarter.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of around 300 crores for FY27 reaffirmed
items.quote: Sir we have done already 60 in Q1. And the balance about 150 crores, the order book that also needs to be finished in this financial year. And definitely there are some orders in pipeline which also we would need to do it by March. So 300 we are in line Sir.

items.statement: Targeting operating cycle of 60 to 70 days by FY28
items.quote: By FY28, we expect an operating cycle with the much more controlled and disciplined working capital structure, with a targeting days of 60 to 70 days.

items.statement: Targeting at least 80% capacity utilization by end of next financial year
items.quote: It will start gradually increasing from this year, Sir. We are targeting to reach at least 80% by the end of the next financial year.

items.statement: Strong demand across thermal, power, railways, defence, oil and gas, shipbuilding
items.quote: Across thermal and power, railways, defence, oil and gas, shipbuilding, multiple opportunities have opened for the company at the same time. These opportunities are clearly visible to us.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 18.89%, PAT margin 11.25%
items.quote: EBITDA increased above approx. 25% year on year to 11.52 crores compared with 9.15 crores in Q1 FY26 with an EBITDA margin of 18.89%. PAT stood at 6.86 crores up to approximately 45% year on year from 4.74 crores, while PAT margins improved to 11.25% from 10.48%.

items.statement: New railway and power fabrication orders at similar margins; niche complex products to improve PAT margin
items.quote: You're right that way that in the fabrication side and in the railway side, PAT will not be higher. Definitely they'll not be higher. They are all tender business. It will be similar to what we have been able to do.

items.statement: Near-term order book expanded to roughly 150 crores plus vs historical 80-100 crores
items.quote: our business pipeline. Our n ear term order book has expanded to roughly 150 crores plus as compared to the historical range of 80 to 100 crores. Providing a strong revenue visibility going forward

items.statement: Mazgaon Dock order for 5 sets worth ~4.5 crores; another ~8 crores in pipeline
items.quote: On an average, the first order for 5 sets is about 4 and a half crore rupees. The one pipeline is about 8 odd crores.

items.statement: Targeting >100 crores from railway bogies and >100 crores from power sector fabrication in FY28
items.quote: Yes, next year we are targeting more than 100 crores from this business only. And in last year also we did not do any power sector, any BHL orders which we have already got through RXIL. So another 100 crores from power sector will get added.

items.statement: Fabrication capacity expansion to 1,500 tons/month (~18,000 tons/year) from current ~6,000 tons/month
items.quote: Sir, we would be in a position to do about 1500 tons a month about what the plan is that capacity is 1500 tons a month that is about 18,000 tons. So that is but at the moment what we are doing is about without this capacity expansion we are doing about 6000.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization 50-60%
items.quote: We are roughly learning on 50 to 60% capacity utilization right now, Sir.

items.statement: Foundry debottlenecking planned (~₹4-5 crore for CNC machine, conveyors, cranes); machine molding plant on drawing board
items.quote: We would be doing some debottlenecking, adding ₹4 -5 crore for one machine, again a CNC machine and debottlenecking by conveyors and cranes and those kind of stuff. But not at the moment. We want to earn some money, be stable.

items.statement: Strategic shift at Unit 1 to faster-moving products with shorter execution/realization cycle; similar shift planned for Unit 3
items.quote: We have already initiated a strategic shift in the product mix at Unit one with a great focus on faster moving products and having a shorter execution and realization cycle. Therefore place significantly lower pressure on working capital.

items.statement: Bill discounting on RXIL/Invoice Mart at 5-5.5% interest rate
items.quote: No, they give us in interest rate of 5%. They discount the bills at somewhere around 5 to 5.5% rate of interest. We get an early payments on that.

items.statement: Targeting 60-70 day operating cycle by FY28 vs current ~100-120 days
items.quote: By increasing this structure now overall 100 or 120 days will come down to roughly figure of 60 to 70 days by next year end we are envisaging that.

items.statement: Recent fundraise sufficient for 500 crore revenue target; no further fundraise needed
items.quote: It will be sufficient this fundraise which we are going ahead, this will sufficiently be used. No more fundraiser required for that is what we believe.

items.statement: Future investments limited to internal accruals; no additional borrowing planned
items.quote: Those will, I mean, what we have thought and what we are looking at is something that can be financed through our own accruals. We are not looking in at any capex, further capex.

items.statement: Railway bogies: 20% direct from Indian Railways, 80% from wagon builders
items.quote: Till 2019 we were doing this bogies in simplest casting only. About 20% comes from railways directly and balance 80% is always was always also previously from wagon builders.

items.statement: Defence: collaborating with ordnance factories (e.g., Gadkari, Khamaria, Jabalpur) for hardware/components
items.quote: We are closely working with Gadkari factory, Khamaria, Jabalpur. Correct. So now they were making if they were making X. The total demand now is for 1.5 or 2X of the same.

items.statement: Shipbuilding: certified by American Bureau of Shipping and Indian Bureau of Shipping; supplying Mazgaon Dock, Goa Shipyard, Hindustan Shipyard, Cochin Shipyard
items.quote: We are one of the few players which are which are visited in American Bureau of Shipping and Indian Bureau of Shipping both. So we have the certifications. So we are expecting these orders because it involves some intricate machining.

items.statement: Targeting 200 bogies/month capacity (conservative; capability slightly higher)
items.quote: That's right, Sir, but we are understating it conservative, that is what we like. it. Capability is slightly more, but we are aiming at 200 numbers.

items.statement: Defence + shipbuilding to contribute 10-15% of revenue in FY27 and FY28
items.quote: It will be 5 to 10% because I would add the shipbuilding to the same. So it will be 10 to 15% and it will continue to be 10 to 15% in the next financial year also.

items.statement: Open to technology JVs/acquisitions to launch own products; leveraging 30 acres, 1,200 workers, 100+ machine tools
items.quote: we buy the technology company or we have a joint venture with the technology company. Today, Simplex can produce. I mean, we have already done in the past complete steel plants

items.statement: Green hydrogen DRI pilot project (₹300 crore, ₹160 crore grant) exited due to GST implications on grant/IP terms
items.quote: The total projects was about 300 crores, about 160 crores was grant from the government. Srikanth Reddy: OK. Ketan Shah: Unfortunately, in the tender, the one of the condition was in lieu of the grant, they need the IP in the same percentage and the asset also in the same

items.statement: Order book deliberately maintained at ₹100-150 crore to manage liquidated damages risk (5-10%)
items.quote: We are trying to keep the order book to same level, about 100-150, where we have sufficient time and we are able to execute it. So we are very confident that at this order book 100-150, we will be able to maintain.

items.statement: No royalty payments on past technical collaborations (technical transfers completed)
items.quote: Fortunately, nothing is on royalty basis. It was on technical transfer. The technical collaborations were technical transfers and they have been completed and it is over. So for the last so many years, we are not required to pay any royalty.

items.statement: Management declined to provide FY27 revenue growth guidance
items.quote: I don't think it will be prudent to give you any number at this time.

items.statement: Regulated market demand expected to improve in next 2-3 quarters; H2 typically stronger due to winter season
items.quote: We hope in the next two, three quarters our demand for the regulated products will improve, and we can do better performance.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin improved ~3pp to 33% vs Q1 FY26; EBITDA rose to INR25 cr from INR10 cr
items.quote: Combined gross margin improved by approximately 3% points to 33% in Q1 '27 compared with approxima tely 30% in Q1 of '26. EBITDA improved to INR25 crores in Q1 of '27 compared with EBITDA of INR10 crores in Q1 of '26

items.statement: Cefixime under maximum margin pressure in rest-of-world markets; other 7-ACA-based APIs more stable
items.quote: Cefixime is the one having maximum pressure. Cefuroxime and other 7-ACA-based, fortunately, seem to be more stable compared to Cefixime.

items.statement: Exblifep Europe volumes grew 300% QoQ in Q3 FY26, 170% in Q4 FY26, 50% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: In Europe, the business is growing at a steady manner whilst volumes grew by approximately 300% in Q3 of '26, 170% in Q4 of '26, and about 50% in Q1 of '27.

items.statement: Russia Exblifep licensing estimated 10-year value ~USD178 million; registration and launch in 1.5-2 years
items.quote: In Russia, the estimated 10 -year value of our licensing arrangement is approximately USD178 million. This is an estimated long -term value and not current p eriod revenue

items.statement: FY27 capex focused on completing 7-ACA (INR750 cr) and cefiderocol (USD20-25 mn) projects; no significant new capex
items.quote: INR750 crore s is for the 7 -ACA project and USD20 million to USD25 million, I don't remember the crore s amount we have disclosed, for the cefiderocol project

items.statement: 7-ACA Jammu plant targets commissioning and first commercial batch by March 2027; ramp-up to 80-100% utilization in first year
items.quote: Our ramp-up plan is to go to about 80% to 100% by the end of the first year. Initially, it would be slow and then increasing progressively.

items.statement: Cefiderocol facility commissioning by Dec 2026, validation and initial batches Jan-Mar 2027; commercial launch subject to DCGI approval
items.quote: We target commissioning by December of '26, followed by validation and initial batches during January to March '27 period. Commercial launch will be subject to the approval process from DCGI.

items.statement: Strategy shifting from volume-driven generic API to value-based diversified portfolio; only Indian player with 20-25 cephalosporin products
items.quote: we are the only company which can make about 20 to 25 products, whereas the others, they make three or four produ cts and focus on the volume. So, our strategy per se as a cephalosporin player is completely different from our competitors in India

items.statement: Plan to supply non-sterile Ceftriaxone to other Indian sterile manufacturers (Aurobindo etc.) using 7-ACA backward integration
items.quote: For Ceftriaxone, not just sterile, we would be supplying to all other players like Aurobindo and other sterile players in India the non-sterile part, which they are currently importing from China.

items.statement: 7-ACA pricing stable ~USD60/kg for 10-12 years; concentrated among 3-4 Chinese makers (Sinopharm Weiqida, Zhuhai United, Yili Pharma, Livzon); limited room for drastic price cuts
items.quote: The pricing in 7-ACA has been stable over the last 10 to 12 years. The weighted average is about USD60. So, we believe that there is not much room to reduce prices drastically.

items.statement: DCGI trial waiver for cefiderocol in India uncertain; precedent exists (Cefepime-Enmetazobactam got waiver); WHO PQ filing targeted, ~2-year timeline
items.quote: Yeah, yeah, our Cefepime-Enmetazobactam itself is a precedent. We got the waiver because the committee thought that the -- because of the antimicrobial resistance, the country needs new antibiotics.

items.statement: PLI benefit eligibility for 2 years based on current timeline; may seek extension after plant starts
items.quote: PLI, we'll probably be entitled for 2 years. Based on the current scenario, we'll be entitled for 2 years.

items.statement: Exblifep partnerships advanced for South America, Mexico, Philippines, Thailand, Morocco, Australia; discussions ongoing for US and China
items.quote: to engage with potential partners in other markets and are at an advanced stage of discussion for South America, Mexico, Philippines, Thailand, Morocco, and Australia. These agreements will lead to large -scale availability of Exblifep across the globe. We are also in discussion with prospective candidates in US and China

items.statement: NP-NC (non-penicillin non-cephalosporin) synthetic business Q1 FY27 sales INR21 cr; incremental product additions planned, not expected to reach 25% of revenue in 3-4 years
items.quote: So, this quarter sales was INR21 crores, and we are working on a couple of molecules. We are also planning to scale up and backward integrate in these molecules also.

items.statement: 7-ACA fermentation scale-up unpredictable; 20x pilot scale-up done, need 800x more to Jammu; technology partner supports strain development and process stabilization
items.quote: We've been successfully been able to commercial -- scale up our existing pilot plant by 20x, and we have to another do about 800x from there to Jammu, but it's a little unpredictable.

items.statement: Chinese VAT refund reductions heard but not confirmed for 7-ACA; management not aware of specific policy changes
items.quote: Honestly, not aware about this. We heard that slowly the VAT refunds are getting reduced, but not aware exactly of this.

items.statement: Merger with Dhanuka Laboratories effective 10 July 2024 (appointed date 1 April 2024); FY25/FY26 results restated on combined basis
items.quote: On 10th of July, the merger with Dhanuka Laboratories became effective with an appointed date of 1st April 2024. Accordingly, the FY25 comparative and FY26 results have been restated to reflect the combined operations of Orchid Pharma and Dhanuka Laboratories.

items.statement: Integration projects started to crystallize merger synergies; initial benefits expected visible next financial year
items.quote: We have also started a number of focused integration projects to crystallize savings from this merger. We expect initial benefits of these initiatives to begin becoming visible in the next financial year.

items.statement: Confident to achieve or cross 15 million tons bauxite volume by FY28
items.quote: We remain confident in our ability to achieve or even cross our guidance of 15 million tons by financial year '28.

items.statement: Expect around USD1 billion sales from bauxite business in FY28 at 15 million tons
items.quote: So even picking that as a baseline kind of number for the next financial year, we can think that around you know, almost about billion dollars of sales we are expecting from bauxite as per the company's plan.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA per ton to remain around USD5.5-6 in near term, targeting USD10 over medium term
items.quote: So around USD6 or USD5.5 to USD6 would be a reasonable, expectation. But again, you know, the situation is very volatile. So, I would take that also with a little bit pinch of salt. But we do expect that the, you know, going forward you know Q3 towards the end and then Q4 maybe I mean we are optimistic, you know earlier we used to operate at around closer to USD10.

items.statement: Planning capex close to INR200 crores across India business verticals
items.quote: As stated previously, we are also planning a capex close to INR200 crores across various projects and business verticals.

items.statement: Bauxite washing plant investment of USD15 million on operate-and-transfer model
items.quote: So washery investment will not be reflecting on our balance sheet as it's on a kind of operate and transfer kind of model. So, but if you were to install this kind of a washery, it would be in the tune of USD15 million.

items.statement: Boffa port capacity enhanced from 5 to 8 million tons per annum, fully operational
items.quote: Our Boffa port is now fully operational with its capacity enhanced from the 5 million tons to 8 million tons per annum.

items.statement: GSM second port new jetty under construction, expected operational by Q4 FY27, increasing capacity from 6 to 10 million tons per annum
items.quote: At GSM, the second port, the new jetty is currently under construction and expected to be operational by Q4 of this financial year, increasing capacity from 6 million tons to 10 million tons per annum.

items.statement: Combined port capacity to reach approximately 23 million tons per annum
items.quote: With these developments, our combined port capacity will reach to approximately 23 million tons, providing us with the infrastructure to support the maximized volume growth and sales over the medium terms.

items.statement: Bauxite washing plant capacity of 20,000 tons per day operational, expandable within one year if viable
items.quote: The bauxite washing plant is already setup, the capacity is about 20,000 tons per day and this washing plant will enhance our resource and will give us more flexibility to increase our volume for the export.

items.statement: Expect market price to gradually improve as China inventory normalizes, new Chinese refineries to add 20-30 million tons bauxite demand
items.quote: Several new refineries are coming on stream, including the four new refineries in China which are expected to create additional bauxite demand of around 20 million tons to 30 million tons over the above current volumes.

items.statement: Guinea government expected to implement bauxite export quota system before end of 2025, seen as positive for prices
items.quote: As discussed in our last earning call, the government of Guinea is expected to implement a quota system for the bauxite export. We believe this could be introduced in the near terms and certainly before end of this year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin 11.7% vs 13.8% YoY due to higher fuel, logistics and input costs
items.quote: EBITDA margin was approximately 11.7% for the quarter, compared to 13.8% in corresponding same quarter of the last year.

items.statement: Guinea bauxite EBITDA per ton improved to USD6.3 from USD5.9 in Q4 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA per ton improved to 6.3 per ton from 5.9 per ton in Q4.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA levels to remain similar until freight situation improves or quota system implemented
items.quote: So we expect that EBITDA will remain in similar levels until the freight situation improves. So in the very short term we would think that EBITDA levels would remain here.

items.statement: Ocean freight rates remain highly volatile and elevated, expected to continue through 2025
items.quote: The freight rates remains highly volatile. Given the current geopolitical environments, we expect this volatility to continue across 2027.

items.statement: Sulphuric acid prices increased five-fold over past year, currently above INR30/kg, impacting bleaching clay business
items.quote: Our bleaching clay business faced significant cost pressures during the quarter with sulphuric acid prices increasing five-fold over the past year and currently standing above INR30 a kg.

items.statement: Advanced ceramic materials business delivered encouraging profitability growth supported by higher premium product mix
items.quote: Our advanced ceramic materials business delivered encouraging growth in profitability supported by change in sales mix with a higher proportion realized from our premium products.

items.statement: Focus on value-added products across bentonite, white performance minerals, targeting >50% EBITDA from value-added in 3 years
items.quote: Over a medium term if we consider three years, we expect that, you know, most or more than half of our current EBITDA or most of our EBITDA would be coming from the value-added products and that's the kind of vision what we have set out.

items.statement: Middle East and Europe customer base impacted by geopolitical and freight environment, shifting focus to India, Asia, Africa
items.quote: Our customer base in Middle East and Europe has been impacted by the current geopolitical and freight environment. We believe freight conditions need to stabilize for demand and volumes in these markets to normalize. In the interim, we are increasing our focus on India, Asia and Africa where the supply chain environment remains relatively manageable.

items.statement: New Guinea bauxite entrants like Nimba (14 million tons target) not expected to significantly disrupt market given 200 million tons total exports
items.quote: So essentially, we believe that it's a new development but it will take some time to materialize and should not have a significant impact on the overall market. I mean Guinea exports close to 200 million ton and they are talking about achieving 14 million tons after some period of time.

items.statement: Guinea quota system implementation expected before end of 2025, seen as positive for global bauxite prices and freight reduction
items.quote: We expect such rationalization of the export volume to be positive for the global bauxite prices and the potentially lead to reduction in the freight cost.

items.statement: China index prices around USD72 CIF, increase from USD61 predominantly due to ocean freight, not FOB price improvement
items.quote: The Chinese index prices are, they are around USD72. But they are kind of a combination of the FOB Guinea price as well as the freight from Guinea to China. So, the increase what we have seen from around USD61 or so to USD72 is predominantly on the back of ocean freight.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR1,616 crores, up 19.2% YoY; EBITDA INR188.9 crores, flat YoY
items.quote: For quarter one, consolidated income from operations stood at INR1,616 crores compared to INR1,356 crores in quarter one of '25-'26, representing a year-on-year growth of approximately 19.2%. Reported EBITDA stood at INR188.9 crores, compared with INR187.7 crores in quarter one of '25-'26.

items.statement: Guinea business contributed INR1,360 crores turnover (84% of consolidated) and INR163 crores EBITDA in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Guinea business reported turnover of approximately INR1,360 crores, which is 84% of the consolidated turnover and EBITDA of INR163 crores during the quarter.

items.statement: Consciously focusing on profitability over volume growth until macro situation improves, operating with focus on profitability in disrupted environment
items.quote: So we are consciously taking a call to focus on profitability while this disrupted situation remains. And we have the all infrastructure and customers and everything in place. Once the things improves, and if they improve then we have the ability to really do well in the quarter three and four.

items.statement: Targets FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin of 15% to 17%
items.quote: We expect about 15% to 17%.

items.statement: Targets rolling stock interior EBITDA margin of 13% to 15%
items.quote: We are targeting an EBITDA margin of 13% to 15% for the rolling stock interior and allied business segment supported by passenger coach modernization, new train additions, and expansion to ORVIN, which is the artificial leather business brand, applications and further backward integrations to improve our profitability.

items.statement: Targets freight wagon EBITDA margin of 15% to 17% over medium term
items.quote: We are targeting an EBITDA margin of 15% to 17% for the freight wagon business over the medium term, with increasing utilization of the existing platform being an important driver towards achieving this objective.

items.statement: Consolidated order book of INR1,692 crores as of August 11, 2026
items.quote: As of August 11, 2026, our consolidated order book stood at approximately INR 1,692 crores, comprising INR1,526 crores of wagon at OFPL and INR 166 crores in the coach interior at Oriental Rail Infrastructure.

items.statement: OFPL order book of INR1,526 crores equals approximately 3,800 wagons
items.quote: The number of wagons is approximately 3800 wagons.

items.statement: Expects order book addition of around INR600 crores in Q1 FY28
items.quote: And we see addition to the order book maybe in the first quarter of financial year '27 * and that would be of anywhere around INR600 crores.

items.statement: OFPL installed capacity 2,400 wagons per annum; Q1 FY27 utilization ~50%
items.quote: Oriental Foundry operates an RDSO -approved manufacturing platform with an inst alled capacity of 2,400 wagons per annum. Its vertical integration across critical wagon components provides greater control over quality, supply, and manufacturing costs. OFPL has delivered more than 4,000 wagons to date. Importantly, capacity utilization was approximately 50% in financial year '26, providing signific

items.statement: Targets 200 wagons per month from Q3 FY27, implying full capacity utilization
items.quote: We project to execute at the rate of 200 wagons per month from quarter three of the present financial year.

items.statement: Plans capacity expansion to 4,800 wagons per annum over 12-18 months starting Q1 FY28
items.quote: In the long run, over a period of say 12 months to 18 months to 4,800 wagons.

items.statement: Capex for expansion from 2,400 to 3,600 wagons estimated at INR60-70 crores
items.quote: The capex requirement for wagon expansion from 2,400 wagons to 3,600 wagons would be roughly about INR60 crores to INR70 crores.

items.statement: Plans dedicated smart wagon component facility in North India by end of FY28
items.quote: We are planning a dedicated smart wagon component facility in North India by the end of financial year ' 28, supporting the commercialization and scale-up of this opportunity, as well as the Make in India initiative to successfully cater to this market requirement.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin 15.2%, up 286 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA increased 43.7% year -to-year to INR20.9 crores, with EBITDA margin improving to 15.2% from 12.4%, an expansion of 286 basis points.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by better product mix, cost absorption, operating leverage
items.quote: The improvement in operating profitability was supported by better product mix, improved cost absorption, and operating leverages.

items.statement: Wagon price escalation clause linked to wholesale price index of steel, labour, commodities
items.quote: See the price escalation clause in the wagons is on account of the wholesale price index of the steel, the labour index, and all major commodities. So that is a very well established and a very well defined price variation clause with the railways which is operationally and practically safeguarding the wagon manufacturer from any abnormal or any increases that may happen.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue mix: wagons 75%, seat and berths 16%, rexine upholstery 5%, others 4%
items.quote: Looking at the consolidated revenue mix, wagons accounted for approximately 75% of revenue, followed by seat and berths at 16%, rexine upholstery at approximately 5% and other products at 4%.

items.statement: Freight wagon demand expected to grow continuously; National Rail Plan targets fleet expansion from 4 lakh to 6 lakh wagons by 2030
items.quote: In freight, the National Rail Plan 2030 targets an expansion of wagon fleet from approximately 4 lakh wagons to 6 lakh wagons, while the freight wagon market is expected to nearly double to approximately INR25,000 crores to INR30,000 crores by 2031.

items.statement: Smart wagon market potential estimated at INR10,000 crores; targets INR750 crores annual revenue at 30,000 units/year
items.quote: Beyond the initial program, the company estimates the smart wagon market potential at approximately INR10,000 crores with estimated annual incremental revenue potential of approximately INR750 crores targeting around 30,000 wagons per year.

items.statement: Smart wagon system realization estimated at INR2.5-3 lakhs per unit
items.quote: See, what happens is that it would be anywhere in the range of about INR2.5 lakhs to INR3 lakhs per unit of wagon. And for the passenger coach, maybe slightly higher. On an average, you can say around INR2.5 lakhs to INR3 lakhs per rolling stock, that is per passenger coach or per wagon.

items.statement: 51:49 JV with HUM Industrial Technology for smart wagon condition monitoring
items.quote: Through our partnership with HUM Industrial Technology, USA, we have entered the Smart Wagon Technology segment through an exclusive joint venture of 51- 49 percentage to integrate HUM's on-board condition monitoring systems into freight wagons and passenger wagons as well.

items.statement: JV with AB Composites for total furnishing of passenger coaches
items.quote: Alongside the above freight initiatives, we have also entered into a strategic tie-up through a joint venture with A B Composites which is focused on offering entire turnkey solutions of total furnishing of passenger coaches, which will be a huge advantage in garnering more market share and also improving our revenues and profit margins.

items.statement: Tie-up with United Wagon Company and VNICT for 25-ton high axle load wagon design
items.quote: The next growth potential that we have is the modern wagon or the next generation wagons for which we have a tie-up with the United Wagon Company and its design arm VNICT for the improved 25-ton high axle load wagon platforms for the Indian markets.

items.statement: Applying for AAR certification to align with global rail quality standards
items.quote: We are also applying for AAR certification which is intent to align our manufacturing capacity with global rail quality standards and support our expansion into international markets, which will be a big revenue booster.

items.statement: In-principle approval received from Railway Board for wagon leasing operations
items.quote: The in- principle approval for a wagon leasing operation has been received from the Railway Board, and we would be participating in active tenders to establish our footprint in the wagon leasing business.

items.statement: Focus on improving working capital efficiency and cash conversion as business scales
items.quote: At the same time, we remain focused on improving working capital efficiency and ensuring that growth translates into stronger operating cash flows.

items.statement: Credit rating CARE BBB Stable / A3; expects debt reduction and positive cash flow with better utilization
items.quote: From a financial discipline perspective, our credit rating continues to be CARE BBB Stable Public A3 and we remain focused on prudent capital allocation and maintaining a strong financial profile as the business scales.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 impacted by US-Iran war and fuel/gas supply crisis in March-April
items.quote: The first quarter of the financial year has been affected by the US -Iran war and, the immediate crisis of the fuel and gas supply which was existing during March and April which is now more or less solved out or under total control.

items.statement: Expects full-year FY27 standalone EBITDA margin of 17%-18% after factoring in price increases
items.quote: So, with the factoring in, price increases coming in, we are expecting the full year to end at 17%-18% EBITDA margin for the standalone business.
